# Choose a Data Streaming Option

Choose an option based on whether you need measurement data at a high rate,
easy parsing, reliable delivery to a PLC, or notifications when device values
change.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Choose a Data Streaming Option:** option, what it is for, advantages, trade-offs, and best fit.</p>

| Option | What it is for | Advantages | Trade-offs | Best fit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Compact Format](./compact-format.md) | SICK binary format for scan, IMU, and encoder data over the transport documented for each device. | Lowest bandwidth; very efficient to parse; each segment can be processed on its own for low latency; Kaitai Struct definitions and a Wireshark dissector are available. | Not self-describing, so the parser must know the layout; UDP packets can be lost or reordered. | High-rate, low-latency integrations in C, C++, or other compiled languages. |
| [MSGPACK Format](./msgpack-format.md) | Self-describing MessagePack encoding of scan data over UDP. | Any standard MessagePack library can parse it; the Python ScanSegmentAPI is a reference implementation. | Uses more bandwidth than Compact; UDP packets can be lost or reordered; documented for multiScan100 and picoScan100. | Scripting and prototyping, especially in Python. |
| [LMDscandata Format](./lmdscandata-format.md) | CoLa scan data telegram; connection and transport depend on the device. | Fits existing CoLa and PLC integrations; telegram content is configurable where supported. | Uses a different angle reference than Compact and MSGPACK; less suited to high data rates. | PLCs and integrations that already use CoLa. |
| [WebSocket Events](./websocket-events.md) | Persistent WebSocket connection that pushes JSON messages when a device value changes. | No polling; low-latency notifications; the payload matches the REST endpoint of the same name. | Carries state and results, not scan data; the client must negotiate `permessage-deflate`. | Monitoring field evaluation results, I/O, temperature alarms, and firmware update progress. |
| [Filter Details](./filter-details.md) | On-sensor filters that change the measurement data before it is sent. | Reduce bandwidth and remove unwanted points such as fog, dust, rain, or snow. | Some filters delay the output or lower the output rate; filtered points may be set to 0 instead of removed. | Tuning the data stream for any of the measurement data formats. |

Compact, MSGPACK, and LMDscandata carry measurement data. WebSocket events
complement measurement data with change notifications. Format availability and
transport vary by product family, variant, and firmware.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Choose a Data Streaming Option:** device family, Compact, MSGPACK, LMDscandata, and WebSocket events.</p>

| Device family | Compact | MSGPACK | LMDscandata | WebSocket events |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LRS4000 | Yes | No | Yes | No |
| multiScan100 | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| multiScan200 | Yes | No | No | No |
| picoScan100 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

The filters apply to the measurement formats supported by the device. Some
filters are variant-specific.

If you are unsure, start with [Compact](./compact-format.md) for a new
integration, [MSGPACK](./msgpack-format.md) for quick Python prototypes on
supported devices, or [LMDscandata](./lmdscandata-format.md) when a PLC or
existing CoLa integration consumes the data.

## Typical Setup

A typical application uses three interfaces side by side where they are
supported: the
[REST API](../configuration/rest-interface.md) to configure the sensor,
[WebSocket events](./websocket-events.md) to get notified when device values
change, and the [Compact format](./compact-format.md) to receive the
measurement data.

<div class="setup-diagram" role="img" aria-label="Customer application on top of three interfaces: REST for configuration, WebSocket for notifications, and Compact for data">
  <div class="setup-diagram__app">Customer Application</div>
  <div class="setup-diagram__box setup-diagram__box--rest">REST</div>
  <div class="setup-diagram__box setup-diagram__box--websocket">WebSocket</div>
  <div class="setup-diagram__box setup-diagram__box--compact">Compact</div>

</div>

# Compact Format

The Compact format is SICK's binary format for measurement data. It uses the least bandwidth of all formats and can be parsed very efficiently, for example by copying the bytes into a C struct with `memcpy`. The fields are not self-describing: your parser must know the layout, which SICK publishes as [Kaitai Struct](https://kaitai.io/) definitions.

The multiScan100 and picoScan100 send each scan segment in a UDP datagram.
The LRS4000 and multiScan200 carry it as a framed telegram in the TCP stream.
Every segment can be processed on its own, which keeps latency low. To work
with a full scan (frame), collect all segments with the same `frame_number`.

To inspect a captured telegram field by field, paste it into the free, browser-based [Kaitai Web IDE](https://ide.kaitai.io/) together with the definitions below.

The Compact format is organized as one frame definition that dispatches to the
individual telegram types. Types 3, 4, 6, and 7 also share the standard header:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CF[compact_frame.ksy]
    T1[type_1_primary_data_spherical_coordinates.ksy]
    T2[type_2_imu.ksy]
    T3[type_3_ambient_light.ksy]
    T4[type_4_encoder.ksy]
    T6[type_6_primary_data_multiscan200.ksy]
    T7[type_7_imu_standard_header.ksy]
    CH[compact_header.ksy]

    CF --> T1
    CF --> T2
    CF --> T3
    CF --> T4
    CF --> T6
    CF --> T7

    T6 --> CH
    T7 --> CH
    T4 --> CH
    T3 --> CH
```

The authoritative Kaitai Struct definitions are in the [`formats` folder on GitHub](https://github.com/SICKAG/KaitaiStructDescriptions/tree/public/formats). Use those files for the complete field layout instead of copying a format definition into this page.

To receive Compact data without writing your own parser, use the C++ [sick_perception_sdk](../recording/sick-perception-sdk.md). It receives the scan, IMU, and encoder data and provides the scans as point clouds.

## Frame Layout

All multi-byte values are little-endian. The frame contains a start marker, a
telegram type, the type-specific payload, and a CRC32 checksum. Verify the
checksum before processing the payload. Use the authoritative
[`compact_frame.ksy` definition on GitHub](https://github.com/SICKAG/KaitaiStructDescriptions/blob/public/formats/compact_frame.ksy)
for the complete frame layout.

## Standard Header

Telegram types 3, 4, 6, and 7 start their payload with the same header. Types
1 and 2 do not. For the complete field layout, use the authoritative
[`compact_header.ksy` definition on GitHub](https://github.com/SICKAG/KaitaiStructDescriptions/blob/public/formats/compact_header.ksy).

For type 4 with `telegram_version` 1, `payload_length` includes `sender_id`; from version 2 onwards it does not.

## Type 1: Scan Data

The scan payload is a header followed by one or more modules. Each module carries per-layer metadata plus the beam data for its layers. Read the first module size from the telegram header, then use each module's `next_module_size` to find the next one; zero marks the last module. Do not assume all modules have the same size.

Read `telegram_version`, `data_content_echos`, and `data_content_beams` before parsing beam data. Versions 3 and 4 have different beam-field ordering; version 4 also adds a distance scaling factor to the module metadata. For version 4, convert a raw distance to millimeters as `distance_mm = distance_raw × distance_scaling_factor`. All segments of one scan share `frame_number` and differ by segment index. The authoritative definition is [`type_1_primary_data_spherical_coordinates.ksy` on GitHub](https://github.com/SICKAG/KaitaiStructDescriptions/blob/public/formats/type_1_primary_data_spherical_coordinates.ksy).

To convert a beam to a 3D point, use `phi` (elevation), `theta` (azimuth), and the distance `d`:

```txt
x = d · cos(phi) · cos(theta)
y = d · cos(phi) · sin(theta)
z = d · sin(phi)
```

### Measurement Data Conventions

#### Azimuth Angles

The `theta` values within a segment are monotonically
increasing. For a 360° sensor, a segment that crosses the +180°/−180° boundary
can therefore continue beyond 180° instead of wrapping immediately to a
negative value. In the example below, the blue segment runs from 160° to 189°,
while the following green segment uses −170° to −141°. Preserve this ordering
while parsing; normalize the angles only afterwards if your application needs
the range (−180°, 180°].

![Azimuth angles of segments crossing the 180-degree boundary](../assets/data-streaming/azimuth-angle-wrap.png){ width="360" }
*Azimuth values remain monotonically increasing within a segment.*

#### Segment Counters

Normally, the segment counter is between `0` and
`number_of_segments - 1` and increases with the azimuth. The multiScan100 has
one exception: when most beams in a segment lie beyond 180°, that segment
belongs to the next frame and receives counter `0`. With 30° segments, an
angle-only calculation would produce counter `12`, which wraps to `0`. Use the
transmitted counter rather than deriving it from `theta`.

![Segment counter at the 180-degree boundary](../assets/data-streaming/segment-counter-wrap.png){ width="480" }
*The blue segment belongs mainly to the next frame and therefore receives counter 0.*

#### RSSI Values

Compact and MSGPACK represent RSSI as a dimensionless 16-bit
unsigned integer. Treat the full range from `0` to `65535` as valid, although a
device may never reach the maximum. RSSI is not standardized, so absolute
values are not directly comparable between device families.

Some device outputs scale an internally measured 8-bit RSSI value depending on
the output format:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**RSSI Values:** format, bit depth, and conversion.</p>

| Format | Bit depth | Conversion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compact type 1 | 16-bit | `16bit = (8bit / 255) × 65535` |
| MSGPACK | 16-bit | `16bit = (8bit / 255) × 65535` |
| `LMDscandata` (CoLa) | 8-bit | none; value `254` = reflector detected |

In 16-bit output, the low byte equals the high byte (for example `0xe6e6`). This is expected.

**Bit fields and beam properties.** `data_content_echos`,
`data_content_beams`, and each beam's `properties` value are bit fields. Test
bit `i` with `(value & (1 << i)) != 0`; do not interpret the complete decimal
value as a single state. In `properties`, bit 0 means that a reflector was
detected for at least one echo of the beam. This can be treated as applying to
the last echo because a reflector echo is not physically followed by another
echo on the same beam. Bits 1 through 7 are reserved and must be ignored.

### Segments (picoScan100)

The picoScan100 scans a range of 276°. One 276° rotation of the scan layer is one scan (frame). For output, each scan is split into segments of a fixed angular size:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Segments (picoScan100):** scanning frequency, segment size, and segments at 276°.</p>

| Scanning frequency | Segment size | Segments at 276° |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ≤ 25 Hz | 30° | 10 |
| ≥ 30 Hz | 60° | 5 |

![picoScan100 scan segments](../assets/picoScan100/img/data-format-picoscan-scan-segments.png)
*Example of 30° scan segments within the 276° scan range.*

Segment boundaries do not move when you reduce the scan range. Measured values in hidden angle ranges are filled with zeros, and a segment that is completely hidden is not sent. Example: 180° (−90° to +90°) at 40 Hz gives 4 segments.

### Segments (multiScan100)

The multiScan100 captures a 360° frame across its scan layers and divides the
output into time-based segments. Each segment contains data from all scan
layers, but the azimuth ranges of those layers do not necessarily line up
spatially. Raw output keeps the original layer timing. Rectified output aligns
the layer start angles as closely as possible and adds at least one segment
interval of latency. See the [multiScan100 overview](../multiScan100/index.md)
for device-specific output context.

![multiScan100 scan segments](../assets/multiScan100/img/data-format-multiscan-scan-segments.png)
*A 360° frame split into twelve 30° segments, each with its own time stamp.*

Each segment covers a different time within the rotation, so `t0` to `t11`
increase in the scan direction. Use the per-segment time stamps rather than the
frame time when you fuse the data with motion or another sensor.

## Type 2: IMU

A flat, fixed-size payload from the integrated inertial measurement unit. It
has no standard Compact header and no optional fields. IMU output is available
on multiScan100 and picoScan100; sampling and available fields depend on the
product. The LRS4000 provides IMU data through CoLa events or
`GET /api/InertialMeasurementUnit`, not as a Compact telegram. The authoritative Compact layout is
[`type_2_imu.ksy` on GitHub](https://github.com/SICKAG/KaitaiStructDescriptions/blob/public/formats/type_2_imu.ksy).

The data is specified in the following coordinate system based on the DIN 70000
system: The x-axis lies on the 90° beam of the 0° plane. The y-axis is
perpendicular to the x-axis and lies in the 0° plane. The y-values increase in
the counter rotation direction (right-handed system). The z-axis is
perpendicular to the y-axis and the top of the device points towards increasing
z-values.

![IMU coordinate system showing the x, y, and z axes and their rotation directions](../assets/data-streaming/imu-coordinate-system.png){ width="520" }
*IMU coordinate system based on DIN 70000.*

## Type 3: Ambient Light

The ambient-light image of the multiScan200 is sent as a separate telegram.
The sensor captures it passively through the same receiver as the distance
data. It follows the [standard header](#standard-header). Use the
authoritative definition linked below for its payload layout.

Distance and ambient-light data measured at the same time share the same
`frame_number`. Use the authoritative
[`type_3_ambient_light.ksy` definition on GitHub](https://github.com/SICKAG/KaitaiStructDescriptions/blob/public/formats/type_3_ambient_light.ksy)
for the complete payload layout.

## Type 4: Encoder

Reports an external rotary encoder attached to a moving axis (picoScan150).
One encoder telegram is sent per scan frame and linked to it by `frame_number`.
It follows the [standard header](#standard-header). Use the authoritative
definition linked below for its payload layout.

See [3D With 2D LiDARs](../integration-notes/3d-with-2d-lidars.md) for how to fuse encoder and scan data.

Use the authoritative [`type_4_encoder.ksy` definition on GitHub](https://github.com/SICKAG/KaitaiStructDescriptions/blob/public/formats/type_4_encoder.ksy) for the complete payload layout.

## Type 6: Scan Data (multiScan200)

The scan data of the multiScan200. One telegram carries one segment: a block
of columns (slots), each with all layers. It follows the [standard
header](#standard-header). Use the authoritative definition linked below for
the complete segment header and data-block layout.

Convert each pixel to a 3D point with the [formula for type 1](#type-1-scan-data), using the elevation angle of its layer as `phi` and the azimuth angle of its column as `theta`. Use the authoritative [`type_6_primary_data_multiscan200.ksy` definition on GitHub](https://github.com/SICKAG/KaitaiStructDescriptions/blob/public/formats/type_6_primary_data_multiscan200.ksy) for the complete segment header and data-block layout.

For interlaced scan configurations, `number_of_interlace_steps` is greater than 1 and consecutive frames must be combined to cover the full field of view; `current_interlace_index` identifies each frame's position in that sequence. Configured data reduction can also leave zero-filled distance and RSSI values in the fixed-size Compact segment, including for angles outside the selected range. A zero value alone therefore does not mean that the beam or column is absent.

## Type 7: IMU with Standard Header

The IMU data of the multiScan200. The content matches [type 2](#type-2-imu), but the payload starts with the [standard header](#standard-header) and has no `telegram_version` field of its own:

Use the authoritative [`type_7_imu_standard_header.ksy` definition on GitHub](https://github.com/SICKAG/KaitaiStructDescriptions/blob/public/formats/type_7_imu_standard_header.ksy) for the complete payload layout.

## Transport

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Transport:** transport, formats and devices, connection, delivery guarantee, and best for.</p>

| Transport | Formats and devices | Connection | Delivery guarantee | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UDP unicast | Compact, MSGPACK (multiScan100); Compact, MSGPACK (picoScan100) | Sensor sends to one host | None; packets can be lost or reordered | Low-latency data to one host |
| UDP multicast | Compact (multiScan100); Compact, MSGPACK (picoScan100) | Sensor sends one stream to a group | None; packets can be lost or reordered | The same data to several hosts |
| TCP | Compact (LRS4000 and multiScan200); [LMDscandata](./lmdscandata-format.md) where supported | Client connects to a device-specific data port or CoLa port | Ordered and error-checked | Data integrity over latency; PLCs |

For UDP, select the required format in the data-output settings and set the
destination IP address and port. For multiScan100 and picoScan100, the REST
API exposes Ethernet destination settings for the scan data stream. The
picoScan100 factory default is `192.168.0.100:2115`.

The multiScan200 sends Compact data over TCP to avoid data loss, on separate
ports per content:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Transport:** TCP port, content, and telegram type.</p>

| TCP port | Content | Telegram type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2115` | Distance and RSSI, optionally with ambient light | [6](#type-6-scan-data-multiscan200) |
| `2116` | Ambient light only | [3](#type-3-ambient-light) |
| `2117` | IMU | [7](#type-7-imu-with-standard-header) |

Select **TCP Compact** as data output mode (`sWN dataOutputMode 1`); see the [multiScan200 CoLa Telegram Listing](../multiScan200/cola-telegram-listing.md#set-data-output-mode-swn-dataoutputmode).

The LRS4000 `ScanDataFormat` REST parameter supports Compact output. The
Compact stream uses TCP, with port `2115` as the Compact data port.

For multicast, set the destination to a multicast address in the range `224.0.0.0` to `239.255.255.255`. Every receiving host joins the same group and listens on the configured UDP port. The sensor sends each packet only once, however many hosts receive it. Make sure that switches and routers forward multicast traffic, and use IGMP snooping when several receivers are connected.

## Wireshark Dissector

SICK provides a Wireshark dissector for Compact measurement and IMU data, so you can inspect the stream field by field instead of reading raw bytes. It supports the Compact format only. Use it to confirm framing, ports, CRCs, and decoded values before you debug your own parser.

### Install the Dissector

1. Download and install [Wireshark](https://www.wireshark.org/download.html).
2. Download the dissector: [COMPACT_Dissector.lua](../assets/data-streaming/COMPACT_Dissector.lua).
3. In Wireshark, open **Help > About Wireshark > Folders** and copy the file to the **Personal Lua Plugins** folder.
4. Restart Wireshark.

### Decode Compact Data

Configure the sensor to output Compact format, then capture on the Ethernet
interface connected to the sensor. Enter `compact` as the display filter. The
Protocol column shows `COMPACT`; select a packet to inspect the decoded
structure and values such as distance.

On Windows, set the Ethernet network profile to Private so that the firewall does not block the stream:

```powershell
Get-NetConnectionProfile
Set-NetConnectionProfile -InterfaceIndex 18 -NetworkCategory Private
```

Replace `18` with the interface index reported by `Get-NetConnectionProfile`.

To disable the plug-in temporarily, choose **Analyze > Enabled Protocols** and clear its checkbox. See [Frame Layout](#frame-layout) for the telegram structure and [Wireshark | pcap](../recording/wireshark-pcap.md) for recording traffic.

### Related Articles

- [How to use the Wireshark dissector for Compact measurement and IMU data](https://support.sick.com/sick-knowledgebase/article?id=26b09bc9-22db-f011-8544-7c1e5228c8a2)
<!-- SICK video: 0_jnvpbvv5; source: https://support.sick.com/sick-knowledgebase/article?id=aeac8012-be4e-f011-877b-000d3a2a3508 -->
*How to receive IMU data and dissect it with Wireshark.*
- [How to use Wireshark to dissect Compact data](https://support.sick.com/sick-knowledgebase/article?id=9338f032-bd4e-f011-877b-7c1e5228c8a2)

# Filter Details

Filters run on the sensor and change the measurement data before it is sent. Use them to reduce bandwidth, remove unwanted points, and keep the data your application needs. The available filters and their settings differ between devices; each section lists the devices it applies to.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Filter Details:** filter, effect, side effect, and devices.</p>

| Filter | Effect | Side effect | Devices |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Interval](#interval-filter) | Sends only every n-th scan | Lower output rate | multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan150 |
| [Fog](#fog-filter) | Removes fog echoes at close range | - | multiScan100, picoScan150 |
| [Echo](#echo-filter) | Selects which echoes are sent | - | LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan150 |
| [Particle](#particle-filter) | Removes dust, rain, and snow hits | Device-specific settings and latency | LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan100 |
| [Moving average](#moving-average-filter) | Averages distances over several scans | Delayed output | multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan150 |
| [Blooming](#blooming-filter) | Removes blooming artifacts next to highly reflective objects | - | multiScan200 |
| [Angle range](#angle-range-filter) | Keeps beams inside a horizontal and vertical angle range | - | multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan150 |
| [Layer](#layer-filter) | Removes complete scan layers from the output | Reduced vertical coverage | multiScan100 |
| [Vertical FoV](#vertical-fov-filter) | Keeps nested vertical regions at different resolutions | Raw stream only | multiScan200 |
| [Angle range focus](#angle-range-focus-filter) | Keeps a 3D angle range with an optional full-resolution region | Raw stream only | multiScan200 |
| [Rectangular](#rectangular-filter) | Keeps points inside an X/Y rectangle | Other points set to 0; data size unchanged | multiScan100, picoScan150 |
| [Distance](#distance-filter) | Keeps points inside a radial range | Other points set to 0; data size unchanged | LRS4000, multiScan100, picoScan150 |
| [Ground](#ground-filter) | Filters ground returns with configurable thresholds | Variant and configuration dependent | multiScan100 |
| [Mean](#mean-filter) | Averages measurement data | Device-specific behavior | LRS4000 |
| [Median](#median-filter) | Applies a median filter to measurement data | Device-specific behavior | LRS4000 |

The filters run one after another, each on the result of the previous one. For exact parameter names and value ranges, see the product's OpenAPI reference: [LRS4000](../LRS4000/rest-api-openapi.md), [multiScan100](../multiScan100/rest-api-openapi.md), [multiScan200](../multiScan200/rest-api-openapi.md), or [picoScan100](../picoScan100/rest-api-openapi.md).

## Interval Filter

The interval filter reduces the scan output rate by a configurable reduction
factor from 2 to 50. For example, a factor of three outputs only every third
scan, reducing the output rate to one third. On picoScan100, this REST setting
is exposed by the picoScan150 OpenAPI.

## Fog Filter

The fog filter removes unwanted echoes at close range (approximately 3 m). This
reduces false activations in fog. On picoScan100, this REST setting is exposed
by the picoScan150 OpenAPI. The multiScan200 has no configurable fog filter.

## Echo Filter

The echo filter suppresses measurement data caused by edge hits, rain, dust,
snow, and other ambient conditions. Pulses attributed to undesirable ambient
conditions are not output. The selectable echoes differ by device:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Echo Filter:** device and selectable echoes.</p>

| Device | Selectable echoes |
| --- | --- |
| picoScan150 | First echo, last echo, or all echoes |
| multiScan200 | First echo, last echo, strongest echo, all echoes, or all echoes with the strongest first |
| LRS4000, multiScan100 | Read the selectable echo options for the installed firmware in the device's OpenAPI description. |

On the multiScan200, field evaluation always uses a single echo. If all echoes
are selected, field evaluation uses the first echo.

<img src="../../assets/picoScan100/img/configuration-echo-filter.png" alt="Echo filter example" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto;">
*Example of retaining or suppressing an echo caused by ambient conditions.*

## Particle Filter

The particle filter suppresses small, irrelevant reflection pulses caused by
dust, raindrops, snowflakes, and similar particles. The filter settings differ
by device.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Particle Filter:** device and settings.</p>

| Device | Settings |
| --- | --- |
| LRS4000 | On/off and a distance-step threshold from 500 to 5000 mm |
| multiScan100 | On/off and a distance-step threshold from 20 to 5000 mm |
| multiScan200 | On/off, a distance threshold from 20 to 2000 mm, and the minimum number of neighbors from 0 to 8 |
| picoScan100 | On/off and a distance-step threshold from 20 to 5000 mm |

For LRS4000, multiScan100, and picoScan100, the threshold is the required
distance step between the echo to be filtered and the echoes of surrounding
beam angles. On multiScan200, a point needs at least the configured number of
neighboring measurements within the distance threshold. In interlaced
multiScan200 scan configurations (10 to 12), the filter compares measurements
from different angular positions, so its effect can change. In the Compact
format (telegram type 6), bit 6 of the multiScan200 echo properties marks
points detected as particles.

## Moving Average Filter

On picoScan150, the moving average filter smooths distance values by calculating the arithmetic
mean over several scans of the same point. Configure an averaging depth of two
to four scans. The first value is output only after the configured number of
scans; invalid distance values (`0`) are excluded from the average.

Example of a four-scan moving average for representative angular positions
(distance values in mm):

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Moving Average Filter:** scan/output, angle 3, angle 4, angle 5, angle 6, angle 7, and angle 8.</p>

| Scan/output | Angle 3 | Angle 4 | Angle 5 | Angle 6 | Angle 7 | Angle 8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Scan 1 | 1100 | 1100 | 1150 | 1150 | 1380 | 1380 |
| Scan 2 | 1200 | 1200 | 1190 | 950 | 1500 | 1500 |
| Scan 3 | 1150 | 1450 | 1200 | 1200 | 1450 | 1450 |
| Scan 4 | 1170 | 1170 | 1220 | 1220 | 1470 | 1150 |
| 1. Output (scans 1–4) | 1155 | 1230 | 1190 | 1130 | 1450 | 1370 |
| Scan 5 | 0 | 1110 | 1150 | 1150 | 1380 | 1380 |
| 2. Output (scans 2–5) | 1173 | 1233 | 1190 | 1130 | 1450 | 1370 |
| Scan 6 | 1200 | 1210 | 1190 | 0 | 1500 | 1500 |
| 3. Output (scans 3–6) | 1173 | 1235 | 1190 | 1190 | 1450 | 1370 |
| Scan 7 | 1150 | 0 | 1200 | 1200 | 1450 | 1450 |
| 4. Output (scans 4–7) | 1173 | 1163 | 1190 | 1190 | 1450 | 1370 |

Individual outliers still influence the average. Invalid distance values (`0`)
are excluded, so fewer scans contribute at those positions (for example angle 3
in the 2nd output: (1200 + 1150 + 1170) / 3 = 1173).

On multiScan200, the moving average filter is called high precision mode and
can only be switched on or off. It averages the distance of each point over
several scans, which reduces distance noise while the output rate stays the
same. The output is delayed by about 0.5 s. If the distance of an object
changes significantly, averaging stops for that object. Use it for static
scenes only. It has no effect in interlaced scan configurations (10 to 12).

On multiScan100, the REST API exposes `LFPmovingAveragingFilter`. Check the
OpenAPI description for the available averaging depth and limits for the
installed firmware.

## Blooming Filter

Highly reflective objects such as retroreflectors can create false points next
to the object (blooming). The blooming filter removes them. Select the strength
low, medium (default), or strong. In the Compact format (telegram type 6),
bit 2 of the echo properties marks points detected as blooming.

## Angle Range Filter

The angle range filter limits the output to a horizontal (theta) and vertical
(phi) angle range. A beam increment outputs only every n-th beam.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Angle Range Filter:** comparison criterion, multiScan100, multiScan200, and picoScan150.</p>

| | multiScan100 | multiScan200 | picoScan150 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Horizontal range | See OpenAPI | −180° to +180° | −138° to +138° |
| Vertical range | See OpenAPI | −90° to +90° | −90° to +90° |
| Beam increment | See OpenAPI | 1 to 50, separately for horizontal and vertical | 1 or more |

On multiScan200, beams outside the range are not transmitted, which reduces the
data size. The ambient-light image is limited in the same way.

## Layer Filter

The multiScan100 layer filter removes complete scan layers from the output
data. Configure one Boolean value per layer through `LFPlayerFilter`; only
enabled layers are serialized. This reduces the data volume when an application
needs only part of the sensor's vertical coverage. The filter changes the
output, not the physical scan performed by the sensor.

## Vertical FoV Filter

The multiScan200 CoLa command `verticalAngleRangeFilter` restricts raw
streaming data to an outer vertical region of interest (ROI). An optional inner
ROI must lie completely inside the outer ROI. Each region has its own layer
increment from 1 to 50, so the inner region can retain more vertical detail
while the surrounding region is subsampled more strongly. Layers outside the
outer ROI are not transmitted.

The filter also limits ambient-light data. In **Full** mode, the remaining
ambient-light region keeps its full vertical resolution. In **Matching** mode,
its vertical resolution matches the primary measurement data, with one
ambient-light pixel per beam.

## Angle Range Focus Filter

The multiScan200 `angleRangeFocusFilter` restricts raw streaming data to a 3D
field of view defined by horizontal (`theta`) and vertical (`phi`) limits.
Beams outside this range are not transmitted. Separate horizontal and vertical
increments from 1 to 50 can subsample the remaining data.

An optional focus region preserves full resolution inside a smaller horizontal
or vertical region while the surrounding data remains subsampled. This filter
affects raw data streaming only and does not affect field evaluation.

## Rectangular Filter

After the measurement filters, data-reduction settings and the region of
interest filter limit the points passed on for further processing. On
picoScan100, this REST setting is exposed by the picoScan150 OpenAPI.

When the rectangular filter is active, only scan parts within the rectangle are retained. The filter does not reduce the data; points outside the rectangle are set to zero. Adjust the rectangle by setting the minimum and maximum X and Y values in millimeters.

## Distance Filter

The distance filter limits the measured radial distance and therefore affects a
circular area around the product. It does not reduce the data; points outside
the selected radial range are set to zero. To keep a circular area, set the
maximum range to the required radius in millimeters. To keep a ring, set the
maximum range to the required radius and the minimum range to a value greater
than 0 mm. On picoScan100, this REST setting is exposed by the picoScan150
OpenAPI.

## Ground Filter

The multiScan100 REST API exposes `groundFilterEnable`,
`groundFilterThresholds`, and `groundFilterType`. The filter can reduce false
field-evaluation triggers caused by the ground while retaining detection of
small objects when configured correctly. The ground filter is not applied to
the raw measurement-data streaming path. Availability can depend on the
variant and software package. See
[multiScan100 release notes](../multiScan100/release-notes.md) and the
[multiScan100 OpenAPI reference](../multiScan100/rest-api-openapi.md).

## Mean Filter

The LRS4000 firmware 1.10.0 OpenAPI description exposes a `MeanFilter` setting.
Use that reference for its parameters and permitted values.

## Median Filter

The LRS4000 firmware 1.10.0 OpenAPI description exposes an
`LFPmedianfilter` setting. Use that reference for its parameters and permitted
values.

<!-- Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/lmdscandata-format/ -->

# LMDscandata Format

`LMDscandata` is a scan data telegram of SICK's [CoLa interface](../configuration/cola-interface.md). LRS4000 and picoScan100 expose it as a selectable scan data format. On picoScan100 it is sent over a TCP connection that the client opens to the sensor, so delivery is ordered and error-checked. Use it for PLCs and integrations that already use CoLa. For new high-rate integrations, use [Compact](./compact-format.md) or [MSGPACK](./msgpack-format.md) over the transport supported by the device.

## Receive LMDscandata

1. Select **LMDscandata** as the measurement data output format (`sWN ScanDataFormat`, or in SOPASair under **Application > Data output**).
2. Open a TCP connection to the sensor: port `2111` for CoLa A or `2112` for CoLa B.
3. Request data:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Receive LMDscandata:** telegram and result.</p>

| Telegram | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `sRN LMDscandata` | Returns one scan (polling) |
| `sEN LMDscandata 1` | Starts continuous output: one telegram per scan |
| `sEN LMDscandata 0` | Stops continuous output |

No data is sent during boot-up or in some error states (for example Device Not Ready). A login session does not block the output. RSSI in LMDscandata is 8-bit; the value `254` marks a detected reflector.

If the output format is not set to LMDscandata, `sRN LMDscandata` still returns an `sRA LMDscandata` telegram, but every field is `0`. There is no error code, so check the output format first when you only receive zeros.

## Angle Reference

LMDscandata uses the CoLa angle convention: `90°` points straight ahead along the sensor X axis. Compact, MSGPACK, and the REST API use `0°` for straight ahead. The same full scan of the picoScan100 therefore starts at `-48°` in LMDscandata and at `-138°` in Compact. Subtract `90°` from an LMDscandata angle to compare it with Compact or MSGPACK data. The start angle and the angular step in the telegram are given in 1/10000°.

## Configure and Parse

- Configure the picoScan100 telegram content, such as the echoes and RSSI, with [`sWN LMDscandatacfg`](../picoScan100/cola-telegram-listing.md#configure-the-data-content-for-the-scan-swn-lmdscandatacfg). Smaller telegrams reduce PLC load.
- The picoScan100 field layout is in the [picoScan100 CoLa Telegram Listing](../picoScan100/cola-telegram-listing.md#poll-one-telegram-srn-lmdscandata).
- For TCP stream parsing (partial and concatenated telegrams), follow [PLC Integration](../integration-notes/plc-integration.md#polling-and-cola-b-framing).

<!-- Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/msgpack-format/ -->

# MSGPACK Format

MSGPACK encodes the measurement data with the [MessagePack](https://msgpack.org/) standard. Unlike [Compact](./compact-format.md), it is self-describing: every field has a keyword, so any standard MessagePack library can parse it without knowing the exact layout. The price is more bandwidth than Compact.

Like Compact, each data package carries one scan segment. Each segment can be processed on its own for low latency; collect all segments with the same `FrameNumber` to get a complete scan. See [multiScan100 segments](./compact-format.md#segments-multiscan100) and [picoScan100 segments](./compact-format.md#segments-picoscan100) for device-specific behavior.

SICK's Python [ScanSegmentAPI](https://github.com/SICKAG/ScanSegmentAPI) (`scansegmentapi/msgpack.py`) is the reference implementation of this format.

## Framing

Each MSGPACK buffer is wrapped in a frame. Size and checksum are little-endian `uint32` values.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Framing:** offset, size, and content.</p>

| Offset | Size | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 4 bytes | `02 02 02 02` (4 × `<STX>`) |
| 4 | 4 bytes | Size n of the MSGPACK buffer in bytes (without the checksum) |
| 8 | n bytes | MSGPACK buffer |
| 8 + n | 4 bytes | CRC32 over the MSGPACK buffer only, without the STX bytes and the size |

## MSGPACK Keywords

To save bandwidth, keywords are encoded as `uint8` codes instead of strings. Map the codes back to names with the table below. After removing the framing, parse the buffer with a standard MessagePack parser. Some parsers must be told to accept integer map keys; in Python:

```python
unpacked = msgpack.unpackb(msgpack_buffer, strict_map_key=False)
```

### Used MSGPACK Keywords and Associated uint8 Codes

Names follow the SICK reference implementation. Some examples use different
capitalization, such as `TimeStampStart` or `PropertyValues`; on the wire only
the code is sent.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Used MSGPACK Keywords and Associated uint8 Codes:** keyword name, code, and description.</p>

| Keyword name | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `class` | `0x10` | Class name of the map: `Scan` or `ScanSegment` ([ScanSegment](#serialization-of-the-scansegment-class), [Scan](#serialization-of-the-scan-class)) |
| `data` | `0x11` | Data part of a ScanSegment, Scan, or array ([arrays](#serialization-of-arrays)) |
| `numOfElems` | `0x12` | Number of elements in an array |
| `elemSz` | `0x13` | Size of one array element in bytes |
| `endian` | `0x14` | Endianness of the array elements |
| `elemTypes` | `0x15` | Type of the array elements |
| `little` | `0x30` | Value: little-endian |
| `float32` | `0x31` | Value: data type float32 |
| `uint32` | `0x32` | Value: data type uint32 |
| `uint8` | `0x33` | Value: data type uint8 |
| `uint16` | `0x34` | Value: data type uint16 |
| `int16` | `0x35` | Value: data type int16 |
| `ChannelTheta` | `0x50` | Channel with azimuth angles |
| `ChannelPhi` | `0x51` | Channel with elevation angles |
| `DistValues` | `0x52` | Channel with distance values |
| `RssiValues` | `0x53` | Channel with RSSI values |
| `PropertiesValues` | `0x54` | Channel with beam properties, for example reflector |
| `Scan` | `0x70` | Class name `Scan` |
| `TimestampStart` | `0x71` | Time stamp of the first beam of a scan |
| `TimestampStop` | `0x72` | Time stamp of the last beam of a scan |
| `ThetaStart` | `0x73` | Azimuth angle of the first beam of a scan |
| `ThetaStop` | `0x74` | Azimuth angle of the last beam of a scan |
| `ScanNumber` | `0x75` | Scan number |
| `ModuleID` | `0x76` | ID of the measuring module |
| `BeamCount` | `0x77` | Number of beams in a scan |
| `EchoCount` | `0x78` | Number of echoes in a scan |
| `ScanSegment` | `0x90` | Class name `ScanSegment` |
| `SegmentCounter` | `0x91` | Segment number |
| `FrameNumber` | `0x92` | Frame number |
| `Availability` | `0x93` | Availability of a segment |
| `SenderId` | `0x94` | Sender ID (device serial number) |
| `SegmentSize` | `0x95` | Segment size |
| `SegmentData` | `0x96` | Array with the measurement data per layer |
| `LayerId` | `0xA0` | Array with layer IDs |
| `TelegramCounter` | `0xB0` | Telegram counter |
| `TimestampTransmit` | `0xB1` | Transmit time stamp |

## Serialization of a Segment

Each data package carries one ScanSegment. Its `SegmentData` array holds one [Scan](#serialization-of-the-scan-class) per layer of the sensor:

```text
ScanSegment
├── TelegramCounter
├── TimestampTransmit
├── SegmentCounter
├── FrameNumber
├── Availability
├── SenderId
├── LayerId
└── SegmentData
    ├── Scan 1
    ├── Scan 2
    ├── ...
    └── Scan N
```

Metadata fields are plain MessagePack values. Measurement arrays (distances, RSSI, angles, properties) are an exception: they are stored as binary blobs, see [Serialization Of Arrays](#serialization-of-arrays).

### Notation Used

The following notes on the notation used relate to the description of the structures encoded in MSGPACK:

- `msgpack_map_header` denotes the header of a MessagePack map, see the [MessagePack specification](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack/blob/master/spec.md#map-format-family).
- Names correspond to the [keyword table](#used-msgpack-keywords-and-associated-uint8-codes); on the wire, each name is its `uint8` code.
- Angle brackets mark placeholders, for example `<numOfElems>` for the number of array elements.
- The structures are written in a JSON-like notation, but the data is encoded according to the [MessagePack specification](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack/blob/master/spec.md).

### Serialization of the ScanSegment Class

The ScanSegment class is represented as a nesting of MSGPACK maps as follows:

```msgpack-schema
msgpack_map_header {
  "class": ScanSegment,
  "data": msgpack_map_header {
    "TelegramCounter": <telegramCounter>,
    "TimestampTransmit": <timestampTransmit>,
    "SegmentCounter": <segmentCounter>,
    "FrameNumber": <frameNumber>,
    "Availability": <availability>,
    "SenderId": <senderId>,
    "LayerId": <layerIdVector>,
    "SegmentData": <segmentData>
  }
}
```

The meaning of the individual fields is shown in the following table.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Serialization of the ScanSegment Class:** name, type, and description.</p>

| Name | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------------- |
| TelegramCounter | MSGPACK int | Counts all telegrams with measurement data sent in MSGPACK format since switching on the device. The counter starts at 1. |
| TimestampTransmit | MSGPACK int | Sensor system time in µs since 1.1.1970 00:00 in UTC. |
| SegmentCounter | MSGPACK int | Index of the segment within the frame. |
| FrameNumber | MSGPACK int | Counts the number of full revolutions since the device was started. |
| Availability | MSGPACK int | Reserved |
| SenderId | MSGPACK int | Device serial number. It can be used to detect on the recipient which sensor the data was sent from. |
| LayerId | MSGPACK array of int | Array of layer indices. The layer indices start at 1 and increase with decreasing elevation angle. |
| SegmentData | MSGPACK array of scans | Array of elements of the Scan class (see [Serialization Of The Scan Class](#serialization-of-the-scan-class)) that contain the actual measurement data. The following applies: The scan at position i has the layer number LayerId[i]. |

The arrays LayerId and SegmentData are MSGPACK arrays as per the MSGPACK specification and are not represented like arrays containing measurement data (see "[Serialization of arrays](#serialization-of-arrays)").

### Serialization of the Scan Class

The Scan class is represented as a nesting of MSGPACK maps as follows:

```msgpack-schema
msgpack_map_header {
  "class": Scan,
  "data": msgpack_map_header {
    "TimestampStart": <timestampStart>,
    "TimestampStop": <timestampStop>,
    "ThetaStart": <thetaStart>,
    "ThetaStop": <thetaStop>,
    "ScanNumber": <scanNumber>,
    "ModuleID": <moduleId>,
    "ChannelTheta": <channelTheta>,
    "ChannelPhi": <channelPhi>,
    "DistValues": <distValues>,
    "RssiValues": <rssiValues>,
    "PropertiesValues": <propertiesValues>,
    "BeamCount": <beamCount>,
    "EchoCount": <echoCount>
  }
}
```

The meaning of the individual fields is shown in the following table:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Serialization of the Scan Class:** name, type, and description.</p>

| Name | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------------- |
| TimestampStart | MSGPACK int | Acquisition time of the first beam of the scan in µs. The device's internal time base is used or, if the sensor offers the feature, the time set externally. |
| TimestampStop | MSGPACK int | Acquisition time of the last beam of the scan in µs. The device's internal time base is used or, if the sensor offers the feature, the time set externally. |
| ThetaStart | MSGPACK int | Azimuth angle of the first beam of the scan in radians. |
| ThetaStop | MSGPACK int | Azimuth angle of the last beam of the scan in radians. |
| ScanNumber | MSGPACK int | Not used. |
| ModuleID | MSGPACK int | Number of the physical module that generated the data. In the case of the multiScan100, for example, this is one of the two measuring modules. |
| ChannelTheta | array of float32 | Array of azimuth angles of a specific beam in radians. The encoding of the data in this array is described in "[Serialization of arrays](#serialization-of-arrays)". The user can configure whether the array is present in the data structure. |
| ChannelPhi | array of float32 | Array with the elevation angle of the scan in radians. Each Scan covers one layer, so this array contains one element. The encoding of the data in this array is described in "[Serialization of arrays](#serialization-of-arrays)". The user can configure whether the array is present in the data structure. |
| DistValues | array of (array of float32) | Array containing an array of distance values for each echo of the scan. The number of sub-arrays corresponds to the number of echoes in the scan, see also the EchoCount field below. The distance values are specified in mm. The encoding of the data in this array is described in "[Serialization of arrays](#serialization-of-arrays)". The user can configure whether the array is present in the data structure. |
| RssiValues | array of (array of uint16) | Array containing an array of RSSI values for each echo of the scan. The number of sub-arrays corresponds to the number of echoes in the scan, see also the EchoCount field below. For the representation of RSSI values, see [RSSI scaling](./compact-format.md#type-1-scan-data). The encoding of the data in this array is described in "[Serialization of arrays](#serialization-of-arrays)". The user can configure whether the array is present in the data structure. |
| PropertiesValues | array of uint8 | Array with additional properties, for example "reflector", for each beam of a scan. The encoding of the data in this array is described in "[Serialization of arrays](#serialization-of-arrays)". This array is optional. |
| BeamCount | MSGPACK int | Number of beams in the current scan. |
| EchoCount | MSGPACK int | Number of echoes in the current scan. |

For more details about the MSGPACK int format family, see the [official msgpack specification](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack/blob/master/spec.md#int-format-family).

![DistValues and RssiValues array structure](../assets/data-streaming/distvalues-rssivalues-structure.png)
*DistValues and RssiValues array structure.*

The diagram illustrates the nested array structure with 3 echoes and 15 beams, showing how each beam contains values for all echoes in both DistValues and RssiValues arrays.

### Serialization of Arrays

Arrays of measurement data (ChannelTheta, ChannelPhi, DistValues, RssiValues, and PropertiesValues) are encoded as follows:

```msgpack-schema
msgpack_map_header {
  "numOfElems": <number of array elements>,
  "elemSz": <size of one array element in bytes>,
  "endian": little,
  "elemTypes": <typesArray>,
  "data": <binaryData>
}
```

The meaning of the individual fields of the Array class are shown in the following table.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Serialization of Arrays:** name and description.</p>

| Name | Description |
| ------ | ------------- |
| numOfElems | Number of array elements |
| elemSz | Size of an array element in bytes, e.g., 4 for float32 or 1 for uint8. |
| endian | The value is always little |
| elemTypes | Array of element types. Only arrays with one element are supported here. Example: {float32} for an array of float32 values. An array of tuples would need multiple element types; such arrays are not used. |
| data | Actual payload. The data is encoded as a byte array in the MSGPACK format and can be copied directly into a structure/array after parsing the MSGPACK structure, taking into account the endianness and the data type. |

<!-- Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/websocket-events/ -->

# WebSocket Events

Instead of polling the REST API for state, you can open one persistent WebSocket connection, register the events you care about, and the device pushes a JSON frame every time a value changes. Use it for low-latency notifications: field-evaluation results, I/O switching, temperature alarms, firmware-update progress.

## Endpoint and Connection

```txt
ws://<device-ip>/apievents
```

Port 80 is used, and no authentication is required to open the connection.
No periodic ping/keep-alive is needed.
Every event has a matching REST endpoint of the same name; the `data` payload is identical to `GET /api/<EventName>`. Use REST for one-shot reads/writes, WebSocket for change notifications.

The device sends compressed frames (`RSV1 = 1`). Your WebSocket library must negotiate the `permessage-deflate` extension during the handshake, or the device closes the connection with protocol error 1002. Libraries that auto-negotiate (e.g. C++ `httplib::WebSocketClient`) work out of the box; Python's `websocket-client` does not do this by default, so use a library that negotiates it, or enable compression explicitly.

## Message Format

All messages are JSON text frames. Five types are used.

Register (client → device): one message per event, where `clientId` is a caller-chosen integer echoed back for that registration.

```json
{ "type": "register", "event": "temperatureAlarmStatus", "clientId": 1 }
```

Registration confirmation (device → client): on success (`status: 0`) the device immediately sends the current value. Dispatch it exactly like a live event; it is your first data point.

```json
{ "type": "register", "event": "temperatureAlarmStatus", "clientId": 1,
  "status": 0, "data": { "AlarmState": "NoAlarm" } }
```

Event push (device → client): sent whenever the value changes.

```json
{ "type": "event", "event": "temperatureAlarmStatus", "clientId": 1,
  "status": 0, "data": { "AlarmState": "OverTemp" } }
```

Error (device → client): sent for an unknown or unavailable event. The connection stays open and other registrations are unaffected.

```json
{ "type": "register", "event": "nonExistentEvent", "clientId": 2,
  "status": 1, "error": "Failed to register event ... Does the event exist?" }
```

Deregister (client → device): no response is sent.

```json
{ "type": "deregister", "event": "temperatureAlarmStatus", "clientId": 1 }
```

## Step by Step

Send registration messages one at a time with at least 200 ms between consecutive frames. If several `register` frames arrive in a tight burst the device resets the connection. The delay is only needed during the initial registration sequence.

1. Open the WebSocket to `ws://<device-ip>/apievents` (with `permessage-deflate`).
2. Register your events, one `register` per event, unique `clientId`, at least 200 ms apart.
3. Receive initial values: each successful registration replies with `type: "register"`, `status: 0`, and the current value in `data`. Dispatch it like a live event.
4. Handle events: keep reading; on change the device pushes `type: "event"`.
5. Handle errors and reconnect: log any `status != 0`; other registrations still work.

## Dispatch Pattern

Dispatch on both `type` and `status` so you also catch the initial value. The snippets are language-neutral pseudocode:

```python
connection = websocket_connect(
    "ws://<device-ip>/apievents",
    compression="permessage-deflate",
)
```

```python
for client_id, event_name in enumerate(events):
    connection.send({
        "type": "register",
        "event": event_name,
        "clientId": client_id,
    })
    sleep(milliseconds=200)
```

```python
while connection.is_open():
    obj = json_parse(connection.receive())

    if obj["type"] == "event" or (
        obj["type"] == "register" and obj["status"] == 0
    ):
        dispatch(obj["event"], obj["data"])
    elif obj["type"] == "register" and obj["status"] != 0:
        log_error(obj["event"], obj["error"])
```

## Advanced: Throttle and Queue

Pass an optional `options` object when registering.

Throttle caps delivery frequency; excess events are dropped before queuing:

```json
{ "type": "register", "event": "LSPdatetime", "clientId": 7,
  "options": { "throttle": { "minOutputIntervalMs": 5000 } } }
```

Queue means each event has its own per-event queue on the shared connection:

```json
"options": { "queue": { "priority": "HIGH", "maxSize": 10, "discardIfFull": "OLDEST" } }
```

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Advanced: Throttle and Queue:** field, values, default, and meaning.</p>

| Field | Values | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `priority` | `HIGH`, `MID`, `LOW` | `MID` | Processing priority among events on this connection |
| `maxSize` | integer | 1 | Maximum buffered events |
| `discardIfFull` | `OLDEST`, `NEWEST` | `OLDEST` | Which event to drop when full |

## Subscribable Events

Event names are case-sensitive. Full data schemas are in the OpenAPI spec under the matching `GET` endpoint.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Subscribable Events:** event and typical trigger.</p>

| Event | Typical trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `DeviceStatus` | Device operational state changes |
| `SCdevicestate` | Safety controller state |
| `FieldEvaluationResult` | Object enters/leaves a detection field |
| `perpendicularDistanceResult` | Perpendicular-distance result changes |
| `InputState` / `OutputState` / `PortState` | Digital I/O state changes (`PortState` preferred) |
| `ContaminationData` / `ContaminationResult` | Lens contamination per sector / global result |
| `InertialMeasurementUnit` | Live IMU data |
| `CurrentTempDev` / `temperatureAlarmStatus` | Temperature (°C) / alarm threshold crossed |
| `UpdateState` | Firmware-update progress |
| `LSPdatetime` | Device clock tick (every second) |

## Test with Insomnia

Before wiring subscriptions into your app, verify them interactively. The video below shows how to open the connection, register an event, and receive WebSocket frames in [Insomnia](https://insomnia.rest/).

## Reliability and Reconnect

The device may close the connection on network interruption or firmware restart, and no subscription state is preserved across connections. On a close event, wait, reconnect, and re-register every subscription.

## Troubleshooting

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Troubleshooting:** symptom, likely cause, and fix.</p>

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connection refused | Wrong IP / not reachable | Ping the device; check firewall |
| Resets after first registration | Register frames sent too fast | ≥ 200 ms between `register` messages |
| Closes immediately (error 1002) | `permessage-deflate` not negotiated | Use a library that negotiates it, or enable compression |
| "Event not found" | Wrong name (case-sensitive) or absent on this firmware | Check the exact name; confirm firmware |
| No events after registration | Value hasn't changed; events are change-driven | Expected; the initial value is still sent on registration |
| Stale app state at startup | Dispatch filter only accepts `type == "event"` | Also dispatch `type == "register"` with `status == 0` |
| Frequent drops | Read timeout too short | Set read timeout ≥ 300 s; events can be infrequent |

Test subscriptions from a plain browser (Chrome/Edge) or from Insomnia/Postman before wiring them into your app. Wireshark on the sensor interface shows the raw WebSocket traffic.

# Contamination Indication

Contamination indication monitors the sensor's optics cover for dirt that
could reduce measurement quality. It evaluates contamination by sector so
maintenance can target the affected area and be scheduled before the optics
become too dirty. picoScan100 evaluates seven sectors; its SOPASair sector
display shows where contamination is accumulating, with overall states of
**Clean**, **Minor**, **Heavy**, and **Blocked**.

Configure the sensitivity, response time, warning threshold, and active
sectors for the installation. The device can expose the result through its
GUI and REST API; depending on configuration, it can also be monitored
through CoLa or mapped to digital outputs. The warning and error behavior,
and whether blocked sectors count as errors, are configurable. Use the
indication as a maintenance signal and inspect and clean the optics according
to the product documentation.

All contamination settings and results are available through the REST API.
The endpoints are listed under **Contamination Indication** in the
[LRS4000 REST API](../LRS4000/rest-api-openapi.md),
[multiScan100 REST API](../multiScan100/rest-api-openapi.md),
[multiScan200 REST API](../multiScan200/rest-api-openapi.md), and
[picoScan100 REST API](../picoScan100/rest-api-openapi.md) references.

Writes require the Authorized Client user level and challenge-response
authentication. Persist configuration changes with `WriteEeprom`; otherwise,
they may be lost after a power cycle.

picoScan100 CoLa clients can read configuration and sector data and subscribe
to event-driven contamination updates. See the
[picoScan100 CoLa Telegram Listing](../picoScan100/cola-telegram-listing.md).
For the interface walkthrough, see
[Contamination Indication in SOPASair](../picoScan100/graphical-user-interface.md#contamination-indication).

# Field Evaluation

The sensor evaluates detection zones on the device. Field evaluation checks whether scan points enter a configured polygon and reports a `FREE` or `INFRINGED` result. The result can drive a digital output and can be read through REST or CoLa where the product exposes those interfaces.

*picoScan100: How to draw fields and detect objects?*

## Configure an Evaluation

Create evaluation groups in SOPASair, or restore them from a [configuration file](../configuration/configuration-backup-and-restore.md). The REST API and CoLa can then change existing evaluations or, on the picoScan100, build complete evaluations from scratch (see [Configure Over The API](#configure-over-the-api)). Call `WriteEeprom` after changes to store them permanently.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Configure an Evaluation:** REST resource, purpose, and devices.</p>

| REST resource | Purpose | Devices |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SetFieldEvaluationContour` | Writes the polygon of an evaluation | LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan100 |
| `GetFieldEvaluationContour` | Reads the polygon of an evaluation | LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan100 |
| `SetFieldEvaluationConfiguration` / `GetFieldEvaluationConfiguration` | Writes or reads evaluation parameters | multiScan200 |
| `EvaluationGroupType` | Selects field evaluation or perpendicular-distance mode | LRS4000, picoScan100 |
| `PortConfiguration` | Configures I/O ports, including outputs used by evaluations | LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan100 |

## Activate and Monitor a Group

A group can be active continuously (`ALWAYS`), controlled by inputs (`INPUTS`), or controlled by a telegram (`TELEGRAM`). `ActivateEvaluationGroup` only affects groups configured with `TELEGRAM`; it cannot switch an `ALWAYS` group.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Activate and Monitor a Group:** REST resource and purpose.</p>

| REST resource | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `ActivateEvaluationGroup` | Activates or deactivates a `TELEGRAM`-controlled group |
| `FieldEvaluationGroupState` | Group state: not configured, active, or inactive |
| `FieldEvaluationResult` | Current result: `FREE`, `INFRINGED`, or a transitional state; also available as a [WebSocket event](../data-streaming/websocket-events.md) |

A typical application creates the groups once, persists the configuration, and at runtime reads the group state and result, updates contours when necessary, and switches telegram-controlled groups.

For full payloads, see the [LRS4000](../LRS4000/rest-api-openapi.md), [multiScan100](../multiScan100/rest-api-openapi.md), [multiScan200](../multiScan200/rest-api-openapi.md), and [picoScan100](../picoScan100/rest-api-openapi.md) REST API references and the device-specific CoLa telegram listings.

## Configure over the API

On the picoScan100, REST and CoLa expose every variable needed to create, change, and delete a field evaluation without SOPASair. The following workflow applies to picoScan150 with firmware V2.3.3. Some of these variables, such as `Eval001`–`Eval048` and `EvaluationGroupMapping`, are not listed in the published OpenAPI file, but can be read and written as REST variables (`GET` / `POST /api/<Variable>`).

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Configure over the API:** variable or method and purpose.</p>

| Variable or method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Eval001`–`Eval048` | Detection parameters of one evaluation slot: mode, minimum object size, timing, and the referenced volume (`VolumeList`) |
| `SetFieldEvaluationContour` / `GetFieldEvaluationContour` | Writes or reads the polygon of an evaluation |
| `EvaluationGroupMapping` | Groups evaluations and sets the activation type of each group |
| `PortConfiguration` | Assigns an evaluation result to a digital output |
| `ActivateEvaluationGroup` | Switches a `TELEGRAM` group on or off; needs no login |
| `FieldEvaluationGroupState` / `FieldEvaluationResult` | Read-only group state and evaluation result |
| `WriteEeprom` (REST) / `mEEwriteall` (CoLa) | Stores the configuration permanently |

To create an evaluation, log in as **Authorized client** or **Service** and write the variables in this order:

1. Write `EvalNNN` with the detection mode, the minimum object size, and `VolumeList = [NNN]`.
2. Write the polygon with `SetFieldEvaluationContour`. It returns error `1` (invalid evaluation) if `VolumeList` of the slot is empty, so write the slot first.
3. Write `EvaluationGroupMapping`. The whole array is replaced on every write: read the current mapping first and include every group you want to keep.
4. Optional: write `PortConfiguration` to switch a digital output when the evaluation is infringed. Outputs refer to evaluations (sources `EG01`–`EG48`), not to groups, and the whole port array must be written.
5. Call `WriteEeprom`. The device re-initializes; wait about 1 s before reading the state.
6. For a `TELEGRAM` group, switch it on with `ActivateEvaluationGroup`.

To delete an evaluation, remove its group from `EvaluationGroupMapping`, clear `VolumeList` and the name of the slot, and call `WriteEeprom`. The group state returns to not configured.

The coordinates are in millimeters in the sensor coordinate system: `x` points forward (depth) and `y` to the side.

**Detection modes** (`EvaluationParamsCommon.Mode` of the evaluation slot):

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Configure over the API:** value, mode, and the field is infringed when.</p>

| Value | Mode | The field is infringed when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | Blanking | An object at least as large as the minimum object size is inside the field. This is the most common mode. |
| `1` | Reflector only | A highly reflective object such as a retroreflector is inside the field. |
| `2` | Contour | The scan deviates from the taught-in contour by more than the tolerance. Requires a valid [teach-in](#teach-in-over-the-api). |

**Activation types** (`Activation.Type` of a group):

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Configure over the API:** value, type, and behavior.</p>

| Value | Type | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | Deactivated | The group is never evaluated. |
| `1` | Always | The group is active as soon as it is stored. `ActivateEvaluationGroup` returns `false` for it and cannot switch it off. |
| `2` | Inputs | Digital inputs activate the group. |
| `3` | Telegram | The group starts in the state set by `InitialActivationStateTelegram` and is switched with `ActivateEvaluationGroup`. |

`FieldEvaluationGroupState` returns one value per group: `0` not configured, `1` active, `2` inactive. `FieldEvaluationResult` returns one state per evaluation: `0` not configured, `1` inactive, `2` free, `3` detecting infringed, `4` infringed, `5` detecting free.

For complete REST and CoLa payloads of every step, see the knowledge base article [picoScan150: Field Evaluation and Perpendicular Distance API Possibilities](https://support.sick.com/sick-knowledgebase/article/?code=KA-10798).

## Editing Field Polygons

Field polygons can be changed through the web GUI, configuration import, REST, CoLa, or the SDK. Select the method that fits whether the change is an interactive adjustment, a repeatable deployment, or an application-driven update.

### Web GUI Configuration

Open the Object Detection application in SOPASair to create and edit polygon points directly. This is the quickest method for commissioning and manual adjustments. The field editor also supports teach-in.

![Field evaluation teach-in tile](../assets/picoScan100/img/application_field_eval_teach_in_tile_20260826_153331.png)
*Field evaluation teach-in tile in SOPASair.*

For bulk coordinate changes, open the Field settings dialog and select JSON in its footer toolbar. The editor switches from the coordinate table to a JSON text field. Paste the prepared polygon to replace all points at once:

```json
{
  "points": [
    { "x": -5, "y": 531 },
    { "x": 837, "y": 565 },
    { "x": 907, "y": -637 },
    { "x": 12, "y": -590 }
  ]
}
```

### Configuration File Import

Use the top-right SOPASair menu to download the complete configuration from a commissioned sensor. It includes field geometries and can be imported into another compatible device, making it suitable for repeatable commissioning and replacement devices. Keep a versioned, validated backup for each deployed configuration.

### Programmatic Updates

The REST API exposes `SetFieldEvaluationContour` to update a polygon. The evaluation must already exist. Use `GetFieldEvaluationContour` to confirm the stored geometry and persist the change with `WriteEeprom`. See [Configure An Evaluation](#configure-an-evaluation) and the [REST client example](https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_scan_rest_client/blob/public/examples/sick_scan_rest_client_object_detection_example.py).

CoLa provides the same `SetFieldEvaluationContour` function through its telegram interface. Use it when the integration already uses CoLa, such as a PLC or legacy client; see [CoLa](../configuration/cola-interface.md).

The `sick_perception_sdk` uses the REST interface and provides an application-level option for changing contours. See the [object-detection example](https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_perception_sdk/blob/main/examples/shared/object_detection.cpp).

## Distance-Dependent

The **Distance-dependent** parameter determines whether two detected objects are evaluated separately or merged into one object based on their axial separation. It works with the configured **Blanking** width to avoid triggering a field evaluation when separate small objects would otherwise appear as one large object.

*picoScan100: 2D Object Detection Parameter Distance-dependent.*

The video uses two objects: a foreground object approximately 60 mm wide, a background object approximately 250 mm wide, and about 450 mm of axial separation. The standard blanking width is 300 mm.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Example:** configuration, result, and explanation.</p>

| Configuration | Result | Explanation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distance-dependent off | Field infringed | Both objects merge into one contiguous object wider than 300 mm. |
| Distance-dependent on; threshold 300 mm | Field not infringed | The objects are at least 300 mm apart and are evaluated separately; neither is wider than 300 mm. |
| Distance-dependent on; threshold 500 mm | Field infringed | The objects are less than 500 mm apart, so they merge and exceed the blanking width. |

Set the separation threshold to the distance at which nearby objects should be merged for your application. See [Configure An Evaluation](#configure-an-evaluation) for the evaluation and polygon.

## Teach In

Teach-in captures the current environment and uses the measured contour as a field for object detection. Use it during commissioning when the surrounding geometry should define the detection field instead of drawing a polygon manually.

### Web GUI Teach In

Open the **Object Detection** application in SOPASair and select **Teach-in** in the field configuration. Set the distances in front of and behind the object, choose the minimum teach-in time, and click **Start**. Stop the teach-in when the environment has been captured, then save the field evaluation configuration.

*Teach-in configuration in SOPASair.*

The configured distances take effect during the next teach-in. Keep the intended environment stable while the contour is captured.

Teach-in uses the same evaluation group and output mechanism as a manually configured field. After the contour has been captured, monitor the evaluation result through the configured output, REST, CoLa, or WebSocket events.

### Teach in over the API

A teach-in evaluation is an evaluation slot with mode `2` (contour). The polygon written with `SetFieldEvaluationContour` is not the detection field: it is the region of interest in which teach-in learns the reference contour. `GetFieldEvaluationContour` therefore returns this region, not the learned contour.

Teach-in is global; it is not bound to an evaluation slot. Set the parameters, then start and stop the teach-in:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Teach in over the API:** variable or method and purpose.</p>

| Variable or method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `TeachInToleranceFront` / `TeachInToleranceBack` | Tolerance in front of and behind the taught contour, in mm (default 250) |
| `TeachInMinimumTimeMs` | Minimum teach-in time, 100 to 60000 ms (default 250) |
| `TeachInActivationInput` | Digital input that starts the teach-in; `0` = software only |
| `StartTeachIn` / `StopTeachIn` | Starts and stops the teach-in |
| `TeachInActive` | `1` while the teach-in runs |
| `TeachInContourValid` | `1` after a teach-in produced a valid contour |

Keep the scene stable for at least the minimum teach-in time, stop the teach-in, check `TeachInContourValid`, and call `WriteEeprom`. To change the field later, repeat the teach-in, for example with a larger tolerance; the region of interest stays the same.

## Ground Filter (multiScan100)

The ground filter uses upper and lower ground thresholds to reduce false
field-evaluation triggers caused by the ground. When configured correctly, it
retains small objects such as forklift tines and can be used indoors and
outdoors. The filter also affects perpendicular-distance evaluations. See
[Ground Filter](../data-streaming/filter-details.md#ground-filter) for
availability and API settings.

*multiScan1xx: Ground-filter behavior in a field application.*

## Related Articles

- [picoScan150: Field Evaluation and Perpendicular Distance API Possibilities](https://support.sick.com/sick-knowledgebase/article/?code=KA-10798)

# Perpendicular Distance Measurement

Perpendicular distance evaluation measures object distances relative to a
reference line in the scan plane. Define a field and reference line in the
application; the sensor evaluates the points in that field and
reports the minimum and maximum perpendicular distances and the positions of
the corresponding measuring points.

*multiScan1xx: Perpendicular distance application demonstration.*

## Configure a Measurement

1. Open **Application > Perpendicular distance measurement** in SOPASair and
   add an evaluation group.
2. Draw the zone in which objects should be measured.
3. Set **Max. blanking size** and **Detection time** under Object detection to
   balance measurement stability and response time for the target.
4. Save the configuration to the device.
5. Check the live minimum and maximum distances and their measuring-point
   coordinates in the result list.

The evaluation runs on the sensor, so the host receives measurement results
without having to detect objects from the raw scan itself. See the
[SOPASair configuration walkthrough](../picoScan100/graphical-user-interface.md#perpendicular-distance-measurement)
for the interface details.

## Read Results

The REST endpoint `GET /api/perpendicularDistanceResult` returns a timestamp
and an `evaluations` array. Each result contains an evaluation ID, minimum and
maximum distance, and the 3D position of each corresponding measuring point.
The `evaluations` array is empty when no object is measured. The result is read-only; see the [picoScan100 REST API reference](../picoScan100/rest-api-openapi.md).

CoLa clients can poll `sRN perpendicularDistanceResult` for the current
measurement or subscribe with `sEN perpendicularDistanceResult` for event
updates. The telegram reports the shortest and furthest measuring point in
the range relative to the reference plane. See the
[picoScan100 CoLa Telegram Listing](../picoScan100/cola-telegram-listing.md).

## Configure over the API (picoScan100)

REST and CoLa expose every variable needed to create, change, and delete a
perpendicular distance evaluation without SOPASair. The following workflow
applies to picoScan150 with firmware V2.3.3. Some of these variables are
not listed in the published OpenAPI file, but can be read and written as REST
variables (`GET` / `POST /api/<Variable>`).

A perpendicular distance evaluation has two parts, as in SOPASair:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Configure over the API (picoScan100):** part, variables, and content.</p>

| Part | Variables | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Object detection | `EvalNNN`, `VolumeNNN` | Detection parameters (blanking mode, minimum object size, detection time) and the field in which objects are measured |
| Reference line | `perpDistNNN` | Normal vector of the line in the scan plane and its signed distance from the sensor, in mm |

To create an evaluation, log in as **Authorized client** or **Service** and
write the variables in this order, using the same slot number `NNN`
throughout:

1. Set the slot to perpendicular distance: write `EvaluationGroupType` with
   all 48 values and `1` at the slot position (`0` = field evaluation).
2. Write `EvalNNN` with `VolumeList = [NNN]`.
3. Write the field polygon directly to `VolumeNNN`. Do not use
   `SetFieldEvaluationContour` here: it returns success for perpendicular
   distance slots but is not reliable for them.
4. Write the reference line to `perpDistNNN`. The normal vector sets the
   orientation, for example `(1, 0, 0)` for a line across the forward
   direction, and the distance sets its position. Because the picoScan100 is a
   2D sensor, the `z` component is always `0`. The no-data mode sets the
   output when no object is measured: `0` zero, `1` hold the last value, or
   `2` a user-defined substitution distance.
5. Add the group to `EvaluationGroupMapping` with `EvalIds = [NNN]`. The whole
   array is replaced on every write, so include every group you want to keep.
6. Call `WriteEeprom` and wait about 1 s before reading the result.

Keep in mind:

- Perpendicular distance groups need their own slots; they cannot share a
  slot with a field evaluation group.
- If the field is missing (empty `VolumeList` or empty `VolumeNNN`) or the
  group references no evaluation, the device reports a recoverable error
  (`DeviceStatus` = `7` instead of `3`) and the result stays empty.
- Perpendicular distance results are not assigned to digital outputs; read
  them from `perpendicularDistanceResult`.
- Group activation (`ALWAYS`, `INPUTS`, `TELEGRAM`) and `ActivateEvaluationGroup`
  work as for [field evaluation](./field-evaluation.md#configure-over-the-api).

To delete the evaluation, remove the group from `EvaluationGroupMapping`,
clear `EvalNNN`, `VolumeNNN`, and `perpDistNNN`, set the slot in
`EvaluationGroupType` back to `0`, and call `WriteEeprom`.

For complete REST and CoLa payloads of every step, see the knowledge base
article
[picoScan150: Field Evaluation and Perpendicular Distance API Possibilities](https://support.sick.com/sick-knowledgebase/article/?code=KA-10798).

For output and evaluation-group concepts shared with field evaluation, see
[Field Evaluation](./field-evaluation.md).

# LRS4000

![LRS4000 2D LiDAR sensor](../assets/LRS4000/img/product-photo.png)
<p class="caption product-image-caption">LRS4000 2D LiDAR sensor.</p>

The LRS4000 is a long-range 2D LiDAR sensor for demanding outdoor
applications. This developer section covers the LRS4581R. Use the Product ID
(PID) to find the exact product variant on [sick.com](https://www.sick.com/):
enter the part number (P/N) and optional serial number (S/N), for example
`1134610/25250710`. A complete [pid.sick.com](https://pid.sick.com/) URL is
also accepted.
