# CoLa Telegram Listing

This reference lists the CoLa telegrams supported by the LRS4000. Use the
command details to build or troubleshoot PLC and other low-level
integrations without guessing the telegram structure. For connection
setup, framing, and log in, see
[CoLa Interface](../configuration/cola-interface.md).

Entries follow the telegram order in the LRS4000 operating instructions. Detailed entries list request and response structures, examples, variable types, lengths, and CoLa A and CoLa B values where applicable.

**Telegram structure: "Command type" "Command"**

| Telegram part                              | Description                                 | Variable                          | Length                      | Additional details                                                             | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                     | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                     |     |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| Lists the different parts of the telegram. | Describes the corresponding telegram parts. | Defines the type of the variable. | Defines the length in byte. | Gives further information regarding the values in CoLa A/ CoLa B if necessary. | Defines the value of the telegram part in CoLa A (ASCII). | Defines the value of the telegram part in CoLa B (Binary). |     |

Commands are colored blue, parameters orange for further differentiation.

**Example: "Command type" "Command"**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                                                                                                                                      |     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<"Start of text">"Command type value (ASCII)""space""Command value (ASCII)""space""Parameter value (ASCII)""space""Parameter value (ASCII)"<"End of text">`        |     |
| CoLa A   | Copy example with framing (ASCII)                                                                                                                                                                            |     |
| CoLa A   | Copy example without framing (ASCII)                                                                                                                                                                         |     |
| CoLa A   | Copy example with framing (Hex)                                                                                                                                                                              |     |
| CoLa B   | `"Start of text and given length" "Command type value (Binary)""space""Command value (Binary)""space""Parameter value (Binary)""Parameter value (Binary)""Calculated checksum"` |     |
| CoLa B   | Copy example without framing (Binary)                                                                                                                                                                        |     |

**Telegram structure: "Command type" "Command" (Answer)**

| Telegram part                              | Description                                 | Variable                          | Length                      | Additional details                                                             | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                     | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                     |     |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| Lists the different parts of the telegram. | Describes the corresponding telegram parts. | Defines the type of the variable. | Defines the length in byte. | Gives further information regarding the values in CoLa A/ CoLa B if necessary. | Defines the value of the telegram part in CoLa A (ASCII). | Defines the value of the telegram part in CoLa B (Binary). |     |

## General

### Log In [sMN SetAccessMode]

A log in to the device is necessary to change parameters. In most cases, the user level 'Authorized client' is needed. Changed parameters are reset to the previous state via a reboot unless they are saved. To save parameter changes, send "sMN mEEwriteall" before logging out.

**Telegram structure: sMN SetAccessMode**

| Telegram part | Description                            | Variable | Length | Additional details                             | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                           | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                   |     |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| Command type  | Method                                 | String   | 3      |                                                | `sMN`                              | `73 4D 4E`                                  |     |
| Command       | User level                             | String   | 13     |                                                | `SetAccessMode`                    | `53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65`    |     |
| User level    | Select user level                      | Int_8    | 1      | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `2<br>3<br>4`                      | `02<br>03<br>04`                            |     |
| Password      | Hash value for the selected user level | Uint_32  | 4      | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `B21ACE26<br>F4724744<br>81BE23AA` | `B2 1A CE 26<br>F4 72 47 44<br>81 BE 23 AA` |     |

**Example: sMN SetAccessMode - Log in as “Authorized client” with password “F4724744”**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                                                        |     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sMN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}3{SPC}F4724744<ETX>`                                  |     |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sMN SetAccessMode 3 F4724744<ETX>`                                              |     |
| CoLa A   | `sMN SetAccessMode 3 F4724744`                                                                    |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 30 33 20 46 34 37 32 34 37 34 34 03`    |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 17 73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 03 F4 72 47 44 B3` |     |
| CoLa B   | `73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 03 F4 72 47 44`                            |     |

**Telegram structure: sAN SetAccessMode**

| Telegram part     | Description   | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                        | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                |     |
| ----------------- | ------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| Command type      | Answer        | String   | 3      |                    | `sAN`           | `73 41 4E`                               |     |
| Command           | User level    | String   | 13     |                    | `SetAccessMode` | `53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65` |     |
| Change user level | Changed level | Bool_1   | 1      | Error:<br>Success: | `0<br>1`        | `00<br>01`                               |     |

**Example: sAN SetAccessMode**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                                            |     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sAN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}1<ETX>`                                   |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 31 03`                      |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 13 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 01 38` |     |

### Read for Frequency and Angular Resolution [sRN LMPscancfg]

Read the scanning frequency, angular resolution and aperture angle of the device. Values show the information of the values before any filters are applied. Therefore aperture angle is always showing the maximum, scanning frequency and angular resolution may also be static depending on device family.

**Telegram structure: sRN LMPscancfg**

| Telegram part | Description                                   | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                     | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                       |     |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| Command type  | Read                                          | String   | 3      |                    | `sRN`        | `73 52 4E`                      |     |
| Command       | Info of scan frequency and angular resolution | String   | 10     |                    | `LMPscancfg` | `4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67` |     |

**Example: sRN LMPscancfg**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                             |     |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sRN{SPC}LMPscancfg<ETX>`                             |     |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sRN LMPscancfg<ETX>`                                 |     |
| CoLa A   | `sRN LMPscancfg`                                                       |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 03`                      |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0E 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 63` |     |
| CoLa B   | `73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67`                            |     |

**Telegram structure: sRA LMPscancfg**

| Telegram part      | Description                                   | Variable | Length | Additional details                                        | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                              | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                       |     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| Command type       | Answer                                        | String   | 3      |                                                           | `sRA`                 | `73 52 41`                      |     |
| Command            | Info of scan frequency and angular resolution | String   | 10     |                                                           | `LMPscancfg`          | `4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67` |     |
| Scan frequency     | [1/100 Hz]                                    | Uint_32  | 4      | 15 Hz ... 50 Hz:<br>(depends on Dynamic Sensing Profile ) | `5DCh ... 1388h`      | `05 DC ... 13 88`               |     |
| Reserved           | -                                             | Int_16   | 2      | Always:                                                   | `1`                   | `00 01`                         |     |
| Angular resolution | [1/10000°]                                    | Uint_32  | 4      | 0.1° ... 1°:<br>(depends on Dynamic Sensing Profile )     | `3E8h … 2710h`        | `03 E8 ... 27 10`               |     |
| Start angle        | [1/10000°]                                    | Int_32   | 4      | -48° ... 228°                                             | `FFF8AD00h … 22CA40h` | `FF F8 AD 00h … 00 22 CA 40h`   |     |
| Stop angle         | [1/10000°]                                    | Int_32   | 4      | -48° ... 228°                                             | `FFF8AD00h … 22CA40h` | `FF F8 AD 00h … 00 22 CA 40h`   |     |

**Example: sRA LMPscancfg - 30 Hz scan frequency, 0.1° angular resolution, -48° start angle, +138° stop angle**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                                                                                      |     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sRA{SPC}LMPscancfg{SPC}BB8{SPC}1{SPC}3E8{SPC}FFEAF160{SPC}150EA0<ETX>`                                        |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 52 41 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 20 42 42 38 20 31 20 33 45 38 20 46 46 45 41 46 31 36 30 20 31 35 30 45 41 30 03` |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 21 73 52 41 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 20 00 00 0B B8 00 01 00 00 03 E8 FF EA F1 60 00 15 0E A0 2A` |     |

### Activate Standby Mode [sMN LMCstandby]

Shut off the laser in order to extend the lifetime of laser diode and reduce motor speed to 25 Hz.

**Telegram structure: sMN LMCstandby**

| Telegram part | Description           | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                     | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                       |     |
| ------------- | --------------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| Command type  | Method                | String   | 3      |                    | `sMN`        | `73 4D 4E`                      |     |
| Command       | Set device to standby | String   | 10     |                    | `LMCstandby` | `4C 4D 43 73 74 61 6E 64 62 79` |     |

**Example: sMN LMCstandby**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                             |     |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |

| CoLa A   | `sMN LMCstandby`                                                       |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 4D 4E 20 4C 4D 43 73 74 61 6E 64 62 79 03`                      |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0E 73 4D 4E 20 4C 4D 43 73 74 61 6E 64 62 79 65` |     |
| CoLa B   | `73 4D 4E 20 4C 4D 43 73 74 61 6E 64 62 79`                            |     |

### Poll One Telegram [sRN LMDscandata]

Asking the device for the measurement values of the last valid scan. The device will respond, even if currently no measurement data is created (e.g. due to standby or log in).

Data is transmitted only via LMDscandata when LMDscandata is selected as data output format.

During the boot up phase of the device, there will be no data telegram or answer from the device.

> **Important:** The `sRN LMDscandata` and `sEN LMDscandata` telegrams must not be sent via CoLa A. Use CoLa B for these data telegrams; sending them over CoLa A can result in data loss.

**Telegram structure: sRN LMDscandata**

| Telegram part | Description       | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                      | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                          |     |
| ------------- | ----------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| Command type  | Read              | String   | 3      |                    | `sRN`         | `73 52 4E`                         |     |
| Command       | Only one telegram | String   | 11     |                    | `LMDscandata` | `4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61` |     |

**Example: sRN LMDscandata**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                                |     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sRN{SPC}LMDscandata<ETX>`                               |     |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sRN LMDscandata<ETX>`                                   |     |
| CoLa A   | `sRN LMDscandata`                                                         |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 03`                      |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0F 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 05` |     |
| CoLa B   | `73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61`                            |     |

**Telegram structure: sRA LMDscandata**

The response uses the scan-data structure documented for `sRA/sSN LMDscandata` below. The `sEA LMDscandata` telegram is the subscription acknowledgement, not the scan-data payload.

### Send Data Permanently [sEN LMDscandata]

Start or stop continuous transmission of measurement data. Data is transmitted as configured as soon as measurement data is generated by the device. No data is generated when there is an active log in, the laser is shut off (e.g. in Standby mode), the motor is stopped, the data format is Compact, or the device is in certain error modes (e.g. Device not ready).

Data is transmitted only via LMDscandata when LMDscandata is selected as data output format.

During the boot up phase of the device, there will be no data telegram or answer from the device.

**Telegram structure: sEN LMDscandata**

| Telegram part | Description   | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                      | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                          |     |
| ------------- | ------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| Command type  | Event         | String   | 3      |                    | `sEN`         | `73 45 4E`                         |     |
| Command       | Data telegram | String   | 11     |                    | `LMDscandata` | `4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61` |     |
| Measurement   | Start/stop    | Enum_8   | 1      | Stop:<br>Start:    | `0<br>1`      | `00<br>01`                         |     |

**Example: sEN LMDscandata**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                                      |     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sEN{SPC}LMDscandata{SPC}1<ETX>`                               |     |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sEN LMDscandata 1<ETX>`                                       |     |
| CoLa A   | `sEN LMDscandata 1`                                                             |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 31 03`                      |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 11 73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 01 33` |     |
| CoLa B   | `73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 01`                            |     |

**Telegram structure: sEA LMDscandata**

| Telegram part | Description   | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                      | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                          |     |

| Measurement   | Start/stop    | Enum_8   | 1      | Stop:<br>Start:    | `0<br>1`      | `00<br>01`                         |     |

LMDscandata - reserved values

Valid distance measurement values are values starting from 16d upwards; everything below has the following meaning:

| DIST     | RSSI   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                     |     |
| -------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| 0d       | 0d     | Invalid measurement value; caused by very low remission (extremely dark object), object distance not within measurement range (too close or too far away) or selected filter settings at device |     |
| 1d - 15d | 0d     | Reserved, currently not in use                                                                                                                                                                  |     |
| ≥16d     | >0h | Valid measurement values                                                                                                                                                                        |     |
| ≥16d     | 254d   | Reflector detected                                                                                                                                                                              |     |
| ≥16d     | 255d   | Reserved                                                                                                                                                                                        |     |

Higher measurement values will be given out with a zero, that means no measurement value detected.

### Set Time Stamp [sMN LSPsetdatetime]

The data format in the telegram is: +2009{SPC}+7{SPC}+22{SPC}+12{SPC}+0{SPC}+0{SPC}+0.The numbers represent year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond.

If plus is used up-front the data it is interpreted as an integer decimal number, without the plus it's the scanner reads the data as hex format.

The answer is always in ASCII format.

Does only work if NTP- respectively PTP-Client is not active.

There is no real time clock inside the device. When the scanner is switched off and after a reboot, the time has to be set again. Therefore, it is recommended to use a NTP or a PTP setting.

**Telegram structure: sMN LSPsetdatetime**

| Telegram part | Description    | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                                | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                   |     |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| Command type  | Method         | String   | 3      |                    | `sMN`                                   | `73 4D 4E`                                  |     |
| Command       | Set time stamp | String   | 14     |                    | `LSPsetdatetime`                        | `4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65` |     |
| Year          |                | Uint_16  | 2      |                    | `+1970d … +2099d (07B2h … 0833h)`       | `07 B2 … 08 33`                             |     |
| Month         |                | Uint_8   | 1      |                    | `+1d … +12d(01h … 0Ch)`                 | `01 … 0C`                                   |     |
| Day           |                | Uint_8   | 1      |                    | `+1d … +31d(01h … 1Fh)`                 | `00 … 1F`                                   |     |
| Hour          |                | Uint_8   | 1      |                    | `+0d … +23d(00h … 17h)`                 | `00 … 17`                                   |     |
| Minute        |                | Uint_8   | 1      |                    | `+0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh)`                 | `00 … 3B`                                   |     |
| Second        |                | Uint_8   | 1      |                    | `+0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh)`                 | `00 … 3B`                                   |     |
| Microsecond   |                | Uint_32  | 4      |                    | `+0d … +999999d(00000000h … 000F423Fh)` | `00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F`                 |     |

## Filters

### Set Particle Filter [sWN LFPparticle]

Filter out disturbances in the meausurement data caused by particles such as dust, snow flakes or similar .

**Telegram structure: sWN LFPparticle**

| Telegram part | Description              | Variable | Length | Additional details   | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                       | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                          |     |
| ------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ------ | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| Command type  | Write                    | String   | 3      |                      | `sWN`          | `73 57 4E`                         |     |
| Command       | Set particle filter      | String   | 11     |                      | `LFPparticle`  | `4C 46 50 70 61 72 74 69 63 6C 65` |     |
| Status code   | Code number              | Bool_1   | 1      | Inactive:<br>Active: | `0<br>1`       | `00<br>01`                         |     |
| Threshold1)   | Particle threshold in mm | Uint_16  | 2      | (must be taken)      | `+500d (1F4h)` | `01 F4`                            |     |

Never change the threshold here, it is taken by the device to handle the particles.

**Example: sWN LFPparticle**

| CoLa B   | `73 57 4E 20 4C 46 50 70 61 72 74 69 63 6C 65 20 01 01 F4`                            |     |

### Read State of the Inputs [sRN LIDinputstate]

Use sEN LIDinputstate 1 to receive a telegram each time an input signal (e.g. by trigger) changes.

**Telegram structure: sRN LIDinputstate**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                        | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                |     |
| ------------- | ----------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| Command type  | Read        | String   | 3      |                    | `sRN`           | `73 52 4E`                               |     |
| Command       | Input state | String   | 14     |                    | `LIDinputstate` | `4C 49 44 69 6E 70 75 74 73 74 61 74 65` |     |

**Example: sRN LIDinputstate**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                                      |     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sRN{SPC}LIDinputstate<ETX>`                                   |     |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sRN LIDinputstate<ETX>`                                       |     |
| CoLa A   | `sRN LIDinputstate`                                                             |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 52 4E 20 4C 49 44 69 6E 70 75 74 73 74 61 74 65 03`                      |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 11 73 52 4E 20 4C 49 44 69 6E 70 75 74 73 74 61 74 65 0F` |     |
| CoLa B   | `73 52 4E 20 4C 49 44 69 6E 70 75 74 73 74 61 74 65`                            |     |

**Telegram structure: sRA LIDinputstate**

| Command                                                                     | Output state                                                                        | String   | 14     |                                           | `LIDinputstate`   | `4C 49 44 69 6E 70 75 74 73 74 61 74 65` |     |
| Status code                                                                 | Version number                                                                      | Uint_16  | 2      |                                           | `0h … FFFFh`      | `00 00 … FF FF`                          |     |

| State of the inputs 1 … n                                                   | Amount of inputs (n) depending of device family                                     | Enum_8   | 1      | Not active:<br>Active:<br>Input not used: | `0<br>1<br>2`     | `00<br>01<br>02`                         |     |

### Set Output State [sMN mDOSetOutput]

Set a specific output to high or low via software command.

Output source needs to be set to "SOPAS command" and the port configured as Output (in case of I/O).

**Telegram structure: sMN mDOSetOutput**

| Telegram part | Description      | Variable | Length | Additional details      | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                         | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                             |     |
| ------------- | ---------------- | -------- | ------ | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| Command type  | Method           | String   | 3      |                         | `sMN`            | `73 4D 4E`                            |     |
| Command       | Set output state | String   | 12     |                         | `mDOSetOutput`   | `6D 44 4F 53 65 74 4F 75 74 70 75 74` |     |
| Output number |                  | Uint_8   | 1      | Depends on system plug: | `1 … 3<br>1 … 6` | `01 … 03<br>01 … 06`                  |     |
| Output state  |                  | Enum_8   | 1      | Not active:<br>Active:  | `0<br>1`         | `00<br>01`                            |     |

**Example: sMN mDOSetOutput**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                                            |     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sMN{SPC}mDOSetOutput{SPC}1{SPC}1<ETX>`                              |     |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sMN mDOSetOutput 1 1<ETX>`                                          |     |
| CoLa A   | `sMN mDOSetOutput 1 1`                                                                |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 4D 4E 20 6D 44 4F 53 65 74 4F 75 74 70 75 74 20 31 20 31 03`                   |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 13 73 4D 4E 20 6D 44 4F 53 65 74 4F 75 74 70 75 74 20 01 01 6B` |     |
| CoLa B   | `73 4D 4E 20 6D 44 4F 53 65 74 4F 75 74 70 75 74 20 01 01`                            |     |

| CoLa B   | `73 52 4E 20 53 65 72 69 61 6C 4E 75 6D 62 65 72`                            |     |

### Read Operating Hours [sRN ODoprh]

Views the total number of operating hours during the lifetime of the device.

**Telegram structure: sRN ODoprh**

| Telegram part | Description          | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                 | Values CoLa B (Binary)                           |     |
| ------------- | -------------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| Command type  | Read                 | String   | 3      |                    | `sRN`    | `73 52 4E`          |     |
| Command       | Read operating hours | String   | 6      |                    | `ODoprh` | `4F 44 6F 70 72 68` |     |

**Example: sRN ODoprh**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                 |     |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sRN{SPC}ODoprh<ETX>`                     |     |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sRN ODoprh<ETX>`                         |     |
| CoLa A   | `sRN ODoprh`                                               |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 52 4E 20 4F 44 6F 70 72 68 03`                      |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0A 73 52 4E 20 4F 44 6F 70 72 68 41` |     |
| CoLa B   | `73 52 4E 20 4F 44 6F 70 72 68`                            |     |

**Telegram structure: sRA ODoprh**

| Telegram part | Description               | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                         | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                  |     |
| ------------- | ------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| Command type  | Answer                    | String   | 3      |                    | `sRA`            | `73 52 41`                 |     |
| Command       | Read operating hours      | String   | 6      |                    | `ODoprh`         | `4F 44 6F 70 72 68`        |     |
| Value         | Operating hours in 1/10 h | Uint_32  | 4      |                    | `0h … FFFFFFFFh` | `00 00 00 00 …FF FF FF FF` |     |

**Example: sRA ODoprh**

| Protocol | Example                                                                                                |     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- |
| CoLa A   | `<STX>sRA{SPC}ODoprh{SPC}1B50B<ETX>`                          |     |
| CoLa A   | `02 73 52 41 20 4F 44 6F 70 72 68 20 31 42 35 30 42 03`                   |     |
| CoLa B   | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0F 73 52 41 20 4F 44 6F 70 72 68 20 00 01 B5 0B D1` |     |

Calculation of the value: 1B50B (hex) 111883 (dez) × 1/10 h = 11188.3 h

### Read for Motor Synchronization [sRN MotorSyncStatus]

**Access:** Authorized client user level is required.

**Request: `sRN MotorSyncStatus`**

| Telegram part / meaning | Variable type | Length (bytes) | Values, ranges, and notes |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Read | String | 3 | CoLa A: sRN |
| Read motor synchronization status | String | 15 | CoLa A: MotorSyncStatus |

**Response: `sRA MotorSyncStatus`**

| Telegram part / meaning | Variable type | Length (bytes) | Values, ranges, and notes |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Answer | String | 3 | CoLa A: sRA |
| Read motor synchronization status | String | 15 | CoLa A: MotorSyncStatus |
| Synchronization status | Enum_8 | 1 | Not synchronized:: 0<br>Only Time synchronized:: 1<br>Synchronized:: 2 |

**Request example**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN MotorSyncStatus<ETX>` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 13 73 52 4E 20 4D 6F 74 6F 72 53 79 6E 63 53 74 61 74 75 73 17` |

**Response example**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |

### Change CoLa TCP Timeout [sWN EtherColaTransmitTimeout]

**Access:** Authorized client user level is required.

| Telegram part / meaning | Variable type | Length (bytes) | Values, ranges, and notes |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Write | String | 3 | CoLa A: sWN |
| Adjust CoLa TCP Acknowledge timeout time | String | 24 | CoLa A: EtherColaTransmitTimeout |
| New timeout time in ms | Uint_16 | 2 | Default: 15000<br>CoLa A: +250d ... +15000d |

| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Answer | String | 3 | CoLa A: sWA |
| Adjust CoLa TCP Acknowledge timeout time | String | 24 | CoLa A: EtherColaTransmitTimeout |

The timeout change takes effect after the sensor is restarted.

### Set Activation of Evaluation Group [sMN ActivateEvaluationGroup]

**Telegram structure: sMN ActivateEvaluationGroup**

| Amount of evaluation groups to activate/ deactivate | Array                                     | Uint_16  | 2      | Each array element contains two parameters:Evaluation group numberDeactivation / activation of evaluation group | `1d ... 48d (1 ... 30h)`  | `00 01 … 00 30`                                                        |     |

| Activate/ deactivate evaluation group               | Activate / deactivate evaluation group 2  | Bool_1   | 1      | Deactivate:<br>Activate:                                                                                        | `0<br>1`                  | `00<br>01`                                                             |     |

| Activate/ deactivate evaluation group               | Activate / deactivate evaluation group 48 | Bool_1   | 1      | Deactivate:<br>Activate:                                                                                        | `0<br>1`                  | `00<br>01`                                                             |     |

# Electrical Connection

The LRS4000 has separate M12 connectors for power, Ethernet, and digital
I/O/encoder signals. The tables below reproduce the assignments from LRS4000
operating instructions 8026337/1VNC, pages 34–35.

## PWR

This connection uses a male, 5-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

![PWR connector face with numbered pins](../assets/electrical-symbols/lrs4000-pwr.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">PWR connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**PWR** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `Vs` | Supply, +10 V DC to +30 V DC |
| 2 | — | Reserved; do not connect |
| 3 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 4 | `IN8/OUT8` | Configurable digital input 8 or output 8 |
| 5 | — | Reserved; do not connect |

## Ethernet

This connection uses a female, 4-pin, D-coded M12 connector.

![Ethernet connector face with numbered pins](../assets/electrical-symbols/lrs4000-ethernet.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">Ethernet connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Ethernet** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `TX+` | Transmit + |
| 2 | `RX+` | Receive + |
| 3 | `TX-` | Transmit − |
| 4 | `RX-` | Receive − |

Connect the D-coded Ethernet interface to an Ethernet port rather than to
general-purpose controller terminals.

## IOs and Encoder

This connection uses a female, 8-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

![I/O and encoder connector face with numbered pins](../assets/electrical-symbols/lrs4000-io.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">I/O and encoder connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**IOs and Encoder** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `IN1` | Encoder input 1 |
| 2 | `IN2` | Encoder input 2 |
| 3 | `IN3/OUT3` | Configurable digital input 3 or output 3 |
| 4 | `IN4/OUT4` | Configurable digital input 4 or output 4 |
| 5 | `IN5/OUT5` | Configurable digital input 5 or output 5 |
| 6 | `IN6/OUT6` | Configurable digital input 6 or output 6 |
| 7 | `GND INx/OUTx` | Common reference for all digital I/O |
| 8 | `IN7/OUT7` | Configurable digital input 7 or output 7 |

# Motor Synchronization

Motor synchronization coordinates measurement start angles across several
LRS4000 sensors. It can increase the effective scan frequency or resolution
of a combined system. The sensor shifts its measurement start angle between
−180° and +180°; set the phase for each device individually.

LRS4000 supports two synchronization methods.

## PTP Synchronization

Synchronize the LiDAR sensors over Ethernet to a central PTP master. The
sensors then share a system time and operate synchronously. The OpenAPI
reference exposes the `SyncMode` and `SyncPhase` settings and provides the
`MotorSyncStatus` endpoint.

## Synchronization Through Inputs and Outputs

Use one LRS4000 as the reference device and configure the remaining devices
as synchronized devices.

1. On the reference device, set the motor synchronization source to **No
   source**, define its start angle, and configure an output with the index
   signal as its source.
2. On each synchronized device, set the motor synchronization source to
   **Line (index signal at IN1)** and define its start angle.
3. Connect each synchronized device's IN1 to the reference device's output
   that generates the index signal.

Combine measurement data from multiple devices in the customer application.

## Check Synchronization Status

Read the `MotorSyncStatus` endpoint in the
[LRS4000 REST API reference](./rest-api-openapi.md). The documented values
distinguish between no clock/rotation synchronization, time synchronization
only, and synchronized operation.

- [LRS4000 REST API | OpenAPI](./rest-api-openapi.md)

# Release Notes

This page summarizes LRS4000 firmware changes, fixes, compatibility notes,
and known issues. The releases apply to the LRS4581R. Check the device serial
number and firmware version before applying release-specific information.

## General Information

The extended-range capability is available for eligible devices. Firmware from
version 1.7.0 supports that mode only on devices produced from November 2024
with serial number `SN2442xxxx` or higher. Earlier devices may be updated, but
do not gain the extended-range feature.

## Update Instructions

Use SOPAS ET or SICK AppManager for firmware updates. Downgrading firmware is not
recommended.

Before updating, unpack the firmware package on the computer, connect the sensor by
Ethernet on the same subnet, and maintain a stable power supply. Save the
parameter file, add the device to the SOPAS ET project, select **Download
firmware**, and install the appropriate `.spk` package. After the sensor
reboots, verify its firmware version and operation. Follow the complete update
procedure for the firmware package before updating a production device.

## Firmware V1.10.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New features:** Redesigned web interface, cybersecurity page, HTTPS for web services, distance-data recording, and Perpendicular Distance.

**Improvements:** SOPAS ET web-server access and encoder settings presentation.

**New features.**

- The web interface was redesigned, and a cybersecurity page was added to
  show open ports and user levels and manage related settings.
- Web-server and REST configuration can use HTTPS.
- Distance-data recording is available through the SICK data recorder;
  download the software from the device web interface.
- Perpendicular Distance functionality was added.

**Improvements.**

- SOPAS ET can enable a disabled web server and now links to the device web
  interface instead of emulating it.
- Encoder settings are shown under inputs and outputs; encoder functionality
  is unchanged.

**Bug fixes.**

Invalid device IP ranges are rejected, field-evaluation bugs were corrected,
and DHCP fallback behavior was corrected to static IP.

**Incompatibilities.**

- `sWN EtherCoLaAEventsEnable` is no longer available. CoLa A event output is
  generally allowed, but do not use it for LMDscandata because data may be
  lost.
- `sWN ScanDataEnable` has no effect. Use the data-output format setting to
  disable output.

**Known issues.**

Device temperature is displayed as 20 °C in the web interface and by
`sRN OPcurtmpdev`. This display and telegram behavior are planned for removal
in a later firmware version.

## Firmware V1.9.1

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R; **Release date:** 2026-04

**Improvements:** Softer motor startup after power-on.

**Bug fixes.**

Field-evaluation group activation through inputs now uses the corrected
input-to-group assignment. The release also fixes an overload error at
startup when multiple configured groups would overload the device if all
were active simultaneously.

**Known issues.**

After reboot, an IP address in the `169.254.x.x` range may cause a fatal
device error. Return the device to `192.168.0.1` and install current firmware
through SOPAS ET as a recovery procedure.

## Firmware V1.9.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New feature:** Adds Sensitivity Mode.

**Sensitivity Mode.**

The mode can extend range and improve detection of highly reflective targets.
Observe the operating conditions in the table below. Using a mode outside its
stated ambient-light conditions may reduce detection probability and increase
noise.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Firmware V1.9.0:** maximum range in standard and extended-range mode (10% remission) and maximum ambient light per sensitivity mode.</p>

| Sensitivity mode | Maximum range, standard mode (10% remission) | Maximum range, extended-range mode (10% remission) | Maximum ambient light |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Normal | 55 m | 100 m | 80 klux |
| Sensitive | 65 m | 115 m | 30 klux |
| Very Sensitive | 70 m | 120 m | 10 klux |

**Incompatibilities.**

The device temperature sensor was removed. `OPcurtmpdev` no longer works.

## Firmware V1.8.1

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**Improvement:** Adds an adjustable TCP transmit timeout for CoLa connections.

`EtherColaTransmitTimeout` adjusts the transmit timeout for TCP connections
on ports 2111 and 2112. The default remains 15 seconds; the setting can be
changed from 250 milliseconds to 15 seconds to speed reconnection after an
unexpected disconnect.

**Bug fixes.**

The release fixes CoLa A/B commands being ignored after reconnecting over an
unstable network on TCP ports 2111 and 2112.

**Known issues.**

The GUI depicts the input/output connector as male A-coded, although the
connector should be female A-coded.

## Firmware V1.8.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New features:** Field-evaluation detection history and teach-in, additional GUI languages, and a cybersecurity tab with a hash calculator.

**Improvements:** Compact timestamps, date/time interface, and maximum region-of-interest range.

**New features.**

- The home page shows field-infringement detection history, with links to
  related field-evaluation pages.
- Teach-in can capture a static background manually or through an input.
  The taught background can be used for blanking and contour evaluation.
- A detection-list shortcut was added to field evaluation.
- Chinese, Japanese, and French were added as GUI languages.
- The cybersecurity tab groups security functions. Its hash calculator is
  required for changing passwords through CoLa A/B or logging in through a
  SICK software driver.

**Improvements and bug fixes.**

The release updates evaluation naming and detection-history presentation,
transmits Compact start/stop timestamps as Linux system time, updates the
date/time GUI, and increases the maximum region-of-interest range from 200 m
to 300 m. It fixes LED enablement not resetting when application defaults are
loaded and corrects SOPAS ET device import so parameters are exported.

**Known issues.**

The input/output connector is depicted as male A-coded in the GUI, but should
be female A-coded.

## Firmware V1.7.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R; extended-range feature only on eligible production units

**New features:** Extended-range mode, field evaluation, online help, user-level management, and distance measurement between two points.

**New features.**

- Extended-range mode increases measurement distance up to 300 m. It is
  selected through the scan configuration, which also changes the scale
  factor. Eligibility is limited to devices produced from November 2024 with
  serial number `SN2442xxxx` or higher.
- Field evaluation supports up to 16 user-defined fields, subject to field
  shape and concurrent application load.
- Online help provides topic descriptions and guided tours.
- Other web-interface user levels can be enabled after logging in at Service
  level; CoLa A/B user levels are unaffected.
- The scan view can measure the distance between two points.

**Improvements and bug fixes.**

The distance filter was renamed **Scanning range filter**, and the ignored
scan area is shown in gray. The 3D scan-recording start/stop control and scan
view were updated. Diagnostic messages gained filtering options. A fatal
error for certain partial scan configurations with first- or last-echo
filtering and a Chromium scan-view compatibility issue were fixed.

**Incompatibilities.**

The default echo-filter value changed from `FIRST_ECHO` to `LAST_ECHO`.

**Known issues.**

During 3D scan recording, an overtime measurement stop may leave the button
showing **Stop**. Pressing it a second time restores the **Start** state.

## Firmware V1.6.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New features:** Scan merge, Compact streaming over TCP, motor synchronization, and system diagnosis.

**New features.**

- Scan merge creates a 3D point cloud using position and orientation from the
  internal IMU or an external encoder. A rotation offset can compensate for
  rotation around a pivot; the recording can be started in the GUI or by a
  digital input. The resulting point cloud can be downloaded through the
  browser.
- Compact streaming was added over TCP port 2115. UDP is not supported for
  this format on this device, and only one streaming format can be enabled at
  a time.
- Motor synchronization can use PTP clock synchronization or a wired index
  signal. Synchronization is disabled by default; the receiver phase can set
  the rotation offset.
- System diagnosis can create a reduced diagnosis after an error or an
  extended file at Service level.

**Improvements.**

Robustness was improved for applications that move or swivel the device.

**Known issues.**

Certain combinations of partial scan configurations and first- or last-echo
filtering could cause a fatal device error. This was fixed in V1.7.0. A
Chrome scan-view issue was also fixed in V1.7.0.

## Firmware V1.5.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New features:** Particle Filter, Distance Filter, updated scan-data viewer, and a prompt to change default passwords.

**New features.**

- Particle Filter removes isolated small-object or noise echoes, such as
  rain or dust, based on distance steps from neighboring beam angles.
- Distance Filter limits scans to a configured range; out-of-range echoes
  receive distance and RSSI values of zero.
- The scan viewer adds 3D and split views.
- The interface prompts users to change passwords that are still at their
  defaults.

**Incompatibilities.**

Customer passwords from firmware earlier than 1.5.0 are reset to defaults
because of updated password handling. The Glare Detection Filter was removed
and replaced by Particle Filter.

**Known issues.**

The fatal-error scan configuration and Chrome scan-view issues from V1.6.0
also apply to this release; both are fixed in V1.7.0.

## Firmware V1.4.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New features:** Contamination Indication, PTP, IMU secondary data, and controls for the web server and CoLaScan/AutoIP.

**New features.**

- Contamination Indication monitors 12 sectors around 360 degrees. Thresholds,
  response time, and weather-protection cover can be configured. Monitoring
  is available by GUI and telegram; evaluation is inactive by default.
- PTP synchronization can be enabled through the web interface or the
  `TSCRole` CoLa parameter.
- IMU secondary data can be read or sent as events.
- The web server can be disabled from connection settings. `EnableColaScan`
  can disable CoLaScan/AutoIP and prevent opening port 30178.

**Improvements.**

The access level for loading factory defaults changed to Service. The 2D
scan-view update interval was improved, connection options were consolidated,
and Expert Mode was removed.

**Bug fixes and incompatibilities.**

The UDP port protocol dialect changed to CoLa B, and SOPAS ET parameter
export was corrected. This release contains an incompatibility affecting
CoLa1.

**Known issues.**

Firmware V1.4.0 has a known fatal-error issue for certain partial scan
configurations with first- or last-echo filtering. Firmware V1.7.0 fixes this
issue.

For feature availability and parameter details, use the documentation for the
device and firmware version.

# SOPASair Walkthrough

SOPASair is the built-in web interface of the LRS4000. It runs directly on
the sensor, so no software installation is needed. Open `http://<sensor-ip>/`
in a browser on the same network as the sensor. The factory default address
is `192.168.0.1`.

You can view status and settings without logging in. To change settings,
log in with the **Authorized Client** user level using the user icon in the
top bar.

![SOPASair Home dashboard showing LRS4581R status, live measurement data, I/O states, and detection history](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_home_overview.png)
*The SOPASair Home dashboard: device status, live scan view, input and output states, and detection history at a glance.*

## Home

The Home page summarizes the sensor's state. It is a good place to start
before you change any settings.

**Status** shows separate indicators for the device, connection,
measurement, field evaluation, and data output. Because each state is
reported independently, measurement can be running while external data
output is switched off.

![LRS4581R device and application status](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_status.png)
*Device and application status indicators.*

**Device information** lists the model, part number, serial number, firmware
version, system time, and the time of the last save. Click **Find device**
to make the sensor LEDs blink, so you can identify the unit on site.

![LRS4581R device information](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_device_information.png)
*Device identity and installed firmware version.*

## Configuration

The Configuration menu contains the measurement, filter, network, and I/O
settings. For the matching REST parameters and value ranges, see the
[LRS4000 OpenAPI reference](./rest-api-openapi.md).

### Basic Settings

**Configuration > Basic settings** defines how the sensor scans. Select a
scan configuration to set the scan rate and angular resolution. The page
also shows the angular range, interlaced mode, and maximum scanning range,
and lets you adjust sensitivity, the status LED, and the measurement state.

![LRS4581R basic settings](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_basic_settings.png)
*Scan configuration and measurement settings. The values shown are an example configuration.*

**Date and system time** shows the device clock and its synchronization
source. **Apply computer time** sets the sensor clock to your computer's
time. For network-based time sources, see
[Time synchronization](../shared-features/time-synchronization.md).

![LRS4581R date and system time](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_date_time.png)
*Device clock and time synchronization settings.*

**Motor synchronization** aligns the rotation of several scanners to avoid
mutual interference. Select the synchronization source here when you
integrate multiple sensors. See [Motor synchronization](./motor-synchronization.md)
for setup details.

![LRS4581R motor synchronization](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_motor_synchronization.png)
*Motor synchronization source.*

### Filter

**Configuration > Filter** combines the echo, particle, median, and mean
filters. The echo filter selects all, first, or last echoes. Expand each
of the other filters to set its threshold, width, or averaging parameters.
See [Filter details](../data-streaming/filter-details.md) for how each filter
affects the measurement data.

![LRS4581R filter settings](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_filters.png)
*Echo, particle, median, and mean filters.*

### Contamination Indication

**Configuration > Contamination indication** monitors the front window for
dirt. The sector diagram shows the contamination state per sector, using
the color legend below it. You can configure whether a warning or error is
output, the sensitivity, the monitored sectors, and the response delay. See
[Contamination indication](../on-device-applications/contamination-indication.md) for
the application background.

![LRS4581R contamination indication](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_contamination.png)
*Contamination status per sector and evaluation settings.*

### Connection Options

**Configuration > Connection options** contains the Ethernet settings:
addressing mode, IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, MAC address, and
link speed.

When you click **Apply**, the new network settings take effect immediately.
The browser loses its connection if the sensor moves to an address that your
computer cannot reach, so note the new address before applying the change.

![LRS4581R Ethernet settings](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_ethernet.png)
*Ethernet addressing and link settings.*

### Inputs and Outputs

**Configuration > Inputs and outputs** assigns each port as an input or an
output. For outputs, select the signal sources, inversion, logic, and
restart behavior. The connector diagram next to each port shows the
corresponding pin, and the status indicators show the current physical
state. Enable **Use encoder** if an external encoder is connected.

![LRS4581R input and output assignments](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_inputs_outputs.png)
*Port assignments with connector pin diagrams.*

## Applications

The Applications menu contains measurement-data output and the on-device
applications: field evaluation, 3D scan recording, and perpendicular
distance measurement.

### Data Output

**Application > Data output** selects the output format: Compact,
LMDscandata, or Deactivated. The page lists the protocols and ports on which
the data is available. See [Data streaming](../data-streaming/index.md) for
the transport options and parser requirements.

![LRS4581R measurement-data output](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_data_output.png)
*Output format, protocols, and ports.*

**Output data format** selects the optional content of each telegram:
device name, time stamp, encoder values, and RSSI. It also sets the output
interval and the distance scaling factor.

![LRS4581R output data format](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_output_format.png)
*Optional telegram content, output interval, and scaling factor.*

**Output range** limits the output to a start and stop angle.

![LRS4581R output angular range](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_output_range.png)
*Start and stop angle of the output range.*

**Range filter** removes measurement points outside a distance window.

![LRS4581R distance filter](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_range_filter.png)
*Distance filter.*

### Field Evaluation

**Application > Field evaluation** monitors fields for objects and switches
outputs when a field is infringed. Each group combines fields, evaluations,
and outputs, and has its own activation source. **Resource requirements**
shows how much of the sensor's evaluation capacity is in use, and
**Detection list** shows recent detections.

![LRS4581R field evaluation groups](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_field_evaluation.png)
*An evaluation group with its field, evaluation, and output.*

**Teach-in** creates a field automatically from the current environment.
Set the distances in front of and behind the detected contour and the
minimum teach-in time, then start teach-in from the button or a digital
input.

![LRS4581R teach-in controls](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_teach_in.png)
*Teach-in parameters and start control.*

See [Field evaluation](../on-device-applications/field-evaluation.md) for a complete
commissioning procedure.

### 3D Scan Recording

**Application > 3D scan recording** combines 2D scans with the sensor's
rotation to build a 3D point cloud. The rotation comes from the internal
IMU or an external encoder. Start the recording with the button or an
input signal, and download the resulting point cloud when it is complete.

![LRS4581R 3D scan recording settings](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_scan_recording.png)
*3D scan recording with the internal IMU as rotation source.*

### Perpendicular Distance Measurement

**Application > Perpendicular distance measurement** reports the shortest
and furthest measuring points within a field, relative to a reference
plane. Use **Add group** to define a new measurement, and
**Result list for distance measurement** to view the results.

![LRS4581R perpendicular-distance application](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_perpendicular_distance.png)
*A perpendicular-distance measurement group.*

## Diagnostics

### Overview

**Diagnostics > Overview** combines status, device identity, operating
information, the current device status, and the message log. Expand
**Operating information** to see the number of power-on cycles, the
operating hours, and the time of the last parameterization.

![LRS4581R operating information](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_operating_information.png)
*Power-on count, operating hours, and last parameterization.*

The message table lists current and past events with their status number
and description. If you need support, use **Create diagnostic file** to
collect the device state in one file and send it to SICK. See
[Contact](../contact.md).

### Cybersecurity

**Diagnostics > Cybersecurity** shows the HTTPS certificate with its
fingerprint, serial number, issuer, and expiry date. Use
**Create certificate** to generate a new certificate. The **Hash calculator**
helps you verify file checksums. See
[HTTPS and certificates](../configuration/https-and-certificates.md) for the
complete certificate setup.

![LRS4581R cybersecurity certificate status](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_certificates.png)
*HTTPS certificate overview.*

### Data Recorder

**Diagnostics > Data recorder** explains how to install the SICK data
recorder on your computer and connect it to the sensor. Use the recorder
to capture measurement data for later analysis or support cases.

![LRS4581R recorder instructions](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_recorder.png)
*Installation and connection steps for the data recorder.*

### Detection History

**Diagnostics > Detection history** records field-evaluation detections.
Select the evaluations to include, then start the history. The
**Statistics** section counts the detections per evaluation, and the
**Detection list** shows each event with its time stamp. Use
**Reset detection history** to clear the counters.

![LRS4581R detection history](../assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair_detection_statistics.png)
*Detection counts per evaluation.*
