# Electrical Connection

## PWR / 8 IOs

System plug part numbers: 2155106, 2148845

The PWR and I/O connection uses a male, 12-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

![PWR and I/O connector face with numbered pins](../assets/electrical-symbols/multiscan200-pwr.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">PWR and I/O connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**PWR / 8 IOs** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `IN1/OUT1` | Configurable digital input 1 or output 1 |
| 2 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 3 | `IN2/OUT2` | Configurable digital input 2 or output 2 |
| 4 | `IN7/OUT7` | Configurable digital input 7 or output 7 |
| 5 | `IN8/OUT8` | Configurable digital input 8 or output 8 |
| 6 | `IN3/OUT3` | Configurable digital input 3 or output 3 |
| 7 | `IN4/OUT4` | Configurable digital input 4 or output 4 |
| 8 | `IN6/OUT6` | Configurable digital input 6 or output 6 |
| 9 | `Vs` | Supply, +9 V DC to +30 V DC |
| 10 | `IN5/OUT5` | Configurable digital input 5 or output 5 |
| 11 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 12 | `Vs` | Supply, +9 V DC to +30 V DC |

**Always wire both supply pins 9 and 12 and both ground pins 2 and 11.** This is
a requirement in the multiScan270 operating instructions, not an optional
parallel connection.

## Ethernet

The Ethernet connection uses a female, 8-pin, X-coded M12 connector.

![Ethernet connector face with numbered pins](../assets/electrical-symbols/multiscan200-ethernet.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">Ethernet connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Ethernet** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `TRD0_P` | Transmit/receive pair 0 + |
| 2 | `TRD0_N` | Transmit/receive pair 0 − |
| 3 | `TRD1_P` | Transmit/receive pair 1 + |
| 4 | `TRD1_N` | Transmit/receive pair 1 − |
| 5 | `TRD3_P` | Transmit/receive pair 3 + |
| 6 | `TRD3_N` | Transmit/receive pair 3 − |
| 7 | `TRD2_N` | Transmit/receive pair 2 − |
| 8 | `TRD2_P` | Transmit/receive pair 2 + |

The X-coded Gigabit Ethernet interface requires all four data pairs. A
four-wire D-coded connection is unsuitable.

# picoScan100

![picoScan100 2D LiDAR sensor](../assets/picoScan100/img/product-photo.png)
<p class="caption product-image-caption">picoScan100 2D LiDAR sensor.</p>

The picoScan100 is a compact 2D LiDAR sensor with one scan plane and a 276° scan range. It comes in two variants: the picoScan120 and the picoScan150. Use the Product ID (PID) to find the exact product variant on [sick.com](https://www.sick.com/): enter the part number (P/N) and optional serial number (S/N), for example `1134610/25250710`. A complete [pid.sick.com](https://pid.sick.com/) URL is also accepted.

# CoLa Telegram Listing

This reference lists the CoLa telegrams supported by the picoScan100. Use the command details to build or troubleshoot PLC and other low-level integrations without guessing the telegram structure.

## General

### Log In [sMN SetAccessMode]

A log in to the device is necessary to change parameters. In most cases, the user level 'Authorized client' is needed. Changed parameters will be reset to the previous state via a reboot unless they are saved. To save parameter changes the command "sMN mEEwriteall" must be sent before log out.

**Telegram structure: sMN SetAccessMode**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | User level | String | 13 | | `SetAccessMode` | `53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65` |
| User level | Select user level | Int_8 | 1 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `2<br>3<br>4` | `02<br>03<br>04` |
| Password | Hash value for the selected user level | Uint_32 | 4 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `B21ACE26<br>F4724744<br>81BE23AA` | `B2 1A CE 26<br>F4 72 47 44<br>81 BE 23 AA` |

**Example: sMN SetAccessMode - Log in as “Authorized client” with password “F4724744”**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sMN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}3{SPC}F4724744<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sMN SetAccessMode 3 F4724744<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sMN SetAccessMode 3 F4724744` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 30 33 20 46 34 37 32 34 37 34 34 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 17 73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 03 F4 72 47 44 B3` |
| CoLa B | `73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 03 F4 72 47 44` |

**Telegram structure: sAN SetAccessMode**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sAN` | `73 41 4E` |
| Command | User level | String | 13 | | `SetAccessMode` | `53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65` |
| Change user level | Changed level | Bool_1 | 1 | Error:<br>Success: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sAN SetAccessMode**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sAN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}1<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 31 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 13 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 01 38` |

### Enable/ Disable CoLa User Levels [sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel]

This command enables and disables a specific CoLa user level (Maintenance, Authorized Client).

**Telegram structure: sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | Enable/ disable CoLa user level | String | 21 | | `EnableLegacyUserLevel` | `45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C` |
| User level | - | Uint_8 | 1 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized Client: | `2<br>3` | `02<br>03` |
| Status | Enable/ disable | Bool_1 | 1 | Disable:<br>Enable: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel - Enable User Level Authorized Client**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sMN{SPC}EnableLegacyUserLevel{SPC}3{SPC}1<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel 3 1<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel 3 1` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 4D 4E 20 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C 20 33 20 31 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1D 73 4D 4E 20 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C 20 03 20 01 21` |
| CoLa B | `73 4D 4E 20 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C 20 03 20 01` |

**Telegram structure: sAN EnableLegacyUserLevel**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sAN` | `73 41 4E` |
| Command | Enable/ disable CoLa user level | String | 21 | | `EnableLegacyUserLevel` | `45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C` |
| Status code | Confirmation | Bool_1 | 1 | unsuccessful:<br>successful: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sAN EnableLegacyUserLevel - Enabling/ disabling of the CoLa User Level was successful**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sAN{SPC}EnableLegacyUserLevel{SPC}1<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 41 4E 20 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C 20 31 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1B 73 41 4E 20 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C 20 01 0E` |

### Read for Frequency and Angular Resolution [sRN LMPscancfg]

Read the scanning frequency, angular resolution and aperture angle of the device. Values show the information of the values before any filters are applied. Therefore aperture angle is always showing the maximum, scanning frequency and angular resolution may also be static depending on device family.

**Telegram structure: sRN LMPscancfg**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Read | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | Info of scan frequency and angular resolution | String | 10 | | `LMPscancfg` | `4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67` |

**Example: sRN LMPscancfg**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN{SPC}LMPscancfg<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN LMPscancfg<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sRN LMPscancfg` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0E 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 63` |
| CoLa B | `73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67` |

**Telegram structure: sRA LMPscancfg**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sRA` | `73 52 41` |
| Command | Info of scan frequency and angular resolution | String | 10 | | `LMPscancfg` | `4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67` |
| Scan frequency | [1/100 Hz] | Uint_32 | 4 | 15 Hz ... 50 Hz:<br>(depends on Dynamic Sensing Profile ) | `5DCh ... 1388h` | `05 DC ... 13 88` |
| Reserved | - | Int_16 | 2 | Always: | `1` | `00 01` |
| Angular resolution | [1/10000°] | Uint_32 | 4 | 0.1° ... 1°:<br>(depends on Dynamic Sensing Profile ) | `3E8h … 2710h` | `03 E8 ... 27 10` |
| Start angle | [1/10000°] | Int_32 | 4 | -48° ... 228° | `FFF8AD00h … 22CA40h` | `FF F8 AD 00h … 00 22 CA 40h` |
| Stop angle | [1/10000°] | Int_32 | 4 | -48° ... 228° | `FFF8AD00h … 22CA40h` | `FF F8 AD 00h … 00 22 CA 40h` |

**Example: sRA LMPscancfg - 30 Hz scan frequency, 0.1° angular resolution, -48° start angle, +138° stop angle**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRA{SPC}LMPscancfg{SPC}BB8{SPC}1{SPC}3E8{SPC}FFEAF160{SPC}150EA0<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 52 41 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 20 42 42 38 20 31 20 33 45 38 20 46 46 45 41 46 31 36 30 20 31 35 30 45 41 30 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 21 73 52 41 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 20 00 00 0B B8 00 01 00 00 03 E8 FF EA F1 60 00 15 0E A0 2A` |

### Autostart Measurement [sWN LMPautostartmeas]

This parameter defines whether the scanner will start to rotate directly and measure when powering up or remain in idle mode. The changed setting (saved with the command sMN mEEWriteall, ) will be then be active with the next power-up cycle.

In case autostart is deactivated, the sensor will remain in idle mode with the laser switched off and a motor speed depending on the Dynamic Sensing Profile .

**Telegram structure: sWN LMPautostartmeas**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | Autostart measurement | String | 16 | | `LMPautostartmeas` | `4C 4D 50 61 75 74 6F 73 74 61 72 74 6D 65 61 73` |
| Status code | Activate / Deactivate Autostart | Bool_1 | 1 | Autostart off:<br>Autostart on: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sWN LMPautostartmeas 1**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sWN{SPC}LMPautostartmeas{SPC}1<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sWN LMPautostartmeas 1<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sWN LMPautostartmeas 1` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 57 4E 20 4C 4D 50 61 75 74 6F 73 74 61 72 74 6D 65 61 73 20 31 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 16 73 57 4E 20 4C 4D 50 61 75 74 6F 73 74 61 72 74 6D 65 61 73 20 01 4F` |
| CoLa B | `73 57 4E 20 4C 4D 50 61 75 74 6F 73 74 61 72 74 6D 65 61 73 20 01` |

**Telegram structure: sWA LMDautostartmeas**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Read Checksum [sRN LFTchecksum]

This command includes the MD5 checksum of multiple software parts to verify their integrity. The checksums help to ensure files have not been corrupted or altered. They are also important for cybersecurity because they detect unauthorized modifications.

**Telegram structure: sRN LFTchecksum**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Command | MD5 checksum | String | 11 | | `LFTchecksum` | `4C 46 54 63 68 65 63 6B 73 75 6D` |

### Change Password [sMN SetPassword]

Changing the log in password for a specific user level.

If logged in with a higher user level you may set the password for lower user levels as well.

**Telegram structure: sMN SetPassword**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Command | Set password request | String | 13 | | `SetPassword` | `53 65 74 50 61 73 73 77 6F 72 64` |
| User level | User level that the password will be applied to | Int_8 | 1 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `2<br>3<br>4` | `02<br>03<br>04` |
| Password | Hash value of the new password | Uint_32 | 4 | | `<Hash value>` | |

Set password for 'Authorized client' to “testtest” (hash value = 1920E4C9).

| CoLa B | `73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 50 61 73 73 77 6F 72 64 20 03 19 20 E4 C9` |

### Set Contamination Indication Settings [sWN ContaminationConfig]

Define how and under which conditions the device shall indicate a potential contamination of the optics cover to enable preventive cleaning.

**Telegram structure: sWN ContaminationConfig**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |

| Strategy | Strategy code | Enum_8 | 1 | No output:<br>All sectors contaminated:<br>One sector contaminated: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Response time | How fast (in seconds) the sensor reacts after a contamination | Uint_16 | 2 | Value range 3 ... 60<br>Default: 3 | `+3d … +60d (03h … 3Ch)` | `00 03 … 00 3C` |
| Threshold warning | Sensitivity | Enum_8 | 1 | High:<br>Medium:<br>Low: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Sector preselection | Selection of either custom sectors or used weather protection hood | Enum_8 | 1 | All sectors:<br>Weather protection hood:<br>Custom sectors: | `0<br>6<br>255d (FFh)` | `00<br>06<br>FF` |
| Length | | UInt_16 | 2 | Always: | `7` | `00 07` |

| Enable Warning | Warning monitoring | Bool_1 | 1 | Off (False):<br>On (True): | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Enable Error | Error monitoring | Bool_1 | 1 | Off (False):<br>On (True): | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

## Measurement Output Telegram

### Configure the Data Content for the Scan [sWN LMDscandatacfg]

Configuration of the channels (e.g. distance) and information that will be send by the device as measurement data (output data format).

**Telegram structure: sWN LMDscandatacfg**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | Configure scandata | String | 14 | | `LMDscandatacfg` | `4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 63 66 67` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_8 | 2 | Always: | `0 0` | `00 00` |
| RSSI | Enable or disable the output of RSSI values | Uint_8 | 1 | RSSI disabled:<br>RSSI enabled: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Reserved | - | Enum_8 | 1 | Always: | `0` | `00` |
| Reserved | - | Enum_8 | 1 | Always: | `0` | `00` |
| Encoder | Encoder data | Uint_8 | 2 | No encoder:<br>Channel 1: | `0 0<br>1 0` | `00 00<br>01 00` |
| Reserved | - | Bool_1 | 1 | Always: | `0` | `00` |
| Device name | Sends the device name | Bool_1 | 1 | No:<br>Yes: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Reserved | - | Bool_1 | 1 | Always: | `0` | `00` |
| Time | Sends time stamp information | Bool_1 | 1 | No:<br>Yes: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_16 | 2 | Always: | `+1d (1h)` | `00 01` |

Example: RSSI enabled

**Example: sWN LMDscandatacfg**

| Protocol | Example |

### Poll One Telegram [sRN LMDscandata]

Asking the device for the measurement values of the last valid scan. The device will respond, even if currently no measurement data is created (e.g. due to standby or log in).

Data is transmitted only via LMDscandata when LMDscandata is selected as data output format.

During the boot-up phase of the device, there will be no data telegram or answer from the device.

**Telegram structure: sRN LMDscandata**

### Send Data Permanently [sEN LMDscandata]

Start/ stop continuous retrievement of measurement data from device. Data will be transmitted as configured as soon as measurement data is generated by the device. No data is generated when there is an active log in, the laser is shut off (e.g. in Standby mode), the motor is stopped or in case of certain error modes (e.g. Device not ready).

Data is transmitted only via LMDscandata when LMDscandata is selected as data output format.

During the boot-up phase of the device, there will be no data telegram or answer from the device.

**Telegram structure: sEN LMDscandata**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Event | String | 3 | | `sEN` | `73 45 4E` |
| Command | Data telegram | String | 11 | | `LMDscandata` | `4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61` |
| Measurement | Start/stop | Enum_8 | 1 | Stop:<br>Start: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sEN LMDscandata**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sEN{SPC}LMDscandata{SPC}1<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sEN LMDscandata 1<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sEN LMDscandata 1` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 31 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 11 73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 01 33` |
| CoLa B | `73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 01` |

LMDscandata - reserved values

Valid distance measurement values are values starting from 16d upwards; everything below has the following meaning:

| DIST | RSSI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0d | 0d | Invalid measurement value; caused by very low remission (extremely dark object), object distance not within measurement range (too close or too far away) or selected filter settings at device |
| 1d - 15d | 0d | Reserved, currently not in use |
| ≥16d | >0h | Valid measurement values |
| ≥16d | 254d | Reflector detected |
| ≥16d | 255d | Reserved |

Higher measurement values will be given out with a zero, that means no measurement value detected.

### Set Time Stamp [sMN LSPsetdatetime]

The data format in the telegram is: +2009{SPC}+7{SPC}+22{SPC}+12{SPC}+0{SPC}+0{SPC}+0.The numbers represent year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond.

If plus is used up-front the data it is interpreted as an integer decimal number, without the plus it's the scanner reads the data as hex format.

The answer is always in ASCII format.

Does only work if NTP- respectively PTP-Client is not active.

There is no real time clock inside the device. When the scanner is switched off and after a reboot, the time has to be set again. Therefore, it is recommended to use a NTP or a PTP setting.

**Telegram structure: sMN LSPsetdatetime**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | Set time stamp | String | 14 | | `LSPsetdatetime` | `4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65` |
| Year | | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+1970d … +2099d (07B2h … 0833h)` | `07 B2 … 08 33` |
| Month | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+1d … +12d(01h … 0Ch)` | `01 … 0C` |
| Day | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+1d … +31d(01h … 1Fh)` | `00 … 1F` |
| Hour | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d … +23d(00h … 17h)` | `00 … 17` |
| Minute | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh)` | `00 … 3B` |
| Second | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh)` | `00 … 3B` |
| Microsecond | | Uint_32 | 4 | | `+0d … +999999d(00000000h … 000F423Fh)` | `00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F` |

**Example 1: sMN LSPsetdatetime Date: 17.02.2009; Time: 16:34**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sMN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}7D9{SPC}2{SPC}11{SPC}10{SPC}22{SPC}0{SPC}0<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sMN LSPsetdatetime 7D9 2 11 10 22 0 0<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sMN LSPsetdatetime 7D9 2 11 10 22 0 0` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 37 44 39 20 32 20 31 31 20 31 30 20 32 32 20 30 20 30 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1E 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 D9 02 11 10 22 00 00 00 00 00 A3` |
| CoLa B | `73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 D9 02 11 10 22 00 00 00 00 00` |

**Example 2: sMN LSPsetdatetime Date: 26.01.2010; Time: 10:35**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sMN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}+2010{SPC}+01{SPC}+26{SPC}+10{SPC}+35{SPC}0{SPC}0<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sMN LSPsetdatetime +2010 +01 +26 +10 +35 0 0<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sMN LSPsetdatetime +2010 +01 +26 +10 +35 0 0` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 2B 32 30 31 30 20 2B 30 31 20 2B 32 36 20 2B 31 30 20 2B 33 35 20 2B 30 30 20 2B 30 30 30 30 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1E 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 DA 01 1A 0A 23 00 00 00 00 00 B3` |
| CoLa B | `73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 DA 01 1A 0A 23 00 00 00 00 00` |

**Telegram structure: sAN LSPsetdatetime**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sAN` | `73 41 4E` |
| Command | Set time stamp | String | 14 | | `LSPsetdatetime` | `4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65` |
| Status code | Code number | Enum_8 | 1 | Success: | `0` | `00` |

**Example 1, 2: sAN LSPsetdatetime**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sAN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}0<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 41 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 30 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 14 73 41 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 00 50` |

Activate time stamp in the output string format or on SOPAS page “data processing”.

| Status code | Code number | Bool_1 | 1 | Inactive:<br>Active: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Threshold1) | Particle threshold in mm | Uint_16 | 2 | (must be taken) | `+500d (1F4h)` | `01 F4` |

### Set Angle Range Filter [sWN LFPangleRangeFilter]

The angle range filter set up the horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) start- and stop angle in rad.

BeamIncrement = the 'beamIncrement' which is used to subsample the beams within the selected angle range. With a 'beamIncrement' of n only every nth beam from the selected angle range is copied to the output scan, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. If the beamIncrement is zero it is set to one.

**Telegram structure: sWN LFPangleRangeFilter**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | filter set up the horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) start- and stop angle in rad | String | 19 | | `LFPangleRangeFilter` | `4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72` |
| Variable Data 1 | Enables/Disables the filter | Bool_1 | 1 | Off:<br>On: | `+0d<br>+1d` | `00<br>01` |
| Variable Data 2 | ThetaStart | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-1,800,000d ... +1,800,000d (FFE488C0 ... 001B7740h)` | `FF E4 88 C0 … 00 1B 77 40` |
| Variable Data 3 | ThetaStop | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-1,800,000d ... +1,800,000d (FFE488C0 ... 001B7740h)` | `FF E4 88 C0 … 00 1B 77 40` |
| Variable Data 4 | PhiStart | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-900,000d ... +900,000d (FFF24460 ... 000DBBA0h)` | `FF F2 44 60 … 00 0D BB A0` |
| Variable Data 5 | PhiStop | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-900,000d ... +900,000d (FFF24460 ... 000DBBA0h)` | `FF F2 44 60 … 00 0D BB A0` |
| Variable Data 6 | BeamIncrement | UInt_16 | 2 | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `1d…+20d` | `00 01 … 00 14` |

Explanation: Enable the angle range filter and set up theta (horizontal) start -90°, theta stop +90°, phi (vertical) start -90°, phi stop +90°, beam increment 1

**Example: sWN LFPangleRangeFilter**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sWN{SPC}LFPangleRangeFilter{SPC}1{SPC}-900000{SPC}+900000{SPC}-900000{SPC}+900000{SPC}1<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sWN LFPangleRangeFilter 1 -900000 +900000 -900000 +900000 1<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sWN LFPangleRangeFilter 1 -900000 +900000 -900000 +900000 1` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 57 4E 20 4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 20 31 20 2D 39 30 30 30 30 30 20 2B 39 30 30 30 30 30 20 2D 39 30 30 30 30 30 20 2B 39 30 30 30 30 30 20 31 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 2B 73 57 4E 20 4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 20 01 FF F2 44 60 00 0D BB A0 FF F2 44 60 00 0D BB A0 00 01 2E` |
| CoLa B | `73 57 4E 20 4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 20 01 FF F2 44 60 00 0D BB A0 FF F2 44 60 00 0D BB A0 00 01` |

**Telegram structure: sWA LFP AngleRangeFilter**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sWA` | `73 57 41` |

### Read Angle Range Filter [sRN LFPangleRangeFilter]

The angle range filter set up the horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) start- and stop angle in rad.

BeamIncrement = the 'beamIncrement' which is used to subsample the beams within the selected angle range. With a 'beamIncrement' of n only every nth beam from the selected angle range is copied to the output scan, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. If the beamIncrement is zero it is set to one.

**Telegram structure: sRN LFPangleRangeFilter**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Read | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | filter set up the horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) start- and stop angle in rad | String | 19 | | `LFPangleRangeFilter` | `4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72` |

**Example: sRN LFPangleRangeFilter**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN{SPC}LFPangleRangeFilter<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 52 4E 20 4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 17 73 52 4E 20 4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 0B` |

**Telegram structure: sRA LFP AngleRangeFilter**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Command | filter set up the horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) start- and stop angle in rad | String | 19 | | `LFPangleRangeFilter` | `4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72` |
| Variable Data 1 | Enables/Disables the filter | Bool_1 | 1 | Off:<br>On: | `+0d<br>+1d` | `00<br>01` |
| Variable Data 2 | ThetaStart | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting | `-1,800,000d ... +1,800,000d (FFE488C0 ... 001B7740h)` | `FF E4 88 C0 … 00 1B 77 40` |
| Variable Data 3 | ThetaStop | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting | `-1,800,000d ... +1,800,000d (FFE488C0 ... 001B7740h)` | `FF E4 88 C0 … 00 1B 77 40` |
| Variable Data 4 | PhiStart | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting | `-900,000d ... +900,000d (FFF24460 ... 000DBBA0h)` | `FF F2 44 60 … 00 0D BB A0` |

## Inputs and Outputs

### Read State of the Ports [sRN LIDportstate]

LIDportstate has to be available additionally or as successor of the LIDoutputstate telegram.

Valid for all sensors with Ethernet and ports (inputs / outputs).

**Telegram structure: sRN LIDportstate**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Read | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | Ask for port configuration | String | 12 | | `LIDportstate` | `4C 49 44 70 6F 72 74 73 74 61 74 65` |

**Example: sRN LIDportstate**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN{SPC}LIDportstate<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN LIDportstate<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sRN LIDportstate` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 52 4E 20 4C 49 44 70 6F 72 74 73 74 61 74 65 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 10 73 52 4E 20 4C 49 44 70 6F 72 74 73 74 61 74 65 60` |
| CoLa B | `73 52 4E 20 4C 49 44 70 6F 72 74 73 74 61 74 65` |

**Telegram structure: sRA LIDportstate**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |

| Status code | System counter (time in µs since power up max. 71min then starting from 0 again) | Uint_32 | 4 | | `0 … FFFFFFFFh` | `00 00 00 00 … FF FF FF FF` |

| | ….. | | | | | |

| State of the ports and count value in hex | External port counter | Uint_32 | 4 | | `0 … FFFFFFFFh` | `00 00 00 00 … FF FF FF FF` |
| Time | States code | Enum_16 | 1 | No time data:<br>Time data: | `00 00<br>00 01` | `00 00<br>00 01` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Year | Array | 2 | E.g. | `1970` | `07 B2` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Month | Array | 1 | | `1 … 12` | `01 … 0C` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Day | Array | 1 | | `1 … 31` | `01 … 1F` |

| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Second | Array | 1 | | `0 … 59` | `00 … 3B` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Microsecond | Array | 4 | | `0 … 999999` | `00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F` |

Inputs/outputs: If the device has separate inputs and outputs (instead of general purpose ports) the ARRAY shall start with inputs followed by the outputs.

Virtual ports are ports that can be used to expand the number of ports but are not physically available. They just show up in the corresponding ethernet telegrams (like LIDportstate).

Tri-State: Port is neither input nor output; the port is set inactive in SOPAS

### Set Port Configuration [sWN PortConfiguration]

Configuration of the given ports. Telegram structure represents the configuration of 1 port.

If the device has multiple ports, use the same structure.

**Telegram structure: sWN PortConfiguration**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | Configuration of the given ports | String | 17 | | `PortConfiguration` | `50 6F 72 74 43 6F 6E 66 69 67 75 72 61 74 69 6F 6E` |
| Port Type | Input or Output | Enum_8 | 1 | Input:<br>Output: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Name | Name of the port | FlexString | 9<br>(0..32) | Default: | `InOut1` | `00 06 49 6E 4F 75 74 31 00` |
| Input Settings | | | | | | |
| Logic | Logic of the input | Enum_8 | 1 | Active high:<br>Active low: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Debounce | Select debouncing time in ms | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d ... +255d (0h … FFh)` | `00 … FF` |
| Reserved | - | Enum_8 | 1 | Always: | `+0d (0h)` | `00` |
| Reserved1 | | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |
| Reserved2 | | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |
| Output Settings | | | | | | |
| Logic | Definition of the output logic | Enum_8 | 1 | Active high:<br>Active low: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Output Mode | Set kind of mode for output pin | Enum_8 | 1 | PNP:<br>NPN:<br>Push-Pull: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Restart Type | Defines type of restart to be used | Enum_8 | 1 | Immediately:<br>Time: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Restart Time | [Only with restart type = Time], time in ms | Uint_32 | 4 | (20 ms … 600,000 ms) | `+20d … +600000d (C8h ... 927C0h)` | `00 00 00 00 … 00 09 27 C0` |
| Restart Input | [Only with restart type = Input], input for restart | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+1d ... +8d (1h ... 8h)` | `00 00 … 00 08` |
| Combination | Combining multiple Events and/or Inputs | Enum_8 | 1 | AND:<br>OR:<br>XOR: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)<br>+2d (2h)` | |

| Reserved | Reserved value 4 | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |

| Source Name | Name of the source option | String | 4 | DeviceNotReady:<br>Input1:<br>Input2:<br>SopasCommand: | `DRDY<br>IN01<br>IN02<br>SC01` | `44 52 44 59<br>49 4E 30 31<br>49 4E 30 32<br>53 43 30 31` |
| Invert | Invert the source signal | Bool_1 | 1 | Not inverted:<br>Inverted: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Reserved | Reserved value 5 | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00` |
| Reserved | Reserved value 6 | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00` |

### Read State of the Inputs [sRN LIDinputstate]

Use sEN LIDinputstate 1 to receive a telegram each time an input signal (e.g. by trigger) changes.

**Telegram structure: sRN LIDinputstate**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Read | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | Input state | String | 14 | | `LIDinputstate` | `4C 49 44 69 6E 70 75 74 73 74 61 74 65` |

**Example: sRN LIDinputstate**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN{SPC}LIDinputstate<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN LIDinputstate<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sRN LIDinputstate` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 52 4E 20 4C 49 44 69 6E 70 75 74 73 74 61 74 65 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 11 73 52 4E 20 4C 49 44 69 6E 70 75 74 73 74 61 74 65 0F` |
| CoLa B | `73 52 4E 20 4C 49 44 69 6E 70 75 74 73 74 61 74 65` |

**Telegram structure: sRA LIDinputstate**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sRA` | `73 52 41` |

### Set Output State [sMN mDOSetOutput]

Output source needs to be set to "SOPAS command" and the port configured as Output (in case of I/O).

| Command | Set output state | String | 12 | | `mDOSetOutput` | `6D 44 4F 53 65 74 4F 75 74 70 75 74` |
| Output number | | Uint_8 | 1 | Depends on system plug: | `1 … 3<br>1 … 6` | `01 … 03<br>01 … 06` |
| Output state | | Enum_8 | 1 | Not active:<br>Active: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

### Read Temperature [sRN OPcurtmpdev]

With this command the internal temperature of the device can be identified. Please note that it does not give an indication of the current ambient temperature.

**Telegram structure: sRN OPcurtmpdev**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Read | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | Read temperature of the device | String | 11 | | `OPcurtmpdev` | `4F 50 63 75 72 74 6D 70 64 65 76` |

**Example: sRN OPcurtmpdev**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN{SPC}OPcurtmpdev<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN OPcurtmpdev<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sRN OPcurtmpdev` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 52 4E 20 4F 50 63 75 72 74 6D 70 64 65 76 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0F 73 52 4E 20 4F 50 63 75 72 74 6D 70 64 65 76 2A` |
| CoLa B | `73 52 4E 20 4F 50 63 75 72 74 6D 70 64 65 76` |

**Telegram structure: sRA OPcurtmpdev**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sRA` | `73 52 41` |
| Command | Read temperature of the device | String | 11 | | `OPcurtmpdev` | `4F 50 63 75 72 74 6D 70 64 65 76` |
| Temperature data | [°C] | Real as float according to IEEE754 | 4 | (-50°C … +100°C) | `C2480000h … 42C80000h` | `C2 48 00 00 … 42 C8 00 00` |

Example: sRA OPcurtmpdev (35°C)

**Example: sRA OPcurtmpdev**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRA{SPC}OPcurtmpdev{SPC}420C0000<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 52 41 20 4F 50 63 75 72 74 6D 70 64 65 76 20 34 32 30 43 30 30 30 30 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 14 73 52 41 20 4F 50 63 75 72 74 6D 70 64 65 76 20 42 0C 00 00 4B` |

### Read the Current Device Temperature Alarm Status [sRN temperatureAlarmStatus]

| Command | Device temperature alarm status | String | 22 | | `temperatureAlarmStatus` | `74 65 6D 70 65 72 61 74 75 72 65 41 6C 61 72 6D 53 74 61 74 75 73` |

**Example: sRN temperatureAlarmStatus**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN{SPC}temperatureAlarmStatus<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sRN temperatureAlarmStatus<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sRN temperatureAlarmStatus` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 52 4E 20 74 65 6D 70 65 72 61 74 75 72 65 41 6C 61 72 6D 53 74 61 74 75 73 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1A 73 52 4E 20 74 65 6D 70 65 72 61 74 75 72 65 41 6C 61 72 6D 53 74 61 74 75 73 44` |
| CoLa B | `73 52 4E 20 74 65 6D 70 65 72 61 74 75 72 65 41 6C 61 72 6D 53 74 61 74 75 73` |

**Telegram structure: sRA temperatureAlarmStatus**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sRA` | `73 52 41` |

| Data | Alarm state | Bool_1 | 1 | Disabled:<br>Enabled: | `0d (00h)<br>+1d (01h)` | `00 ... 01` |

**Example: sRA temperatureAlarmStatus - Temperature alarm status is off. The device runs in the defined temperature range**

## Interfaces

### Set IP Address [sWN EIIpAddr]

Save permanently to set values. Changes will be active after rebooting the device. Settings must correspond with network in which scanner is used. Else device cannot be found any more.

**Telegram structure: sWN EIIpAddr**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | Set IP address | String | 8 | | `EIIpAddr` | `45 49 49 50 41 64 64 72` |
| IP address | Set values | Uint_8 | 1 | First part of IP address | `0 …+255d (00 ... FF)` | `00 … FF` |
| IP address | Set values | Uint_8 | 1 | Second part of IP address | `0 …+255d (00 ... FF)` | `00 … FF` |
| IP address | Set values | Uint_8 | 1 | Third part of IP address | `0 …+255d (00 ... FF)` | `00 … FF` |
| IP address | Set values | Uint_8 | 1 | Fourth part of IP address | `0 …+255d (00 ... FF)` | `00 … FF` |

**Example: sWN EIIpAddr 192.168.0.2**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sWN{SPC}EIIpAddr{SPC}C0{SPC}A8{SPC}0{SPC}2<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sWN EIIpAddr C0 A8 0 2<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `sWN EIIpAddr C0 A8 0 2` |
| CoLa A | `02 73 57 4E 20 45 49 49 70 41 64 64 72 20 43 30 20 41 38 20 30 20 32 03` |
| CoLa B | `02 02 02 02 00 00 00 11 73 57 4E 20 45 49 49 70 41 64 64 72 20 C0 A8 00 02 06` |
| CoLa B | `73 57 4E 20 45 49 49 70 41 64 64 72 20 C0 A8 00 02` |

**Telegram structure: sWA EIIpAddr**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |

### Set Device Search Mode [sWN EtherColaScanMode]

This command configures the Auto IP functionalities (Device search by SICK Enginnering Tools) and the changeability of the IP address. The functionality can reduces the number of open ports to a minimum.

**Telegram structure: sWN EtherCoLaScanMode**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | Set CoLa Scan / AutoIP search settings | String | 17 | | `EtherCoLaScanMode` | `45 74 68 65 72 43 6F 4C 61 53 63 61 6E 4D 6F 64 65` |
| CoLa Scan / AutoIP search settings | Choose setting | Uint_8 | 1 | IP address can be found/changed without login:<br>IP address can be found/ changed with login:<br>Disable the Auto IP search/ IP change:<br>IP address can be found/changed for 1 min: | `0<br>1<br>2<br>3` | `00<br>01<br>02<br>03` |

**Example: sWN EtherCoLaScanMode 2 - Disable the Auto IP search/ IP change**

| Protocol | Example |
| --- | --- |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sWN{SPC}EtherCoLaScanMode{SPC}2<ETX>` |
| CoLa A | `<STX>sWN EtherCoLaScanMode 2<ETX>` |

## Field Application

### Set Activation of Evaluation Group [sMN ActivateEvaluationGroup]

The telegram is intended to activate or deactivate groups via telegram. The group activation needs to be changed from always to telegram in advance.

**Telegram structure: sMN ActivateEvaluationGroup**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | Activate / deactivate evaluation group | String | 23 | | `ActivateEvaluationGroup` | `41 63 74 69 76 61 74 65 45 76 61 6C 75 61 74 69 6F 6E 47 72 6F 75 70` |
| Amount of evaluation groups to activate/ deactivate | Array | Uint_16 | 2 | Each array element contains two parameters:Evaluation group numberDeactivation / activation of evaluation group | `1d ... 48d (1 ... 30h)` | `00 01 … 00 30` |
| Evaluation group number | Evaluation group 1 | UInt_16 | 2 | | `1` | `00 01` |
| Deactivation / activation of evaluation group | Activate / deactivate evaluation group 1 | Bool_1 | 1 | Deactivate:<br>Activate: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Evaluation group number | Evaluation group 2 | UInt_16 | 2 | | `2` | `00 02` |
| Activate/ deactivate evaluation group | Activate / deactivate evaluation group 2 | Bool_1 | 1 | Deactivate:<br>Activate: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| ... | | | | | | |
| Evaluation group number | Evaluation group 48 | UInt_16 | 2 | | `48d (30h)` | `00 30` |
| Activate/ deactivate evaluation group | Activate / deactivate evaluation group 48 | Bool_1 | 1 | Deactivate:<br>Activate: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Telegram structure: sMN SetFieldEvaluationContour**

## Perpendicular Distance

## PWR / 3 IOs

This system plug uses a male, 5-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

<p class="caption connector-caption">5-pin PWR connector face with numbered pins.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `Vs` | Supply, +9 V DC to +30 V DC |
| 2 | `IN2/OUT2` | Configurable digital input 2 or output 2 |
| 3 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 4 | `IN1/OUT1` | Configurable digital input 1 or output 1 |
| 5 | `IN3/OUT3` | Configurable digital input 3 or output 3 |

# Release Notes

This page records picoScan100 firmware changes, fixes, and compatibility notes across releases. Use it to assess update impact and find the release information relevant to your installed firmware.

## General Information

V1.x.x/V2.x.x is standard firmware for all picoScan100 variants. Downgrades are not possible. A firmware update typically does not affect active parameter settings or purchased features / licenses for picoScan100 variants. Restart the device after activating or deactivating licenses.

## Update Instructions

**Recommended update path to V2.3.3.**

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Update Instructions:** current firmware, target firmware, recommended update tool / procedure, and firmware update file.</p>

| Current firmware | Target firmware | Recommended update tool / procedure | Firmware update file            |
| ---------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| V2.3.1           | V2.3.3          | SOPASair, web browser, or REST API  | `picoScan100_V2.3.3.spk.signed` |
| V2.2.1           | V2.3.3          | SOPASair, web browser, or REST API  | `picoScan100_V2.3.3.spk.signed` |
| V2.1.0           | V2.3.3          | SOPASair, web browser, or REST API  | `picoScan100_V2.3.3.spk`        |
| V2.0.0           | V2.3.3          | SOPAS ET                            | `picoScan100_V2.3.3.spk`        |
| V1.x.x           | V2.3.3          | SOPAS ET                            | `picoScan100_V2.3.3.spk`        |

After selecting a `.spk.signed` file, the upload process may take several seconds. Once the upload is complete, the **Install now** button becomes active and allows the update to begin. After a successful update, the device indicates completion by showing a green LED again. If the dialog becomes unresponsive, refresh the browser.

**Firmware update via SOPASair.**

Recommended for firmware versions `>= V2.1.0`. SOPASair offers the possibility of a firmware update via web browser.

**Headless firmware update via HTTP / REST.**

Possible with firmware versions `>= V1.4.0`.

The firmware update takes place in two steps:

1. Transfer the firmware file (`.spk`) to the device via HTTP:

    ```http
    PUT <ip>/api/update
    ```

2. Trigger the actual update via HTTP:

    ```http
    POST <ip>/api/RunFirmwareUpdate
    ```

The current update status can be monitored via:

```http
GET <ip>/api/UpdateState
```

See [Firmware Update](../shared-features/firmware-update.md#headless-via-the-rest-api) for the complete sequence with authentication. The OpenAPI description is available in the product download section.

**Firmware update via SOPAS ET.**

Recommended for firmware versions `<= V2.0.0`.

1. Save and unpack the files on your local hard disk. Use full admin rights on your PC.
2. Make sure the picoScan100 is connected via Ethernet to your PC and booted up.
3. Keep the power supply stable during the update process.
4. Use SOPAS ET or AppManager for firmware updates. The following steps refer to SOPAS ET.
5. Search for the connected picoScan100 and drag and drop the device into the SOPAS project.
6. Recommendation: save your parameter file (`.sopas`) before starting the update.
7. Open the settings and choose **Download firmware**.
8. Select the firmware package (`.spk`) and start the update process.
9. Log in to the picoScan100 with user level **Service**.
10. The update procedure may take up to 2 minutes.
11. Wait until the reboot is completed and the device LED turns green.
12. Check the SOPAS window for the correct firmware version.
13. Depending on the firmware update, the SOPAS ET device driver may need to be reinstalled by pressing **install device driver**.
14. Before using the picoScan100 for operation, ensure the device works as expected and all parameters are set as intended.
15. In case of uncertainty, set factory defaults in the device with user level **Service**, then load your parameter file (`.sopas`) onto the device.
16. Done.

## Firmware V2.3.3

**Compatible with:** picoScan120 and picoScan150; **Release date:** cw 31/2026; **Effective from:** S/N 2632xxxx

> Important note: Devices with serial numbers `>= 2632xxxx` can only be operated with firmware version V2.3.3 or later. Earlier firmware versions are not supported.

**Improvements and fixes.**

**Improvement of motor control.**

With this firmware version, the motor control for picoScan150 and picoScan120 has been improved.

**Known issues.**

- Contamination indication segments show **clean** if the measurement is stopped or the device is in stand-by mode. After a device reboot, the contamination indication output may initialize with an incorrect logical state when assigned to a digital output with inversion enabled. The output status is corrected once a new contamination event is detected.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load. This happens when the system diagnosis is called on a device where Particle filter, Moving average filter, and Streaming are active. Deactivate those filters before executing the system diagnosis.
- In very rare cases, device availability after startup is slightly delayed. In this case, the device is fully operational within 20 seconds.
- When changing input and output settings or importing configuration files, an occasional parameterization message can appear in the diagnostics overview: **Too many functions are active at the same time. Deactivate functions that are not required.** This message can be safely ignored because the error becomes inactive immediately.
- Native ROS 2 provides the ROS standard message type `MultiEchoLaserScan`. For this message type, scan profiles 1, 2, 4, and 11 are recommended.

## Firmware V2.3.1

**Compatible with:** picoScan120 and picoScan150; **Release date:** cw 22/2026; **Effective from:** S/N 2625xxxx

**New features.**

**Data output format LMDscandata configurable.**

The graphical user interface allows users to configure the content of the LMDscandata output format, for example disabling RSSI values to reduce network bandwidth.

**Data output format Compact configurable.**

The graphical user interface allows users to configure the content of the Compact output format, for example disabling RSSI values to reduce network bandwidth.

**3D point cloud capture and data export.**

For demonstration purposes, it is possible to swivel or move the scanner in a linear direction to capture a 3D point cloud of the surrounding environment using the encoder input or the integrated IMU of the picoScan150. The captured 3D point cloud is visualized in the Scan View GUI and can be exported as a `.pcd` file.

**Support for PoE system plug.**

This firmware version is required to operate the picoScan150 in combination with the newly developed PoE system plug variant.

**Support for new frontend.**

With this firmware version, picoScan150 and picoScan120 are prepared for compatibility with a new laser frontend as hardware change. The hardware change is planned for implementation in production at a later point in time. Firmware V2.3.1 or later is required to operate devices with the new hardware. Earlier firmware versions are not compatible with the new hardware.

**WebSocket events.**

Added WebSocket-based event subscription support, enabling real-time push notifications over a persistent `/apievents` connection. A single WebSocket link handles multiple event registrations, e.g. contamination, device status, field evaluation, temperature and other events.

**UDP multicast for IMU and encoder data.**

Added support for UDP multicast for both IMU and encoder data streams. The UDP destination address can now be configured as a multicast address.

**CoLa A/B port configurable.**

The CoLa A and CoLa B communication ports, default 2111 and 2112, can now be configured individually. This is useful for compatibility with other SICK LiDAR devices that support the LMDscandata output format.

**Support of Virtual Sensor Lab.**

The [Virtual Sensor Lab](https://devices.cloud.sick.com/) enables users to explore the graphical user interface without requiring a physical device. It also allows the creation of offline configuration files (`.json`) which can be exported and later imported into another device. Configuration files from physical devices can be loaded and viewed in the Virtual Sensor Lab. The web-based tool can set the system plug type, 5-pin or 12-pin. Import and export of `.sopas` files is not supported.

**Cybersecurity improvements.**

System plug variants can clone network parameters, and this firmware allows network parameter cloning to be disabled. The GUI Cyber Security page displays the encoder setup and can enable or disable encoder data streaming. Internal device dependencies were updated to address security vulnerabilities and align with cyber secure software development.

**Improvements and fixes.**

The **Optimized for Robustness** sensitivity mode improves measurement performance on retro-reflector targets and mitigates blooming effects. This release fixes reflector tagging at distances between 20 m and 30 m, implausible encoder values caused by incorrect interpolation, and contamination-indication sector selection after a reboot. Persistent environment teach-in is retained after a reboot and after downloading a parameter file. It also fixes the interchanged Native ROS 2 parameter descriptions for **child frame** and **parent frame**, and Native ROS 2 now works reliably with DHCP IP address servers.

**API changes and publications.**

For a complete reference, consult the OpenAPI description in the product
download section on [sick.com](https://www.sick.com/).

Session-token-based authentication now secures parameter-file upload, download, and import. A short-lived `X-Session-Token`, obtained at service level, creates, downloads, re-uploads, and restores a JSON parameter file.
New full-screen URLs are `http://<ip>/#/?fullscreen=` and `http://<ip>/#/?fullscreen_mode=`.
`http://<ip>/#/?scanview_fullscreen=` has been disabled.

The OpenAPI files are available for [picoScan120](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp684461) and [picoScan150](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp678507).

**Introduced telegrams / REST endpoints.**

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Firmware V2.3.1:** description, CoLa A/B, and REST.</p>

| Description                                                                         | CoLa A/B                                    | REST                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Returns the type of the sending unit                                                | `sRN laserType`                             | `GET /api/laserType`                              |
| Returns the type of the receiving unit                                              | `sRN sipmType`                              | `GET /api/sipmType`                               |
| Returns/sets whether blocked sectors are treated as blocked or contaminated sectors | `sRN/sWN treatBlockedSectorsAsErrorSectors` | `GET/POST /api/treatBlockedSectorsAsErrorSectors` |
| Enables/disables system plug cloning                                                | `sRN/sWN enableCloningPlug`                 | `GET/POST /api/enableCloningPlug`                 |
| Returns/sets Compact telegram type 1 content                                        | `sRN/sWN compactTelegramType1Content`       | `GET/POST /api/compactTelegramType1Content`       |
| Returns/sets LMDscandata configuration                                              | `sRN/sWN LMDscandatacfg`                    | `GET/POST /api/ScanDataConfig`                    |
| Returns/sets LMDscandata CoLa ASCII TCP port settings                               | `sRN/sWN EIAuxPort`                         | `GET/POST /api/EtherAuxIPPort`                    |
| Returns/sets LMDscandata CoLa Binary TCP port settings                              | `sRN/sWN EIHstPort`                         | `GET/POST /api/EtherHostIPPort`                   |
| Returns/sets session timeout for LMDscandata output                                 | `sRN/sWN EtherSessionTimeout`               | `GET/POST /api/EtherSessionTimeout`               |

**Known issues.**

- Contamination indication segments show **clean** when measurement is stopped or the device is in stand-by mode.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load when Particle filter, Moving average filter, and Streaming are active; deactivate those filters before running the diagnosis.
- Device availability may very rarely be delayed but becomes fully operational within 20 seconds.
- The occasional parameterization message **Too many functions are active at the same time. Deactivate functions that are not required.** can be ignored when it becomes inactive immediately.
- Native ROS 2 provides `MultiEchoLaserScan`, for which scan profiles 1, 2, 4, and 11 are recommended.

## Firmware V2.2.0

**Compatible with:** picoScan120 and picoScan150; **Release date:** cw 03/2026; **Effective from:** not released for production

**New features.**

**Encoder input support.**

The device has a digital encoder input for recording incremental encoder signals. Configuration can be done via the user interface or telegram using the communication interface. The encoder input supports single-channel encoders (A) and dual-channel encoders (A/B) for direction determination. Recorded pulses are provided with a high-resolution timestamp using NTP / PTP and output either as a separate UDP stream or as part of LMDscandata. External reference signals can also be fed in, for example encoder Z signal or limit switch signals.

**Download and import of parameter files via SOPASair.**

The parameter set can be manually saved as a project file (`*.json`) on the computer via **Download / Import configuration file**. This is the generally recommended procedure. The project file can be transferred to another product and optionally password-protected. SOPAS ET is obsolete for transferring project files.

**Temperature alarm via digital output.**

The device can set a temperature alarm via digital output. The internal temperature is continuously monitored. If the set temperature is exceeded, a digital output is switched. Threshold settings can be applied via the communication interface.

**Checksum for device validation.**

The sensor can compute a checksum to verify critical device information, including device type, system plug, parameter setting, point of time of last save, calibration data, operating system and active licenses.

**Full screen mode button.**

The three-dot menu includes a full screen mode. When activated, it hides the main menu control bar. Press ESC to exit full screen.

**Improvements and fixes.**

The GUI now implements native ROS 2 communication via DDS and lets users select the **Native ROS 2** data format. The motor controller has been improved during startup, and the issue preventing the angle range filter from being disabled for LMDscandata has been fixed.

**Cybersecurity improvements.**

**Signed firmware update support.**

This firmware forms the basis for signed firmware updates. Future firmware packages in `.spk.signed` format will be validated by the sensor before installation to help ensure that only authentic and tamper-proof software is installed.

**Behavioral changes.**

The release adds an undo function for the last parameter change, minor visual improvements, and the **Evaluation for blocked sectors** setting for contamination indication. SOPAS ET now displays a generic start page with a browser link. An IMU data plausibility check logs an error when data is missing or frozen. **Reset and maintain communication interfaces** no longer deletes HTTPS certificates.

**API changes and publications.**

The OpenAPI files are available for [picoScan120](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp684461) and [picoScan150](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp678507).

**Known issues.**

- Contamination indication segments show **clean** when measurement is stopped or the device is in stand-by mode.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load with Particle filter, Moving average filter, and Streaming active.
- Device availability may very rarely be delayed but becomes fully operational within 20 seconds.
- The occasional parameterization message can be safely ignored when it becomes inactive immediately.

## Firmware V2.1.0

**Compatible with:** picoScan120 and picoScan150; **Release date:** cw 16/2025; **Effective from:** S/N 2517xxxx for picoScan120 and picoScan150

**New features.**

**Perpendicular distance evaluation.**

Perpendicular Distance evaluation is part of the 2D Object Detection Advanced license package. It allows fields to be drawn and evaluates the minimum and maximum perpendicular distance between objects entering the field and a reference line.

A new device can be configured through the sales configurator with the 2D Object Detection Advanced package. On an existing device, activate license `1146093 PICOSCAN PERPENDICULAR DISTANCE` through License Manager.

**Reflector detection improvements.**

The reflector-detection algorithm has been improved, particularly for false positives in ambient light. Devices with serial numbers `> 2422xxxx`, which were more sensitive to false-positive reflector detection, benefit from this improvement. LMDscandata provides reflector information using RSSI value 254, and a reflector-detection filter handles double echoes from reflector targets. On picoScan120, the **optimized for reflector** mode improves measurement performance on reflector targets but can overlook very small, transparent, or mirroring objects.

**HTTPS.**

picoScan100 supports HTTPS, enabling secure and encrypted communication.

**Firmware update via SOPASair.**

SOPASair now offers firmware update capability. SOPAS ET is no longer needed for a firmware update for supported versions.

**Full screen scan view URL.**

For full-screen visualization of measurement data or 2D Object Detection:

```text
<IP>/#/?scanview_fullscreen=
```

Example:

```text
http://192.168.0.1/#/?scanview_fullscreen=
```

**Measurement data recording.**

Measurement and IMU data can be recorded and played back when used with additional recorder software.

Use the [Recorder software](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp681956).

**Improvements and fixes.**

This release improves the 2D Object Detection history-table visualization, `.sopas` file import across former firmware versions, and error and warning handling. It fixes inconsistent configurations after evaluations are deleted, renamed, or recreated with the same names; output-counter behavior; the LMDscandata scan-range filter's first-beam distance value of `0`; and persistence of the **Start/Stop by Input Signal** Teach-In setting. The GUI measurement tool can measure distance to the device center, while SOPASair adds show/hide controls for reflector and non-reflector scan points. The contamination-indication element has been reworked with UX improvements and bug fixes. LMDscandata includes I/O states, and the diagnostics overview shows message category, message number, and whether warnings are active. The CoLa A/B user levels **Maintenance** and **Authorized Client** are disabled by default.

**Behavioral changes.**

When more than 20 fields are active, 2D Object Detection stops working and the device status changes to **device not ready**. Devices shipped with firmware V2.1.0 use **Static IP** instead of **Repeat DHCP** as the DHCP fallback default; this does not apply to devices updated in the field from V1.5.0 or lower.

**API changes and publications.**

The OpenAPI files are available for [picoScan120](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp684461) and [picoScan150](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp678507).

Selected changes include `perpendicularDistanceResult`, which returns the perpendicular-distance feature's minimum distance, maximum distance, and timestamp, and `EtherCoLaScanMode`, which replaces `EnableColaScan` with the Enabled, Time-Limited, Restricted, and Disabled modes. Send `EthernetUpdate` after updating IP configuration to trigger reconfiguration. `changePassword` sets the REST interface password, `SetPassword` sets the CoLa A/B interface password, `EnableUserLevel` activates or deactivates the REST user level, and `EnableLegacyUserLevel` activates or deactivates the CoLa A/B user level. `EnableDetectionHistory` returns or sets detection history, `EvaluationsToLog` returns or sets the evaluations that are logged, and `ResetDetectionHistory` resets detection-history logs. `httpsStatus` returns HTTPS interface status, `certificateBundleInfo` returns information about the uploaded certificate bundle, `setCertificateBundleInfo` uploads a certificate bundle in PEM format through JSON, and `removeCertificateBundleInfo` removes the uploaded certificate bundle.

**Known issues.**

- Contamination indication segments show **clean** when measurement is stopped or the device is in stand-by mode.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load, and an error-log message can occur during a factory reset; both can be ignored as applicable.
- Device availability may very rarely be delayed but becomes fully operational within 20 seconds.
- There is a minimal chance of a fatal error after a firmware update; if it occurs, repeat the update. The update was successful if the device operates stably with a green LED for more than 10 minutes.
- The angle range filter cannot be disabled for LMDscandata; use start angle `-138°` and stop angle `138°`, or perform a factory reset, to output the full field of view.
- In SOPAS ET, 2D object-detection parameters can influence one another, so SOPASair is strongly recommended for parameterization.
- An invalid measurement point can appear at 0° in GUI Application > Data output, but this does not affect Compact or LMDscandata output.
- Some SOPASair notifications during and after a factory reset, firmware update, or reboot can be ignored.

## Firmware V1.3.0

**Compatible with:** picoScan150 only; **Release date:** cw 18/2024; **Effective from:** S/N 2418xxxx

**New features.**

**2D Object Detection.**

The new **Field Evaluation** application allows definition of up to 48 individual fields / evaluations.

Fields can be merged into groups, which can be activated by telegram or input signal. Telegrams and output signals can monitor field and application status. Maximum blanking size and detection time are individually configurable. Distance-dependent mode combines measuring points inside a field according to distance, while manipulation prevention triggers object detection if monitoring from the device to the field boundary is insufficient. **Ignore missing echo** treats a missing echo as a measuring point in the field. In Blanking mode, field evaluation reacts to all measurement points; in Reflector mode, it reacts only to points marked as reflectors. Detection history can store up to 200 entries, deleting the oldest entry when a new detection occurs.

**Contamination indication.**

The contamination indication evaluates 7 sectors regarding contamination levels. Results can be monitored in the GUI, via digital outputs or via telegram. Response time can be adjusted.

**New scan configuration.**

New scan configuration with 15 Hz scanning frequency and 1° angular resolution, profile number 11. This configuration can be used to retrofit, for example, TiM351 or TiM551.

**Improvements and fixes.**

Multi-Echo is available for the 40 Hz / 0.125° scan configuration, profile 10, with all available echoes. Compact and MSGPACK start/stop timestamps now match system time, and the IMU data-streaming timeout is fixed. LMDscandata now limits output through the scan-range filter, has no zero values outside the scan range, and includes device-status and scanning-frequency information. The interval filter's default and minimum value changed from 1 to 2. `mResetCounter` no longer sets an IO port to its default state. The release also adds GUI notifications and fixes the LED indication for the **RecoverableError** device state.

**Known issues.**

- Object-detection output-reset behavior, detection-history refresh and consistency, and incorrect online help for **ignore missing echo**.
- Contamination indication segments show **clean** when measurement is stopped or in stand-by mode.
- The sector dropdown has no effect for **None** or **Weather protection hood**.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load.
- The LMDscandata angle range filter can output a first beam with distance `0` and cannot be disabled.
- An error-log entry during a factory reset can be ignored.

## Firmware V1.2.0

**Compatible with:** picoScan150 only; **Release date:** cw 09/2024; **Effective from:** S/N 2410xxxx

**New features.**

**Precision Time Protocol support.**

PTP is a synchronization mechanism for precise coordination of data acquisition across multiple LiDAR units or other clients in a network. By synchronizing internal clocks, PTP enables accurate timestamping of measurements, supporting spatial mapping and object detection. It minimizes latency and supports reliable data fusion in applications such as autonomous vehicles or industrial automation.

**Native ROS 2.**

Native ROS 2 is a digital add-on with license. The device offers native ROS 2 support using DDS to enable real-time communication and optimize interoperability with ROS 2 standards. To enable it:

Install the corresponding license through License Manager, disable MSGPACK, Compact, or LMDscandata data output, and enable Native ROS 2 with telegram `RosConnectEnable`.

**License Manager support.**

License Manager is integrated and available via:

```text
http://192.168.0.1/#/license
```

**Improvements and fixes.**

Boot time has been optimized, and the device is typically ready after 9.5 seconds. Digital-output behavior during startup and reflector detection have been improved. The maximum debounce time increased to 1000 ms, and the Compact-format scaling-factor issue under rare range-extension conditions is fixed. The IMU data stream now contains a system timestamp and updates when time is set by the user, NTP, or PTP. GUI optimizations update the sensor model, reduce the post-reboot refresh time to 10 s, show only enabled user levels in the login dropdown, avoid rounding angular resolution, and fix visual and wording issues and the distance-measuring tool. The redundant `SaveParameters` method was removed; `mEEwriteall` stores parameters permanently.

**Known issues.**

- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load.
- In rare cases, IMU data streaming can pause for about 1 second before continuing with the latest data.
- A factory reset can trigger **IMU Queue Overflow**, which can be ignored.

## Firmware V1.1.0

**Compatible with:** picoScan150 only; **Release date:** cw 50/2023; **Effective from:** S/N 2350xxxx

**New features.**

**IMU support.**

IMU data is enabled with this release and available in Compact format. IMU type: [BOSCH BHI160B](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/smart-sensor-systems/bhi160b/).

**Cloning of communication parameters.**

Every system plug has cloning memory on board. Communication parameters such as IP address, subnet mask and gateway are stored automatically to the system plug when parameters are saved permanently. Parameters are loaded on boot up. This enables faster device exchange if the system plug remains in the application.

**Improvements and fixes.**

Reflector detection has improved at close ranges: Core typically supports `0.3 m <= x <= 25 m`, Prime typically supports `0.3 m <= x <= 60 m`, and Pro typically supports `0.3 m <= x <= 120 m`. Devices calibrated in the production line no longer generate false-positive reflector flags at target edges. This release fixes measurement-core lockups in complex scenarios, scan-segment latency, and Ethernet-configuration input validation. It improves angular error for calibrated devices, optimizes boot-up time to typically 11 seconds, sends command responses before reboot or factory-default command execution, and ensures the static DHCP fallback IP address works as expected. The GUI and the Microsoft Edge and Firefox user experience have also been improved.

**Known issues.**

- Incorrect distance data is possible in range-extension mode when using picoScan150 Pro-1 with Compact output, active range extension, scan profile 1, 2, 4, 5, or 7, and a highly reflective target at a distance greater than 65 m.
- In SOPASair, a browser tab can consume memory over time and produce an Out of memory error; restart the browser to recover.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load.
- In rare cases, IMU data streaming can time out for about 1 second.
- The IMU data-stream timestamp begins at boot and does not update with user-set time or an NTP server.
