# PLC Integration

Use the CoLa command protocol over a TCP/IP socket to receive measurement,
field-evaluation, and I/O data from SICK LiDAR sensors on Siemens, Beckhoff,
Mitsubishi, or Rockwell PLCs. SICK does not provide maintained PLC function
blocks for the product families on this page; implement a small
length-prefixed receive routine using the controller's native TCP socket API.

## Interface and Approach

For PLC applications, use CoLa B on TCP port `2112`. Its length-prefixed telegrams are easier to process than CoLa A on port `2111`. Open one bidirectional TCP connection from the PLC to the sensor, keep it open, and poll the required values by sending an `sRN` request and reading the matching `sRA` response on that same connection.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Interface and Approach:** interface, transport, and suitable use.</p>

| Interface | Transport | Suitable use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CoLa A / B | TCP 2111 / 2112 | PLC commands and telegram access |
| Compact / MSGPACK | UDP | High-rate scan streams to a computer or edge device |
| REST API | HTTP(S) 80 / 443 | Configuration, diagnostics, and firmware updates |

Configure the sensor once through SOPASair: use a fixed IP address reachable from the PLC, configure scan profiles, field-evaluation groups, and I/O, then export a parameter backup. Do not repeatedly configure the sensor from cyclic PLC logic. Enable LMDscandata only when the PLC requires distance data.

## Polling and CoLa B Framing

The PLC is the client and connects to `<device-ip>:2112`. Send a request, receive one complete telegram, parse it, and reconnect after an error or timeout.

```txt
connect(device_ip, 2112)
loop:
  send(frame("sRN LMDscandata"))
  reply = receive_one_telegram()
  parse(reply)
```

Every CoLa B telegram has this layout:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Polling and CoLa B Framing:** field, size, and value.</p>

| Field | Size | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start | 4 bytes | `02 02 02 02` |
| Length | 4 bytes | Big-endian payload length |
| Payload | N bytes | Command type, name, and data |
| Checksum | 1 byte | XOR of all payload bytes |

TCP is a byte stream: a receive operation can return a partial telegram or several telegrams. Buffer incoming bytes; after at least eight bytes are available, validate the start sequence, read the big-endian length, then wait for exactly `8 + length + 1` bytes. Validate the XOR checksum, consume one telegram, and retain any remaining bytes for the next call.

## Common Telegrams

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Common Telegrams:** telegram, purpose, and PLC consideration.</p>

| Telegram | Purpose | PLC consideration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SCdevicestate` | Device health | Poll slowly and invalidate dependent values when not ready. |
| `LMDscandata` | Distance and optional RSSI data | Reduce it below the network MTU where possible. |
| `perpendicularDistanceResult` | Minimum and maximum distance to a field boundary where the device supports perpendicular distance | Its value can remain unchanged after the field is clear; gate it with field state. |
| `FieldEvaluationResult` | Free/occupied result for each evaluation group | Map each group index to the configured physical zone. |
| `LIDinputstate` / `LIDoutputstate` | Digital I/O states | Use to mirror sensor I/O in the PLC process image. |

Request each with `sRN <name>` and parse the `sRA <name> ...` response. Confirm the exact payload layout, byte offsets, and data types against the Telegram Listing for the installed firmware.

To keep `LMDscandata` manageable, use only the required echo, disable RSSI when not needed, restrict the scan angle, and select the coarsest acceptable angular resolution. A small telegram reduces PLC processing load and TCP segmentation.

## Controller Notes

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Controller Notes:** controller and TCP mechanism.</p>

| Controller | TCP mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Siemens S7-1500 / S7-1200 | Open User Communication: `TCON_IP_v4`, `TSEND_C`, and `TRCV_C`; use variable-length receives. |
| Siemens S7-300 / S7-400 | CP module with `AG_SEND` / `AG_RECV` and FB54 TCP. |
| Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 | Tc2_TcpIp: `FB_SocketConnect`, `FB_SocketSend`, and `FB_SocketReceive`. |
| Mitsubishi GX Works2 / iQ | Ethernet socket services: `SP_SOCOPEN`, `SP_SOCSND`, `SP_SOCRCV`, and `SP_SOCCLOSE`. |
| Rockwell / Allen-Bradley | Raw TCP socket object with MSG instructions for connect, write, read, and close. |

The transport API differs, but the CoLa B framing and receive-buffer logic are identical for every PLC.

## Troubleshooting

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Troubleshooting:** symptom, cause, and action.</p>

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connection refused on `2112` | Incorrect network settings or CoLa B disabled | Verify the sensor IP/subnet and CoLa B configuration. |
| No response | Malformed request or wrong telegram name | Validate start bytes, length, XOR checksum, and case-sensitive command name. |
| `sFA` error response | Unsupported or unavailable variable | Check the [CoLa error codes](../configuration/cola-interface.md#cola-error-codes), Telegram Listing, and firmware version. |
| Receive never completes | Fixed-size receive or TCP fragmentation | Buffer data and use the length field to determine the complete frame. |
| Misaligned data | Concatenated frames or unconsumed bytes | Consume exactly one frame and retain the buffer remainder. |
| Frozen values | Repeated scan or stale perpendicular-distance result | Verify scan counter/timestamp and use `FieldEvaluationResult` to validate the distance. |

# ROS Integration

There are two ways to get LiDAR data into ROS 2: the sensor publishes ROS 2
messages itself (native ROS 2), or a driver on the host receives sensor data
and publishes the messages (`sick_scan_xd`). Both deliver standard ROS 2
messages to your nodes. The difference is which product families they cover
and where decoding and publishing run.

<div class="center-table-headers" markdown="1">

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**ROS Integration:** integration path and compatible devices.</p>

| Integration path | Compatible with |
| --- | --- |
| Native ROS 2 | multiScan200, picoScan100 |
| `sick_scan_xd` | LRS4000, multiScan100, picoScan100 |

</div>

The LRS4000 and multiScan100 do not support native ROS 2. Use `sick_scan_xd`
for these families.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**ROS Integration:** option, what it is, advantages, trade-offs, and best fit.</p>

| Option | What it is | Advantages | Trade-offs | Best fit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Native ROS 2](#native-ros-2) | The sensor firmware assembles the scan segments and publishes ROS 2 messages over DDS. | No driver on the host; lower host CPU load; hardware timestamps; any number of subscribers and other DDS clients can receive the data directly. | Cyclone DDS is the specified middleware; uses more network bandwidth than Compact; no IMU or diagnostics topics; configuration stays outside ROS 2; the picoScan150 needs a license. | ROS 2 systems where host CPU matters, for example navigation or SLAM on embedded computers. |
| [sick_scan_xd](#sick_scan_xd) | A ROS 2 driver on the host receives data through the driver-supported sensor protocol, assembles the scans, and publishes the messages. | Publishes `PointCloud2`, `LaserScan`, and IMU messages where supported; decoding is under host-side control; supports recording to rosbag files. | Decoding and publishing use host CPU; the driver must be installed and maintained on the host. | Applications that need IMU topics, LRS4000 or multiScan100 integration, or host-side control over decoding. |

## Native ROS 2

The product supports native ROS 2 communication via the DDS (Data Distribution Service) protocol. This enables efficient real-time transmission of measured data without additional drivers and with minimum delay time. The data is output directly in ROS 2-compatible formats.

**Note:**

- Filter settings in the product have a direct effect on the published data.
- Subscribed topics are published even if no measurement points are available. It is therefore recommended that you only subscribe to required topics.
- If the static IP address is changed, a restart of the device is required to output the topics correctly.

### Quick Start

1. Verify the ROS 2 with middleware Cyclone DDS is installed. Install the Eclipse Cyclone DDS middleware using the [Cyclone DDS installation instructions](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/Installation/DDS-Implementations/Working-with-Eclipse-CycloneDDS.html).
2. Enable **Native ROS 2 (DDS)** in the device web interface, open **Application → Data output** and set **Measurement data output format** to **Native ROS 2 (DDS)**.
3. Configure Cyclone DDS with the IP address of the host interface connected to the sensor.
4. Start `rviz2` and add one of the published topics.

The picoScan150 requires firmware V2.2.1 or later and an activated native ROS 2 license (`PICOSCAN RosConnect`). picoScan150 PRO versions (part numbers 1134610 and 1142273) are delivered with this license pre-installed. If the license is missing, contact SICK. See [LiDAR License Activation](../shared-features/license-activation.md) for the official activation instructions.

The picoScan120 requires firmware V2.2.1 or later. The latest firmware and update instructions for both devices are available from the [SICK firmware download](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp680096).

![picoScan150 native ROS 2 license](https://support.sick.com/api/data/v9.2/msdyn_knowledgearticleimages(e84df29d-3542-f111-88b4-00224880a9a4)/msdyn_blobfile/$value?w=1800px)
*picoScan150 native ROS 2 license.*

On Windows, DDS discovery requires the sensor network interface to allow local network traffic. In PowerShell, inspect the interface and set it to `Private` if necessary. Replace `5` with the interface index connected to the sensor:

```powershell
Get-NetConnectionProfile
Set-NetConnectionProfile -InterfaceIndex 5 -NetworkCategory Private
```

The ROS 2 domain ID on the host (`ROS_DOMAIN_ID`) must match the device. The default is `0`; it can be changed with `rosDomainId` (0-232) or in SOPASair (multiScan200; picoScan100 from firmware V2.3.1). DDS/RTPS discovery must be able to reach the sensor interface. Native ROS 2 publishes data only; configure the sensor through the REST API, CoLa, or the web interface.

### Visualize the Point Cloud

Create a Cyclone DDS configuration file and set `NetworkInterfaceAddress` to the IP address of the host interface connected to the sensor. This example uses `192.168.0.100`. See the [Cyclone DDS configuration reference](https://cyclonedds.io/docs/cyclonedds/latest/config/index.html) for additional options.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<CycloneDDS
  xmlns="https://cdds.io/config"
  xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="https://cdds.io/config https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eclipse-cyclonedds/cyclonedds/master/etc/cyclonedds.xsd">
  <Domain>
    <General>
      <NetworkInterfaceAddress>192.168.0.100</NetworkInterfaceAddress>
    </General>
  </Domain>
</CycloneDDS>
```

=== "Linux"

    Source ROS 2, select Cyclone DDS, set the configuration file, and start `rviz2`:

    ```bash
    . ~/ros2_humble/install/local_setup.bash
    export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
    export CYCLONEDDS_URI="file://$HOME/CycloneDDS/my-config.xml"
    rviz2
    ```

    In `rviz2`, add `/cloud/all_points` or a scan topic. Set **Fixed Frame** to `world`, or to the frame configured on the device.

=== "Windows"

    In a Windows command prompt, source ROS 2, select Cyclone DDS, set the configuration file, and start `rviz2`:

    ```bat
    call C:\dev\ros2_humble\local_setup.bat
    set RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
    set CYCLONEDDS_URI=file://%USERPROFILE%/cyclonedds.xml
    rviz2
    ```

    In `rviz2`, add `/cloud/all_points` or a scan topic. Set **Fixed Frame** to `world`, or to the frame configured on the device.

### Limitations and Trade-Offs

Native ROS 2 is a sensor-to-host data publisher, not a complete ROS 2 control
interface:

- **No ROS diagnostics topic:** Device health and diagnosis are not exposed as
  a diagnostics topic in the ROS 2 graph. Use the device web interface for
  diagnosis and troubleshooting. See the [SOPASair overview](../visualization/sopasair.md).
- **Configuration stays outside ROS 2:** The interface does not expose sensor
  parameters, services, or actions. Configure scan profiles, field of view,
  filters, and other device settings through the web interface, REST API, or
  CoLa; they cannot be set as ROS parameters or from a ROS 2 launch file.
- **Use CycloneDDS:** Native ROS 2 is specified for CycloneDDS as the ROS
  middleware (RMW) on the host. Other RMW implementations, such as Fast DDS
  or Zenoh, and custom DDS environments are not validated. If you use one,
  test discovery and communication with your device firmware and ROS
  distribution.
- **Account for network load:** Native ROS 2 uses more network
  bandwidth than Compact over UDP. The device publishes its available ROS
  topics concurrently, and topics can continue to be published when a scan
  contains no measurement points. Subscribe only to topics the application
  needs, monitor network utilization at the selected scan configuration, and
  consider Compact if bandwidth is constrained.
- **Publisher changes follow firmware releases:** The DDS publisher runs in
  the sensor firmware, rather than a host-side driver. Publisher fixes and
  feature changes therefore depend on a firmware release.

### Published Topics

The native publisher exposes these topics simultaneously. All messages carry the hardware PTP timestamp in `header.stamp`. The `rt` prefix is the DDS-level name: in ROS 2 tools, `rt<namespace>/cloud/all_points` appears as `<namespace>/cloud/all_points`, for example `/cloud/all_points`.

The multiScan200 and picoScan100 publish the same PointCloud2 and LaserScan topics. The multiScan200 also publishes the `ambient_light` and `imu` topics, and a PointCloud2 topic per segment and echo.

**PointCloud2 topics**

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Published Topics:** PointCloud2 topic, contents ¹⁾, output frequency, and description.</p>

| PointCloud2 topic | Contents ¹⁾ | Output frequency | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rt<namespace>/cloud/all_points` | x,y,z,i,p | Scan rate | Valid scan points of all segments and all echoes |
| `rt<namespace>/cloud/all_points_echo0` | x,y,z,i,p | Scan rate | Valid scan points of echo 0 |
| `rt<namespace>/cloud/all_points_echo1` | x,y,z,i,p | Scan rate | Valid scan points of echo 1 (only available if multi-echo is configured) |
| `rt<namespace>/cloud/all_points_echo2` | x,y,z,i,p | Scan rate | Valid scan points of echo 2 (only available if multi-echo is configured) |
| `rt<namespace>/cloud/reflector_points` | x,y,z,i,p | Scan rate | Valid scan points that were recognized as reflectors |
| `rt<namespace>/cloud/segment[s]` | x,y,z,i,p | Segment frequency | Valid scan points of a selected segment s (only available for segments that are available after application of the angle range filter) |
| `rt<namespace>/cloud/segment[s]_echo[e]` | x,y,z,i,p | Segment frequency | multiScan200 only: valid scan points of echo e in segment s (only available for segments that are available after application of the angle range filter and depending on the configuration of the echo filter) |

¹⁾ intensity (i): RSSI with value range: 0.0 ... 1.0; properties (p): Bit mask 0b00000001 indicates whether this measurement point was recognized as a reflection. On the multiScan200, `sWN rosPointCloud2Content` selects the optional channels RSSI, properties, time offset, and ring (layer index); see the [multiScan200 CoLa Telegram Listing](../multiScan200/cola-telegram-listing.md#set-optional-channels-of-pointcloud2-topics-swn-rospointcloud2content).

**Additional topics (multiScan200)**

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Published Topics:** topic and content.</p>

| Topic | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `ambient_light` | Passive ambient light image, synchronized with the point cloud |
| `imu` | IMU data: acceleration, angular velocity, and orientation |

**LaserScan / MultiEchoLaserScan topics**

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Published Topics:** LaserScan / MultiEchoLaserScan topic, data format, contents ¹⁾, output frequency, and description.</p>

| LaserScan / MultiEchoLaserScan topic | Data format | Contents ¹⁾ | Output frequency | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rt<namespace>/scan/all_points` | MultiEchoLaserScan | x,y,z,i | Scan rate | Valid scan points of all segments and all echoes |
| `rt<namespace>/scan/all_points_echo0` | LaserScan | x,y,z,i | Scan rate | Valid scan points of echo 0 |
| `rt<namespace>/scan/all_points_echo1` | LaserScan | x,y,z,i | Scan rate | Valid scan points of echo 1 (only available if multi-echo is configured) |
| `rt<namespace>/scan/all_points_echo2` | LaserScan | x,y,z,i | Scan rate | Valid scan points of echo 2 (only available if multi-echo is configured) |
| `rt<namespace>/scan/segment[s]` | MultiEchoLaserScan | x,y,z,i | Segment frequency | Only for available segment s (only available for segments that are available after application of the angle range filter) |
| `rt<namespace>/scan/segment[s]_echo[e]` | LaserScan | x,y,z,i | Segment frequency | Only for available segments and echo e (only available for segments that are available after application of the angle range filter and depending on the configuration of the echo filter) |

¹⁾ intensity (i): Value range 0.0-1.0 for natural targets, 1.05 for detected reflector

### Frame and Position Parameters

Set the frames and the mounting position on the device; Native ROS 2 has no ROS parameters. Use the CoLa telegrams below, the REST endpoint of the same name, or the web interface.

<div class="center-table-headers" markdown="1">

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Frame and Position Parameters:** parameter, CoLa telegram, and effect.</p>

| Parameter | CoLa telegram | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frame ID | `sWN rosFrameId` | `header.frame_id` of the published messages |
| Parent frame ID | `sWN rosParentFrameId` | Parent frame of the sensor transform, for example `world` |
| Namespace | `sWN rosNamespace` | Prepended to all topic names; empty for no namespace |
| Sensor position | `sWN SensorPosition` | Mounting position (x, y, z in mm) and orientation (yaw, pitch, roll in 1/10000°), published as a transform on `/tf` |
| Domain ID | `sWN rosDomainId` | ROS 2 domain ID (0-232); must match `ROS_DOMAIN_ID` on the host |

</div>

For the telegram structures and examples, see the CoLa Telegram Listings of the [multiScan200](../multiScan200/cola-telegram-listing.md#measurement-output-telegram) and the [picoScan100](../picoScan100/cola-telegram-listing.md). After changing the static IP address, restart the device so that the topics are published correctly.

### DDS Capabilities

Because the device runs a DDS participant in its firmware, it joins the ROS 2 network as a first-class peer:

- **Interoperability:** ROS 2 nodes, MathWorks ROS Toolbox, OpenDDS-based systems, and custom DDS clients can subscribe directly.
- **Multiple subscribers:** The sensor publishes once per scan; adding subscribers does not add another device-side publishing step.
- **Per-subscriber QoS:** Subscribers can negotiate policies independently, such as `BEST_EFFORT` for control and `RELIABLE` for recording.
- **Automatic discovery:** RTPS discovery finds subscribers without a broker or static IP table.
- **Hardware timestamps:** `header.stamp` is set at the hardware scan trigger. With PTP synchronization, it aligns with other sensors.

## sick_scan_xd

The `sick_scan_xd` driver runs as a ROS 1 or ROS 2 node on the host. It
receives sensor data, assembles complete scans, and publishes ROS messages.
Choose this approach when you need host-side decoding control, IMU data on
ROS topics where supported, or integration with a device that has no native
publisher. It also supports recording and playback with rosbag `.db3` files.
The driver is available from the [sick_scan_xd](https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_scan_xd)
GitHub repository.

## CPU Load Comparison

Measurements across 11 picoScan150 profiles used 15-50 Hz scan rates, 0.05-1.0° angular resolutions, 100 scans per method, and IEEE 1588 PTP synchronization. Single-echo `sensor_msgs/LaserScan` data was used for a direct comparison.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**CPU Load Comparison:** parameter and value.</p>

| Parameter | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Host | Raspberry Pi 4, ARM Cortex-A72, 4 cores, Ubuntu 22.04 |
| RMW | Fast DDS (`rmw_fastrtps_cpp`) |
| Network | Direct Gigabit Ethernet |
| Latency definition | `Δt = treceive_on_host − header.stamp` |

Average system CPU load was **8.5%** for native ROS 2 and **21.5%** for `sick_scan_xd`, expressed as the percentage of one Raspberry Pi 4 CPU core.

# Beginner Projects

These examples outline how to turn a LiDAR use case into an application. Each
starts with a goal, a sensor-to-application data path, and practical steps for
prototyping and validation. Level 1 projects introduce guided sensor
applications, Level 2 adds 3D evaluation or point-cloud tools, and Level 3
introduces a robotics software stack.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Beginner Projects:** level, example, and goal.</p>

| Level | Example | Goal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Building security](./building-security.md) | Monitor an area (e.g. a room floor) very precisely. |
| 1 | [Bulk scan](./bulk-scan.md) | Measure woodchip profiles and calculate volume throughput using belt speed. |
| 2 | [Reversing Assistant](./reversing-assistant.md) | Detect the closest obstacle behind a vehicle and flash the warning LEDs faster as it gets closer. |
| 2 | [3D Height Measurement](./height-measurement.md) | Measure body height with a multiScan100 using perpendicular distance above a floor reference. |
| 2 | [House in 3D](./house-3d-capture.md) | Record picoScan 3D point clouds around a house and inspect the exported PCD files. |
| 3 | [ROS 2 SLAM](./slam.md) | Build a map and localize a vehicle within it using ROS 2 and SLAM Toolbox. |

# Building Security Example

Security access gates form a transition between secure and non-secure areas
of an airport. An object-detection check can help identify items left in the
gate area before access is granted.

![Security access gate with a red detection area and an inset showing the mounted LiDAR sensor](../assets/shared-features/security-door-detection-area.png)
*Example security-door installation. The red overlay illustrates the detection area; the inset shows the LiDAR sensor mounting position.*

A compact 2D LiDAR sensor can monitor a configured detection zone and report
objects that interrupt the scan or differ from a taught reference contour.
This can support a security workflow concerned with prohibited items, such
as weapons, but LiDAR object detection alone does not identify an object's
type or determine whether it is prohibited. Validate detection coverage and
performance for the installation and combine it with the required security
checks.

## Suggested Data Path

Configure detection zones on the sensor using [field evaluation](../on-device-applications/field-evaluation.md).
Use [teach-in](../on-device-applications/field-evaluation.md#teach-in) to capture the
surrounding geometry as a reference contour for detection. Keep the scene
stable during capture, then validate the evaluation with representative
objects and movement.

## Example Solution

The following video demonstrates teach-in for a building-security example.

*Teach-in demonstration for the building-security example.*

# 3D Height Measurement

A multiScan100 can measure the body height of a person in a defined area.
The sensor scans the area in 3D, while perpendicular-distance evaluation
measures the detected points relative to the floor. The maximum distance
inside the evaluation field represents the person's height.

![People passing through a LiDAR height-measurement area](../assets/beginner-projects/height-measurement-application.png)
*A 3D LiDAR measures people as they pass through a defined detection area.*

## Suggested Data Path

1. Mount the multiScan100 so its field of view covers the measuring area and
   the top of the person's head remains within the scan range.
2. Create an evaluation group in **Application > Perpendicular distance
   measurement** and draw a field around the measuring area.
3. Use the floor as the reference plane. Keep walls, door frames, and other
   fixed objects outside the field so they cannot become the maximum value.
4. Configure the object-detection settings for stable measurements.
5. Read the minimum and maximum perpendicular distances from the evaluation
   result. Use the maximum distance as the measured body height.

For configuration and result-access details, see
[Perpendicular Distance Measurement](../on-device-applications/perpendicular-distance-measurement.md).

## Example Solution

The following screenshot shows the evaluation in SOPASair. The 3D field
covers the person above the floor, and the result list reports the minimum
and maximum distances for the evaluation.

![SOPASair perpendicular-distance evaluation with a 3D measuring field around a person and a maximum distance of 1766 mm](../assets/beginner-projects/height-measurement-perpendicular-distance.png)
*Height-measurement example using perpendicular distance. The maximum distance of 1766 mm represents the measured body height.*

Validate the setup with people of known height and verify that the reported
maximum remains stable as a person moves through the measuring area.

# House in 3D

This example shows how to use a picoScan150 3D scan recording as a starting
point for documenting a building. The sensor combines its 2D scan profiles with
rotation information from its internal IMU or an external encoder and exports
the result as a `.pcd` point-cloud file.

## Suggested Data Path

The on-device scan merger records one point cloud at a time.

Mount and orient the sensor so its scan plane sweeps the area of interest as
it rotates. Configure an IMU or encoder rotation source and the sensor offset
in **Application → 3D scan recording**. Clear the previous recording, capture
the sweep, stop recording, and wait for saving to finish. Download `/cloud.pcd`
before starting the next capture; the device keeps only the most recent point
cloud.

## Example Solution

picoScan150:

*House environment captured as a 3D point cloud with picoScan.*

Open each `.pcd` capture in [CloudCompare](../visualization/cloudcompare.md)
to inspect coverage, identify missing areas, and compare the separate
viewpoints.

The next video shows the captured point cloud being opened and inspected in
CloudCompare:

*House point cloud opened and inspected in CloudCompare.*

# Reversing Assistant

When reversing a vehicle, objects behind it can be difficult to see and the
available stopping distance decreases quickly. A LiDAR sensor can monitor this
area and provide an immediate warning: the closer the nearest obstacle is, the
faster the sensor LEDs flash.

![Forklift with a LiDAR sensor monitoring the reversing area and detecting a pallet](../assets/beginner-projects/reverse-camera-application.png)
*The LiDAR monitors the reversing area. A shorter distance to the nearest obstacle produces a faster warning flash.*

## Before You Start

- Connect the picoScan150 and the development computer to the same network.
- Mount the sensor so its field of view covers the monitored reversing area.
- Build and install
  [sick_perception_sdk](https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_perception_sdk) with the
  `picoScan100` examples.
- Change `receiverAddress` if the computer does not use `192.168.0.100`.
- This minimal example uses the default Service password `servicelevel`.

## Minimal Example

This example is based on the SDK's UDP streaming example. The point-cloud
callback only calculates the flash period; the main loop performs the REST
writes so scan reception is not blocked by an HTTP request.

The warning uses the radial range supplied by the scanner in the Compact scan
data. Every point in the received frame is considered.

<details>
<summary>Expand to view the complete C++ example</summary>

```cpp
#include <sick_perception_sdk/compact_format/PointCloud/UnorganizedPointCloud.hpp>
#include <sick_perception_sdk/drivers/picoScan100/PicoScan100Driver.hpp>
#include <sick_perception_sdk/sensor_configuration/HttpClient/httplib_client/HttpClient.hpp>
#include <sick_perception_sdk/sensor_configuration/picoScan150/PicoScan150Configurator.hpp>

#include <atomic>
#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <csignal>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <memory>
#include <thread>

// The signal handler changes this flag when the user presses Ctrl+C.
std::atomic<bool> running {true};

int main()
{
  // Change these addresses if the sensor or computer uses another subnet.
  constexpr char sensorAddress[] = "192.168.0.1";
  sick::IpV4Address receiverAddress {"192.168.0.100"};
  constexpr std::uint16_t scanPort = 2115;

  auto const httpClient =
    std::make_shared<sick::httplib_client::HttpClient>(sensorAddress, 80);
  sick::picoScan150::v2_3_3::Configurator configurator(
    httpClient, sick::UserLevel::Service, "servicelevel");

  configurator.enableScanDataStreamingCompactUdp(receiverAddress, scanPort);

  // The scan callback writes these values while the main loop reads them.
  std::atomic<int> flashPeriodMs {0};
  std::atomic<std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point> lastFrame {
    std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point {}};

  // Request the scanner-provided radial range for every point.
  sick::point_cloud::PointCloudConfiguration pointCloudConfig;
  pointCloudConfig.fields.enableSpherical = true;

  sick::picoScan100::Driver driver;
  driver.scanDataReceiver()
    .setup(scanPort)
    .setOnNewFrameCallback(
      [&](sick::point_cloud::UnorganizedPointCloud const& cloud) {
        // Find the closest valid radial range in the complete scan frame.
        float nearest = std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity();
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < cloud.numberOfPoints(); ++i)
        {
          nearest = std::min(nearest, cloud.getRange(i));
        }

        // Store one full LED on/off period for the selected warning level.
        flashPeriodMs =
          nearest <= 0.5F ? 333 :
          nearest <= 2.0F ? 500 :
          nearest < std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity() ? 2000 : 0;
        lastFrame = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
      },
      pointCloudConfig);
  driver.run();

  std::signal(SIGINT, [](int) { running = false; });
  bool ledOn = false;
  while (running)
  {
    // Treat missing scan data as "no obstacle" after 500 ms.
    bool const scanIsCurrent =
      std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - lastFrame.load() <=
      std::chrono::milliseconds(500);
    int const period = scanIsCurrent ? flashPeriodMs.load() : 0;

    if (period == 0)
    {
      if (ledOn)
      {
        configurator.setLEDEnable(false);
        ledOn = false;
      }
      std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(50));
      continue;
    }

    // Toggling after half a period produces the requested flash frequency.
    ledOn = !ledOn;
    configurator.setLEDEnable(ledOn);
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(period / 2));
  }

  configurator.setLEDEnable(true);
}
```

</details>

Add the source as another picoScan100 example target and link it with
`sick_perception_sdk::drivers` and
`sick_perception_sdk::sensor_configuration`, like the SDK's
`data_streaming_udp` example. Stop it with **Ctrl+C**; the final call enables
the LEDs again, which is their default state.

## Expected Behavior

If no scan frame arrives for 500 ms, the scan is treated as stale and the LEDs
are switched off.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Expected Behavior:** nearest point, flash frequency, and result.</p>

| Nearest point | Flash frequency | Result |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| No obstacle or stale scan | Off | LEDs stay off |
| 0 m to 0.5 m | 3 Hz | Fast warning |
| More than 0.5 m to 2 m | 2 Hz | Medium warning |
| More than 2 m | 0.5 Hz | Slow warning |

Move a test object through the sensor's field of view and check that the reported behavior
changes monotonically: every smaller distance must produce the same or a
shorter period. Test only in a controlled area; this example is a warning aid,
not a safety function.

## Optional Digital Output

The same `ledOn` value can be sent to `POST /api/SetOutput` at the same cadence.
First configure that output's source as **SOPAS command**, then call the SDK's
`setOutput()` method with the output number and value. Do not use
`OutputState` for this: that endpoint only reads the current output states.

# Localization with ROS 2 and SLAM Toolbox

Reliable localization is essential for autonomous driving, driverless-vehicle
navigation, and a smooth material flow. High-resolution LiDAR measurements
help map the surroundings. Localization software compares measurements with
the map to estimate the vehicle's position and orientation, also called its
**pose**. Accuracy depends on the environment, sensor setup, and software
configuration.

![Warehouse scene showing a mobile robot, LiDAR scan lines, occupancy map, and localization status display](../assets/beginner-projects/slam-localization-example.png)
*Illustration of LiDAR mapping and localization with a mobile robot, occupancy map, and pose estimate.*

## ROS 2 for Beginners

For the simplest setup, run this example on an Ubuntu system supported by
your ROS 2 distribution. ROS 2, SLAM Toolbox, and RViz are readily available
as packages on supported Ubuntu releases. Match the Ubuntu version to the
ROS 2 distribution's installation requirements.

ROS 2 is a software framework for connecting robot components. It is not a
complete robot application: you combine programs called **nodes** to handle
tasks such as receiving sensor data, estimating position, and driving motors.
Nodes exchange messages over named **topics**.

For this example, a LiDAR integration publishes scan measurements. Mapping
or localization software consumes those measurements together with robot
motion information. Coordinate transforms (**TF**) describe how the sensor,
robot, and map are positioned relative to one another.

## Mapping, Localization, and Navigation

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Mapping, Localization, and Navigation:** task and what it does.</p>

| Task | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| SLAM | Simultaneous localization and mapping: builds a map while estimating the robot's pose. |
| Localization | Estimates the robot's pose within an existing map. |
| Navigation | Uses the pose and a destination to plan and follow a route while considering obstacles. |

This example only builds a map and estimates the vehicle's pose within it.
Use **SLAM Toolbox** for both stages: first run mapping, then load the saved
pose graph in localization mode. A navigation stack, route planner, and
motion controller are not required for this example.

## Suggested Data Path

The typical data path is:

**LiDAR LaserScan → scan-matching odometry + TF → SLAM Toolbox → map-relative pose in RViz**

This example uses LiDAR scan matching to estimate movement, without wheel
encoders. Run a separate scan-matching odometry node alongside SLAM Toolbox;
excluding encoders does not remove SLAM Toolbox's odometry requirement.
Provide a suitable `LaserScan` topic to both nodes.

## Example Solution

*LiDAR mapping and localization example with ROS 2 and SLAM Toolbox.*

## Project Prompt

<details>
<summary>Expand to view the project prompt</summary>

```text
Help me with a beginner-friendly ROS 2 handheld mapping
project, primarily on Linux, with Windows supported where feasible. Ask for
my OS/version and ROS distribution first. A reference implementation was tested
on Kilted, but do not require migration from a compatible working installation.
Assume I am starting from scratch without an existing repository, configuration,
dependency patches or helper scripts. Prefer compatible ROS binary packages on
Linux; build from source only when necessary. Record dependency versions or
pinned commits and preserve any required patches. Keep the architecture
OS-neutral and clearly label platform-specific install, build and activation
commands. Create any required launch files, configuration, tests and helper
scripts, and explain where to put them.

A SICK picoScan150 publishes native ROS 2 (DDS) LaserScan directly; do not add
a host-side SICK driver. I move the scanner by hand without wheel odometry.
Use RF2O scan odometry, SLAM Toolbox mapping and RViz to show live scans, a
growing occupancy map and the moving sensor pose. Use
https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/ for integration facts.

Verify firmware and license, Cyclone DDS, network interface,
discovery/domain, actual full single-echo LaserScan topic, QoS, frame,
angular geometry and acquisition timestamps. Discover values rather than
inventing settings or reusing another sensor's topic/frame blindly.

Preserve native scan timestamps. For standalone handheld mapping, publish
acquisition time on /handheld/clock, remap /clock and use_sim_time consistently
in RF2O, SLAM and RViz. Isolate motion TF on /handheld/tf and
/handheld/tf_static; exclude the sensor's identity world transform. Use the
observed laser frame as the handheld base, without an invented mounting TF.
RF2O owns handheld_odom -> laser; SLAM owns map -> handheld_odom. This
dedicated clock does not synchronize hardware clocks: do not connect robot
odometry, other sensors or Nav2 without verifying real clock alignment.

Verify RF2O handles asymmetric angular coverage, a valid initial quaternion,
invalid ranges, identical stationary scans, stable startup geometry and
strictly increasing timestamps. Reject incompatible geometry and report
failed matches instead of publishing stale poses. Verify SLAM accepts
translation OR in-place rotation with correct angle units. On Windows,
verify binary-mode pose-graph serialization and required native build fixes.
Check the installed versions before applying patches; do not duplicate fixes
already present upstream.

Deliver working launch/configuration and reproducible setup, not only proposed
commands. Automate SLAM lifecycle activation, prevent duplicate mapping
sessions and shut down if a critical process exits.
Explain environment activation, startup, Ctrl+C shutdown,
fresh-map restart, graph save and reload. Preserve both .posegraph and .data;
distinguish saved-pose-graph SLAM Toolbox localization from occupancy-grid
AMCL. Do not assume archive compatibility across versions or platforms.
```

</details>

# Troubleshooting

Quick fixes for the problems you are most likely to encounter during commissioning and integration. Each row links to the page with the details.
Available settings, protocols, and menu paths vary by device family and firmware.
Use the relevant device guide and release notes to confirm support.

## Connection

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Connection:** symptom and check.</p>

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Sensor not reachable / ping fails | Computer and sensor in the same subnet; power and Ethernet connected ([Getting Started](getting-started.md)) |
| IP address unknown | [Device Discovery](shared-features/device-discovery.md): SOPAS ET search, or ARP when device search is disabled |
| Lost connection after an IP change | Move the computer to the new subnet, or use device search to find the sensor |
| Web UI does not load | Open `http://<ip>/` in Chrome, Edge, or Firefox; clear the cache; check that the web server is not disabled ([Cybersecurity](integration-notes/cybersecurity.md#web-server)) |

## Configuration

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Configuration:** symptom and check.</p>

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Cannot change settings in the web UI | Log in with an enabled [user level](shared-features/user-levels.md); without login, the UI is read-only |
| REST response has `header.status` 4 (Access Denied) | The HTTP status is always `200`; check `header.status`. Fetch a new challenge for every `POST`, check the password and that the user level is enabled, and wait 30 s after five failed logins ([REST Interface](configuration/rest-interface.md#status-codes-and-errors)) |
| REST file transfer returns 403 | Send a valid `X-Session-Token` header ([Backup & Restore](configuration/configuration-backup-and-restore.md)) |
| Settings lost after power cycle | Persist with `WriteEeprom` or **Save permanently** ([REST Interface](configuration/rest-interface.md#reading-vs-writing)) |
| CoLa `sFA` error response | Look up the [CoLa error code](configuration/cola-interface.md#cola-error-codes) |
| Web UI shows an error ID | Look up the ID in the [Error Codes](shared-features/error-codes.md) list |
| Need to restore factory settings | [How to perform a factory reset](https://support.sick.com/sick-knowledgebase/article?id=e1f49414-a351-f011-877b-7c1e52263b55) |

## Measurement Data

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Measurement Data:** symptom and check.</p>

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| No UDP data arrives | Data output enabled and destination IP/port set to your computer; Windows network profile set to Private; firewall allows the UDP port ([Compact Format](data-streaming/compact-format.md#transport)) |
| Scan view empty | Measurement is active and data output is enabled in the device's web interface |
| CRC errors in your parser | Compact: CRC32 over the whole frame; MSGPACK: CRC32 over the MSGPACK buffer only ([MSGPACK Format](data-streaming/msgpack-format.md#framing)) |
| Fewer points than expected | [Filters](data-streaming/filter-details.md) and scan range reduce or zero out points |
| No ROS 2 topics visible on a device with Native ROS 2 support | Cyclone DDS configured with the host interface IP; matching domain ID ([Native ROS 2](integration-notes/ros-integration.md#native-ros-2)) |
| WebSocket closes with error 1002 on a device with WebSocket support | Negotiate `permessage-deflate` ([WebSocket Events](data-streaming/websocket-events.md#troubleshooting)) |
| Reduced range or warnings | Check [contamination indication](on-device-applications/contamination-indication.md) and clean the optics cover |

## Get Support

Create a diagnostic file in SOPASair (**Diagnostics → Overview → Diagnostic file**) and send it to SICK with a description of the problem. See [Contact](contact.md).

# Glossary

This glossary explains the terms, abbreviations, and SICK-specific names used in this guide. Where a term has its own page, the entry links to it.

<div class="glossary-tables" markdown="1">

## A

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| AAS (Asset Administration Shell) | Standardized digital twin of a product with its data sheet, operating instructions, certificates, and CAD data. See [Asset Administration Shell](shared-features/asset-administration-shell.md). |
| Activation type | Setting of an evaluation group that defines when the group is evaluated: always, controlled by digital inputs, or controlled by a telegram. See [Field Evaluation](on-device-applications/field-evaluation.md#configure-over-the-api). |
| Ambient light image | Passive, narrow-band image around 905 nm that the multiScan200 captures through its LiDAR receiver. It is not a camera image. |
| AMR (autonomous mobile robot) | Mobile robot that navigates without fixed guidance. A typical application for LiDAR sensors. |
| Angle range filter | Filter that limits the output to a horizontal and vertical angle range. See [Filter Details](data-streaming/filter-details.md#angle-range-filter). |
| API (application programming interface) | Interface through which programs access the sensor, for example REST or CoLa. |
| Authorized Client | User level for configuring the sensor in daily operation. See [User Levels](shared-features/user-levels.md). |
| AutoIP | Method in which the sensor assigns itself an IP address when no DHCP server answers. |
| Azimuth | Horizontal angle of a beam (theta). |

## B

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Beam | One measurement direction of the sensor. Each beam can return one or more echoes. |
| Blanking | Detection mode of field evaluation: the field is infringed when an object at least as large as the minimum object size is inside the field. Smaller objects are ignored ("blanked"). |
| Blooming | False points next to highly reflective objects such as retroreflectors. The multiScan200 blooming filter removes them. |

## C

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Challenge-response authentication | Login method of the REST API. The client requests a one-time challenge and answers with a hash that includes the password; the password itself is not transmitted. See [REST Interface](configuration/rest-interface.md). |
| Checksum | Value calculated over data to detect transmission errors or changes. CoLa B uses an XOR checksum, the Compact format CRC32, and the device reports MD5 checksums of its software and parameters. See [Checksums](shared-features/checksums.md). |
| CloudCompare | Open source software for viewing and processing 3D point clouds. See [CloudCompare](visualization/cloudcompare.md). |
| CoLa (Command Language) | SICK telegram protocol for configuration and data requests. CoLa A uses ASCII text on TCP port 2111, CoLa B binary data on TCP port 2112, and CoLa 2 uses TCP port 2122. See [CoLa Interface](configuration/cola-interface.md). |
| CoLa1 | Collective name for CoLa A and CoLa B. |
| Compact format | SICK binary format for measurement data over UDP or TCP, described by Kaitai Struct definitions. See [Compact Format](data-streaming/compact-format.md). |
| Contamination indication | Function that detects dirt on the optics cover and reports warnings or errors. See [Contamination Indication](on-device-applications/contamination-indication.md). |
| Contour mode | Detection mode of field evaluation that compares the scan with a taught-in reference contour. |
| CRC32 | 32-bit cyclic redundancy check. Protects each Compact and MSGPACK telegram. |
| Cyclone DDS | DDS implementation specified as the ROS 2 middleware for native ROS 2. |

## D

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Data output | Application in SOPASair that configures which measurement data the sensor sends and in which format. |
| DDS (Data Distribution Service) | Publish-subscribe middleware used by ROS 2. Native ROS 2 runs a DDS participant on the sensor. |
| Device Not Ready | Device state that signals that the sensor does not work correctly. Can be output on a digital output (`DRDY`). |
| Device search | Discovery of sensors in the network through UDP broadcasts on port 30718. See [Device Discovery](shared-features/device-discovery.md). |
| DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) | Protocol with which a network server assigns IP addresses automatically. |
| Diagnostic file | File with log entries for in-depth analysis by SICK. Created in SOPASair under Diagnostics. |
| Distance-dependent | Field evaluation parameter that decides, based on their axial separation, whether two objects are evaluated separately or merged. See [Field Evaluation](on-device-applications/field-evaluation.md#distance-dependent). |

## E

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Echo | Reflection of one laser pulse. One beam can return several echoes, for example from a raindrop and a wall behind it. |
| Echo filter | Filter that selects which echoes are output, for example the first, the last, or all echoes. See [Filter Details](data-streaming/filter-details.md#echo-filter). |
| EEPROM | Non-volatile memory of the sensor. Changes are stored permanently only after `WriteEeprom` (REST) or `mEEwriteall` (CoLa). |
| Elevation | Vertical angle of a beam (phi). |
| Encoder | Rotary sensor on a moving axis. The picoScan150 can read an encoder to build 3D point clouds. See [3D With 2D LiDARs](integration-notes/3d-with-2d-lidars.md). |
| Evaluation | One detection field with its parameters. Up to 48 evaluations can be configured. |
| Evaluation group | Set of evaluations that is activated and deactivated together. |

## F

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Field evaluation | On-sensor application that checks whether objects are inside a defined field and reports `FREE` or `INFRINGED`. See [Field Evaluation](on-device-applications/field-evaluation.md). |
| Firmware | Software that runs on the sensor. See [Firmware Update](shared-features/firmware-update.md). |
| Fog filter | picoScan100 filter that removes fog echoes at close range. |
| Frame | One complete scan. A frame is split into segments for output. |

## I

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| IMU (inertial measurement unit) | Built-in sensor that measures acceleration, angular velocity, and orientation. |
| Interlaced mode | multiScan200 scan configurations 10 to 12, which combine several scans that are shifted against each other to reach a higher resolution. |
| Interval filter | Filter that outputs only every n-th scan. |

## K

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Kaitai Struct | Language for describing binary formats. SICK publishes the Compact format as Kaitai Struct definitions (`.ksy`). |

## L

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Layer | One horizontal scan line at a fixed elevation angle. Multi-layer devices such as multiScan100 and multiScan200 provide several layers; LRS4000 and picoScan100 have one layer. |
| LiDAR (light detection and ranging) | Measurement principle that determines distances from the time-of-flight of laser pulses. |
| LMDscandata | CoLa telegram with measurement data. See [LMDscandata Format](data-streaming/lmdscandata-format.md). |

## M

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Maintenance | User level for maintenance tasks. See [User Levels](shared-features/user-levels.md). |
| Mean filter | Filter that averages the distance of each point over several scans, also called moving average filter. On the multiScan200 it is called high precision mode. See [Filter Details](data-streaming/filter-details.md#moving-average-filter). |
| Minimum object size | Smallest object that infringes a field in blanking mode. |
| MSGPACK (MessagePack) | Binary serialization format; used by multiScan100 and picoScan100 for measurement data. See [MSGPACK Format](data-streaming/msgpack-format.md). |
| Multi-echo | Ability of the sensor to measure several echoes per beam. |
| Multicast | Transmission of one data stream to a group of receivers. |

## N

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Native ROS 2 | Function with which the sensor publishes ROS 2 messages itself over DDS, without a host driver. See [ROS Integration](integration-notes/ros-integration.md#native-ros-2). |
| NTP (Network Time Protocol) | Protocol for synchronizing the sensor clock with a time server. See [Time Synchronization](shared-features/time-synchronization.md). |

## O

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAPI | Machine-readable description of a REST API. SICK publishes an OpenAPI file for each device. |

## P

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Particle filter | Filter that removes isolated points caused by dust, rain, or snow. See [Filter Details](data-streaming/filter-details.md#particle-filter). |
| pcap | File format for recorded network traffic, created for example with Wireshark. See [Wireshark](recording/wireshark-pcap.md). |
| Performance profile | See scan configuration. |
| Perpendicular distance measurement | picoScan100 application that measures the distance of objects to a reference line. See [Perpendicular Distance Measurement](on-device-applications/perpendicular-distance-measurement.md). |
| PLC (programmable logic controller) | Industrial controller. See [PLC Integration](integration-notes/plc-integration.md). |
| Point cloud | Set of 3D points calculated from the measured distances and angles. |
| PointCloud2 | ROS message type for point clouds. |
| Product ID | Unique identification of a device from its part number and serial number, reachable at [`pid.sick.com/{P/N}/{S/N}`](https://pid.sick.com/). |
| PSIRT (Product Security Incident Response Team) | SICK team that handles reports of security vulnerabilities. |
| PTP (Precision Time Protocol, IEEE 1588) | Protocol for precise time synchronization over Ethernet. |

## Q

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Quaternion | Four values (w, x, y, z) that describe an orientation in 3D. The IMU reports its orientation as a quaternion. |

## R

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Reflector | Highly reflective target, such as a retroreflector. The sensor can mark points on reflectors. |
| Region of interest | Area to which an evaluation or a filter is limited. For teach-in, the polygon that bounds where the contour is learned. |
| Remission factor | Share of the emitted light that an object reflects back, also called remission. Ranges are specified for a given remission factor, for example 10 %. |
| REST (Representational State Transfer) | HTTP-based interface of the sensor for reading and writing variables and calling methods. See [REST Interface](configuration/rest-interface.md). |
| RMW (ROS middleware) | Layer that connects ROS 2 to a DDS implementation. |
| ROS (Robot Operating System) | Open source framework for robot software. See [ROS Integration](integration-notes/ros-integration.md). |
| ROS bag | Recording of ROS messages in a file (`.bag` in ROS 1, `.db3` or `.mcap` in ROS 2). See [ROS Bag](recording/ros-bag-db3.md). |
| RSSI (received signal strength indicator) | Measure of the strength of an echo. |

## S

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Scan configuration | Predefined combination of aperture angle (field of view), scanning frequency, and angular resolution, identified by a number. |
| Scan range | Angle range covered by the sensor, for example 276° for the picoScan100. |
| ScanSegmentAPI | SICK Python and C# libraries for receiving segmented scan data. The Python library supports LRS4000, multiScan100, and picoScan100; the C# library supports multiScan100 and picoScan100. |
| Segment | Part of a frame that is sent as one telegram so that it can be processed immediately. |
| Service | Highest user level. Enabled on delivery. See [User Levels](shared-features/user-levels.md). |
| Session token | Token that authorizes binary file transfers, for example firmware updates and configuration backups. |
| sick_perception_sdk | SICK C++ SDK for configuring LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, and picoScan100 sensors and receiving Compact data. See [Programming Tools and Examples](integration-notes/programming-tools-and-examples.md). |
| sick_scan_xd | SICK driver for ROS 1, ROS 2, and applications without ROS. See [ROS Integration](integration-notes/ros-integration.md#sick_scan_xd). |
| Slot | One column of measurements at a horizontal angle step; on the multiScan200, each slot contains all layers. |
| SOPAS ET | SICK Engineering Tool for Windows for configuring and visualizing devices. See [SOPAS ET](visualization/sopas-et.md). |
| SOPASair | Web interface of the sensor, opened in a browser. See [SOPASair](visualization/sopasair.md). |
| STX / ETX | Start of text (`0x02`) and end of text (`0x03`), the control characters that frame a CoLa A telegram. |
| Swagger UI | Interactive viewer for OpenAPI files. |
| System plug | Exchangeable connector unit of the sensor that also stores a copy of the parameters. |

## T

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Teach-in | Function that learns the current environment as the reference contour of a field. See [Field Evaluation](on-device-applications/field-evaluation.md#teach-in). |
| Telegram | One message exchanged with the sensor, for example a CoLa command or a Compact data packet. |
| Telegram type | Number in a Compact telegram that identifies its content, for example scan data or IMU data. |

## U

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Unicast | Transmission of a data stream to one receiver. |
| User level | Access level that defines which settings a user can change: Maintenance, Authorized Client, or Service. See [User Levels](shared-features/user-levels.md). |

## V

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Virtual Sensor Lab | Browser-based simulation of SICK sensors. See [Virtual Sensor Lab](simulation/virtual-sensor-lab.md). |

## W

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| WebSocket | Protocol for a persistent connection over which the sensor pushes events. See [WebSocket Events](data-streaming/websocket-events.md). |
| Wireshark | Network analysis tool. SICK provides a Wireshark dissector for the Compact format. |

## X

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| XOR checksum | Checksum of CoLa B telegrams: the exclusive OR of all payload bytes. |

</div>

# Contact

Choose the contact option that best fits your question.

## Local Sales

Contact your local SICK sales representative for product selection,
application advice, pricing, and availability. Visit [sick.com](https://www.sick.com/)
and select your country or region to find the local sales contact.

## Support Portal Case

For technical troubleshooting, open a support case at
[support.sick.com](https://support.sick.com/). Describe the issue, your setup,
and the steps needed to reproduce it. Include the part number and serial
number from the device's type label, together with the firmware version.

If your device provides a diagnostic-file export, create the file through
its configuration interface and attach it to the case. Diagnostic information
helps SICK investigate the issue; the available export options depend on the
device and firmware.

## Public Discussion

For general integration questions and sharing experience with other users, join the
[GitHub Discussions space](https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_lidar_developer_guide/discussions)
or [start a new discussion](https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_lidar_developer_guide/discussions/new/choose).

Discussions are public. Do not post credentials, confidential project data,
or diagnostic files containing sensitive information; use a Support Portal
case for information that should not be shared publicly.
